title: [Core][Scheduler] Batch small prefill chunks under decode load
body:
## Review summary

- Default-off, text-only scheduler policy; existing behavior is unchanged when `--min-prefill-chunk-tokens=0`.
- Batches sub-threshold prefill chunks only while decode work is runnable, with a bounded delay and cleanup on schedule/abort/finish/preemption.
- Targets long-prompt mixed prefill/decode workloads where the objective is to maximize stable per-GPU QPS under an average E2E latency budget.
- In controlled single-GPU RTX PRO 5000 experiments with the policy predecessor, enabling Small Prefill reduced average E2E from 2.931s to 2.388s at QPS 12 (-18.5%) in one fixed configuration, and moved the stable <=3s capacity knee from 11 to 13 QPS (+18.2%) in another.
- Timeline analysis showed context tokens per step increasing from 1,669 to 4,785, while incremental prefill GPU time fell from 15.069 to 8.788 us/token (-41.7%).
- Focused scheduler/CLI tests and changed-file pre-commit pass; the policy lineage is also operating on approximately 1,600 RTX PRO 5000 workers.

## Purpose

Decode-heavy workloads can leave small text prefill chunks in the remaining
token budget. Launching those chunks individually may underutilize the GPU.

This PR adds an opt-in scheduler policy that:

- defers text prefill chunks smaller than `--min-prefill-chunk-tokens` while
  decode work is runnable;
- releases deferred chunks when their combined size reaches that threshold or
  `--max-prefill-chunk-delay-steps` expires;
- clears pending state on schedule, abort, finish, and preemption; and
- excludes multimodal requests.

The feature is disabled when `--min-prefill-chunk-tokens=0` (the default), so
the existing scheduling path is unchanged by default.

### Duplicate-work check

I searched open PRs for the CLI names and for small-prefill/deferred-prefill
batching and found no implementation of this policy.

Two adjacent policies use different control signals:

- #54627 applies `prefill_schedule_interval` to single-engine runs. It defers
  all prefills on a fixed cadence to protect decode interactivity.
- This PR is size-aware: it defers only sub-threshold text chunks and releases
  them by aggregate tokens or bounded per-request age. It targets batching
  efficiency under an E2E capacity budget.

They are not duplicates. If both are eventually composed, precedence should be
defined because the cadence gate currently runs before this PR's threshold/age
check. They should not be enabled together by default without an interaction
benchmark.

The adjacent P-PAS RFC (#52906) controls the aggregate prefill token budget
under pressure, whereas this PR keeps global budgets unchanged and batches
sub-threshold chunks. A controlled 2x2 experiment found that these policies are
also not universally additive.

### AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with porting the implementation to current `main`, test
drafting, and the upstream overlap audit. I reviewed every changed line,
understand the implementation and validation, and can defend the change.

This changes scheduling timing without changing kernels, token accounting, or
sampling. The TTFT trade-off is documented below.

## Test Plan

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu uv run --active --no-project python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/v1/core tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  -k small_prefill -v

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu uv run --active --no-project python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/engine tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py \
  -k small_prefill -v

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
```

The scheduler tests cover aggregation, bounded delay, no-decode behavior,
default-off behavior, abort/preemption cleanup, allocation failure, and config
validation.

## Test Result

- Small-prefill scheduler tests: `8 passed`
- CLI parsing test: `1 passed`
- Changed-file pre-commit: all hooks passed, including ruff, formatting, mypy,
  Markdown lint, and config validation

An exploratory full scheduler-file run in the reused minimal CPU environment
reached `122 passed`; 36 multimodal/EC tests could not run because the optional
`mistral_common` dependency was absent. The focused tests above completed
cleanly, and upstream CI has the complete test dependency set.

### SLA-oriented serving validation

The primary use case is not maximum QPH with a relaxed latency target. It is
long-prompt mixed prefill/decode serving where the objective is the highest
stable per-GPU QPS satisfying all of the following:

- average E2E latency <=3s;
- completed QPS keeps up with offered QPS;
- no failures, OOMs, core dumps, or restarts; and
- running and waiting requests do not grow persistently.

The controlled workload used a single RTX PRO 5000 72GB GPU, a Qwen3.5-0.8B
model, TP=1, non-streaming open-loop requests, and a production-derived request
distribution averaging about 5.4K prompt tokens and 300 output tokens. MTP was
disabled; chunked prefill, an 8,192-token batch budget, and FP8 KV cache were
enabled.

The following comparisons changed only Small Prefill within each fixed
configuration:

| Comparison | Fixed configuration | Result |
|---|---|---|
| C -> F | BF16 LM Head + FP8 KV | At QPS 12, average E2E fell from 2.931s to 2.388s (-18.5%); the stable <=3s knee remained at 12 QPS. |
| D -> E | FP8 LM Head + FP8 KV | The stable <=3s knee moved from 11 to 13 QPS (+18.2%). E at QPS 13 measured 2.661s and 2.700s across two GPUs; QPS 14 measured 3.408s and 3.528s and failed the SLA. |

Timeline analysis explains the gain: context tokens per step increased from
1,669 to 4,785 (2.87x), raw context GPU time fell from 16.699 to 9.390 us/token,
and incremental prefill GPU time fell from 15.069 to 8.788 us/token (-41.7%).

These controlled measurements used the production predecessor of this policy.
The PR retains the threshold/delay behavior while hardening per-request age and
lifecycle cleanup. A separate run of the hardened implementation at `3072/384`
sustained QPS 12 at 2.462s average E2E with no failures, preemptions, or
sustained waiting; QPS 13 measured 3.096s. That later baseline was not a fully
matched crossover, so it is supporting reproduction rather than the main
capacity-delta claim.

### Production validation

This policy lineage is currently deployed in a production serving cluster with
approximately 1,600 single-GPU NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 workers and is serving live
traffic. The production configuration uses:

- `--min-prefill-chunk-tokens 3072`
- `--max-prefill-chunk-delay-steps 192`

At the time of verification, all allocated workers were ready and available.
This operational deployment is separate from the controlled `3072/384`
experiments. It demonstrates production-scale operational viability, but is
not used to claim a fleet-wide capacity or latency improvement.

### Interaction with adjacent prefill policies

In a separate peak-throughput 4B experiment, Small Prefill alone improved
QPH/GPU by 1.90%, while combining it with P-PAS was 7.06% below Small Prefill
alone. This is an interaction warning, not the primary performance claim. Both
policies gate prefill admission, so the tested combination is not recommended
without workload-specific validation.

Documentation for both CLI options and the TTFT trade-off is included.

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

title: [Kernel][GDN] Tune packed decode launch on SM120
body:
## Review summary

- Applies `BV=16` only to SM120, Qwen3.5's `H=HV=16, K=V=128` packed-decode shape, and batches up to 24; every other path keeps `BV=32`.
- Rebased onto current `main` and preserves #53877's FP32 `beta` semantics and regression test.
- Post-rebase SM120 validation of all three PR-touched files: 29 tests passed, wrapper output/state were bit-exact for B1--64, and changed-file pre-commit passed.
- Current SM120 kernel measurements show 1.06x--1.20x speedup for B1--24; the advantage narrows and reverses at larger batches, so the selector remains conservatively capped at B24.

## Purpose

Tune the packed recurrent GDN decode launch on SM120 for the Qwen3.5 shape
`H=HV=16, K=V=128`. Batches up to 24 use `BV=16`; all other shapes and batch
sizes keep the existing `BV=32` launch.

This is complementary to #51954. That PR removes decode-time gate copies; this
change only selects a benchmark-backed launch configuration for the packed
recurrent kernel. Searches for the helper name, target shape, and SM120 GDN
keywords found no open PR implementing the same launch policy.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py -q

.venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_qwen_gdn_packed_decode.py \
  --validate-wrapper --batch-sizes 1 8 14 16 19 24 25 32 48 64

.venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_qwen_gdn_packed_decode.py \
  --batch-sizes 1 8 14 16 19 24 25 32 48 64 \
  --bvs 16 32 --num-warps 1 --num-stages 3 --rep-ms 500

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/fused_recurrent.py \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_qwen_gdn_packed_decode.py
```

## Test Result

RTX PRO 5000 72GB Blackwell (SM120); all three PR-touched files checksum-matched commit `9823c325bb`:

- 29 tests passed, including the upstream FP32-`beta` regression test.
- Packed output and recurrent state were bit-exact for batch sizes
  1, 8, 14, 16, 19, 24, 25, 32, 48, and 64.
- `BV=16` vs `BV=32` kernel-time ratios (`BV=32 / BV=16`) were 1.20x at B1,
  1.07x at B8, 1.18x at B14, 1.17x at B16, 1.10x at B19, and 1.06x at B24.
  The margin narrows to 1.02x at B32 and reverses at B48/B64, so the selector
  stays capped at B24.
- A serving A/B on the same GPU family observed 1.90% lower end-to-end
  latency with no correctness change.
- Nine CPU-capable selector tests and all changed-file pre-commit hooks passed
  after the rebase.

## AI Assistance

OpenAI Codex was used to help port the change, draft tests, build the benchmark,
and resolve the rebase conflict. The human submitter reviewed every changed
line, understands the change end-to-end, and personally ran or verified the test
results above.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend]keep anthropic tool-result images in tool messages
body:
## Purpose

Addresses #58647, item 6: "Images in a tool_result become a separate user message inserted between tool messages".

The Anthropic converter extracts images from `tool_result` into a separate
`user` message. With parallel tool calls, this produces
`assistant → tool → user(image) → tool`, breaking tool-result continuity
and causing some renderers to reject the conversation or drop later results.

Keep text and image parts in the corresponding `tool` message, preserving
their order and `tool_call_id`. String and text-only results retain their
existing string representation.

```text
Before:
assistant(tool_calls A, B)
tool(A, "")
user(image A)
tool(B, "result_B")

After conversion:
assistant(tool_calls A, B)
tool(A, [image A])
tool(B, "result_B")
```

Real Ministral validation exposed an additional compatibility requirement:
its v13 tokenizer rejects image chunks in tool messages with HTTP 400.

Add a compatibility adapter at the Mistral renderer boundary:

- Tokenizer v15+ keeps images in tool messages.
- For older tokenizers, collect tool-result images and place them after
  the entire consecutive tool-result group, merging them into the next
  user message when present.

This fallback preserves tool-result continuity and image input, but cannot
preserve native image-in-tool attribution on older Mistral tokenizers.

## Test Plan

Converter regression coverage includes:

- Image-only and text/image/text results.
- Multiple images using base64 and URL sources.
- Consecutive parallel tool results with correct IDs.
- Empty image URLs preserving text-only behavior without an extra user turn.
- Existing tool-reference behavior, including coexistence with images.

Mistral renderer tests cover the pre-v15 fallback and v15 passthrough.

## Test Results

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic -v
# 94 passed, including all 7 test_messages.py service tests

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/renderers/test_mistral.py -v
# 4 passed
```

The final converter regression tests produce **5 failed, 6 passed**
against the baseline and **11 passed** with the fix. The full conversion
test file passes all **85 tests**.

All applicable default pre-commit hooks passed for the four changed files,
including Ruff, mypy, test tethering, SPDX, and import checks.
`git diff --check` also passed.

### Multimodal validation

- **Gemma 4:** converter → parser → template/tokenizer validation retained
  the decoded image, image placeholder/token, and subsequent tool result.
- **Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512:** reproduced the converter-only HTTP 400
  with its real v13 tokenizer. With the renderer adapter, the actual
  `/v1/messages` request returned **HTTP 200**, executing the tokenizer,
  Pixtral image encoder, model weights, and generation. Rendered output
  retained the image markers and each of `before_A`, `after_A`, and
  `result_B` exactly once.

title: [Frontend] Integer token IDs for generate output logprobs (GenerateLogProbs)
body:
## Purpose

Implements the `GenerateLogProbs` shape agreed in #57574. `/inference/v1/generate` is a vLLM-defined token-in/token-out API, but its output logprobs used the OpenAI shape: the generate server has no tokenizer, so it wrote every token as a `"token_id:N"` placeholder string that derender parsed back out, and the two frontends disagreed on `bytes` (Python left it unset, the Rust frontend set it to the UTF-8 bytes of the placeholder itself).

Scope is exactly the split @hickeyma described in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57574#issuecomment-5745092183: this PR is `content` only. #57442 stacks `GenerateLogProbs.sampled` on top afterwards.

## Shape

```python
class GenerateLogProb(BaseModel):
    token_id: int
    logprob: float = -9999.0
    rank: int | None = None

class GenerateLogProbsContent(GenerateLogProb):
    top_logprobs: list[GenerateLogProb] = []

class GenerateLogProbs(BaseModel):
    content: list[GenerateLogProbsContent] | None = None
```

- `top_logprobs` is a **list in rank order**, not a dict: JSON turns dict keys into strings and the order would be implicit.
- `rank` is **kept**: the engine already computes it and the Rust frontend's gRPC `CandidateTokenInfo` carries it. It was being dropped on the floor before.
- No `bytes`, no string `token`.
- `content=None` is the normal "no per-token candidates were requested" state, not an error.
- The `-9999.0` default matches what the OpenAI shapes already put on the wire when the sampled token is absent from the engine's top-k map, so that case is unchanged.

## What changed

- **Python generate server** (`scale_out/token_in_token_out`): `_create_tokens_logprobs` builds the new type; `GenerateResponseChoice.logprobs` and `GenerateResponseStreamChoice.logprobs` are `GenerateLogProbs | None`, streaming and non-streaming.
- **Rust frontend** (`routes/inference/generate`): same field swap, `position_to_generate_logprobs_content` emits ids + rank instead of `format_token_id`.
- **Derender**: `_resolve_logprobs` converts `GenerateLogProbs` → `ChatCompletionLogProbs`, filling `token`/`bytes` from the tokenizer, and `_convert_chat_logprobs_to_completion_logprobs` then produces `CompletionLogProbs` as before. The U+FFFD byte-fallback correction (`_correct_decoded_token`) is untouched — it needs the preceding sampled token ids as context, and the integer shape now carries those directly instead of reconstructing them from placeholder strings.
- **Placeholder layer deleted from the generate path**: `_parse_token_id_placeholder` and `resolve_token_id_placeholder` are gone; the id-taking core is now `decode_token_id` in `entrypoints/generate/base/serving.py`.
- **Out of scope, unchanged**: `prompt_logprobs` (already integer-keyed) and `return_tokens_as_token_ids` on `/v1/chat/completions` / `/v1/completions`, which is a user-facing OpenAI option that uses `token_id:N` on purpose.

## Release note

> **Breaking:** output logprobs on `/inference/v1/generate` are now `GenerateLogProbs` with integer `token_id` instead of `ChatCompletionLogProbs` with `"token_id:N"` placeholder strings, in both the Python and Rust frontends, streaming and non-streaming. `rank` is now reported and `bytes` is gone. Clients reading only `content[i].logprob` are unaffected; clients that parsed the placeholder should read `content[i].token_id`. Derender output (`/v1/chat/completions/derender`, `/v1/completions/derender`) is unchanged. `return_tokens_as_token_ids` on the OpenAI endpoints is unchanged.

Documented in `docs/serving/online_serving/renderer.md` (new "Generate Output Logprobs" section, with the breaking-change note) and `derenderer.md`.

## Test Plan

- `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_generate_logprobs_conversion.py` (new): unit tests over `_resolve_logprobs` with a stub tokenizer — decoding + bytes + rank-order preservation, the U+FFFD byte-fallback path where the second half of a two-byte character is only decodable with the preceding sampled id as context, and `content=None`.
- `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_tokens_logprobs.py`: sampled entry carries `token_id`/`rank`, per-candidate ids, `logprobs=0` still emits the sampled token, sampled token missing from the top-k map keeps the `-9999.0` sentinel.
- `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py`, `test_derender_parity.py`: derender chat/completion logprob tests and the coupled-vs-derender parity test now feed the generate-shaped payload; parity assertions on `token`/`bytes` are unchanged.
- `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py`, `test_serving_tokens.py`: streaming chunks and the sampling-mask test read `token_id`.
- Rust: `routes::tests::non_stream_raw_generate_returns_token_output_envelope` and `stream_raw_generate_returns_sse_chunks_and_usage` assert integer `token_id` + `rank` and a null `token`/`bytes` on the wire.

## Test Result

Rust, locally:

```
cargo check -p vllm-server --tests          # clean
cargo test -p vllm-server raw_generate      # 9 passed; 0 failed
```

The two updated assertions run through the mock engine and confirm the wire shape end to end (`"token_id": 33, "rank": 1`, `token`/`bytes` absent), streaming and non-streaming.

Python, locally (CPU-only box, no GPU):

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_generate_logprobs_conversion.py \
       tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_tokens_logprobs.py
7 passed
```

`ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on every touched file.

Caveat on the local Python run: the box has no GPU, so the interpreter is a vLLM 0.29.0 install with this branch's source on `PYTHONPATH`. That is enough for the pure-Python paths above, but the server-backed entrypoints tests do not run in it. `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py` fails there — identically (29 failed, 1 passed) on unmodified `main` in the same setup, so those failures are the environment, not this change. CI is still the first real execution of the server-backed tests; happy to fix up promptly if anything falls over.

## Essential Elements

- [x] Purpose, shape and scope stated above
- [x] Unit tests for the new conversion, updated tests for every touched path
- [x] Docs and release note

title: [Frontend][Core] Sampled-token logprob fast path for /inference/v1/generate (return_token_logprobs)
body:
## Purpose

RL rollout collectors using `/inference/v1/generate` need one float per generated token: the sampled token's logprob. Today that means requesting `logprobs=0` and reading `choices[].logprobs.content[i].logprob`. On the server, that one float travels a path built for top-k logprob objects: the scheduler slices a `LogprobsLists` (token ids, logprobs, ranks — three numpy arrays) per request per step, encodes it into `EngineCoreOutput`, the output processor `.tolist()`s it, detokenizes every entry and appends `Logprob` objects (or `FlatLogprobs`), and the frontend builds a `ChatCompletionLogProbsContent` Pydantic object per token before JSON.

Measured on one L20 with an 8-core host (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, 256-token rollouts with `ignore_eos`, prompts = 2 × concurrency, `temperature=1, top_k=50, top_p=0.95`), `logprobs=0` takes throughput to **0.67–0.73× of no-logprobs** at concurrency 64–512. Where the cost sits, established by switching layers off one at a time (raw runs linked below): the GPU kernels are not it (skipping `_ranks_kernel` is within noise; skipping every logprob kernel is worth ≤5 points); the D2H copy and `tolists()` are free; the per-request `LogprobsLists` slicing → IPC → output-processor → Pydantic path is the whole cost (skipping the slicing alone restores 1.00× at c256).

This PR adds a sampled-token logprob fast path, end to end:

- `GenerateRequest.return_token_logprobs` (request field) and an internal `SamplingParams.sampled_logprobs_only` (requires `logprobs == 0`).
- The scheduler emits `EngineCoreOutput.new_sampled_logprobs`: one float per new token, read from column 0 of the step's logprobs array (the sampler stores the sampled token first), through the `cu_num_generated_tokens` boundaries. No `LogprobsLists` for these requests.
- The output processor keeps a plain float list and the cumulative logprob; it never builds `Logprob` entries and never detokenizes.
- The response carries `choices[].token_logprobs: list[float]`, clamped with the same `max(x, -9999.0)` as the `logprobs` objects, and omits the OpenAI-style `logprobs` object. With `logprobs > 0` both are returned (the sampled column then comes from the existing flat representation). `token_logprobs` is omitted from responses that did not ask for it, so the existing schema is unchanged.
- Requires `--logprobs-mode raw_logprobs` or `processed_logprobs` (400 otherwise): the field is named for log-probabilities and does not hand back logits under that name. `stream=True` is rejected with a 400 (the per-chunk shape is a separate decision).
- The Rust frontend rejects the field with an explicit `invalid_request_error` instead of ignoring it (its `GenerateRequest` flattens unknown fields); the Rust engine-core client mirrors the new last-appended `EngineCoreOutput` field. `cargo check -p vllm-server --tests` and `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client --lib engine_core_output` pass.

It composes with `--return-sampling-mask` (#54901): the rollout contract "mask + sampled-token logprob" is then one ragged list and one flat list per request.

## Test Plan

- `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py -k "return_token_logprobs or sampled_token_logprobs or omits_token_logprobs"` (9 tests, all against a live server): flat array equals the object path's per-token `logprob` (greedy; and under n-gram speculative decoding, where steps produce a ragged number of tokens per request, on a `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` server — without batch-invariant execution the object path was not a stable numerical oracle in that configuration: repeated object-path requests returned identical tokens but sampled logprobs differing by up to ~2e-2, while under batch-invariant execution object and sampled-only paths match exactly across fresh server lifetimes); `logprobs` unset defaults to 0; `logprobs=2` returns both representations with matching values; `n=2` / `n=4` return one aligned array per choice; `-inf`/extreme values clamp like the object path; `stream=True` → 400; field absent unless requested.
- `tests/v1/test_outputs.py`: column-0 selection with and without `cu_num_generated_tokens`, including the ragged `[0, 3, 4, 6]` case; `tests/v1/engine/test_logprobs_processor.py`: float-list accumulation and cumulative logprob, `SamplingParams` validation.
- Exactness under sampling: one server with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and `--return-sampling-mask`, 16 seeded prompts × 64 tokens, each sent once as `logprobs=0` (objects) and once with the field: token sequences identical 16/16, array length equals generated length 16/16, max abs difference 0.0.
- Serving A/B: one `vllm serve` per condition, 3 interleaved rounds, per-round API-server and EngineCore CPU from `/proc`.

## Test Result

vLLM 0.29.0 + #54901 backported, one L20, driver 580.159.04, `/inference/v1/generate`, non-streaming. "vs gen" is relative to the same server with no logprobs requested.

| Model | Concurrency | no logprobs | `logprobs=0` objects | `return_token_logprobs` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | 64 | 18,592 tok/s | 13,495 (0.73×) | **17,868 (0.96×)** |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | 256 | 23,038 | 15,451 (0.67×) | **21,846 (0.95×)** |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B, `--return-sampling-mask` | 64 | 16,452 | 11,106 | **15,453 (0.94×)** |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B, `--return-sampling-mask` | 256 | 20,313 | 13,088 | **19,132 (0.94×)** |
| Qwen3-4B | 64 | 3,524 | 3,351 (0.95×) | **3,503 (0.99×)** |
| Qwen3-4B, `--return-sampling-mask` | 64 | 3,442 | 3,320 | **3,443 (1.00×)** |

On the 0.5B model the field recovers ~84–86% of the throughput that `logprobs=0` costs; response size per request goes from ~41 KB to ~6.8 KB; API-server CPU with logprobs returns to the no-logprobs level (0.39 vs 0.37 of a core at c256) and the EngineCore is at parity. On the GPU-bound 4B model the sampled-token logprob becomes essentially free.

Raw runs, the layer-by-layer decomposition, and the exactness check: <https://github.com/yinli-systems/single-gpu-inference-lab/tree/stage2-compact-sampling-mask/benchmarks/results/l20-flat-token-logprobs> and `.../l20-logprob-engine-decomposition`.

Related: #42259 (logprobs semantics RFC), #54901 (compact sampling masks), #48314 (RL roadmap: RL artifacts data plane). #42283 (FlatLogprobs tail slices) is orthogonal. The AuxOutput connector work (#45635) targets persistence/prefix reuse/external transfer of auxiliary outputs; this change stays on the request-local serving path and does not add a new artifact plane.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for `token_in_token_out logprobs`, `flat logprobs`, `LogprobsProcessor`, `sampled logprobs` on 2026-09-18. #46422 (skip detokenization in beam search) and #55029 (streaming derender logprobs) touch adjacent code; neither changes the generate response shape or the engine-core transport. `SamplingParams.flat_logprobs` is reused for the `logprobs > 0` case rather than adding a second representation.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change; the submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [ROCm] Bump AITER to v0.1.23
body:
## Purpose

Bump the ROCm base image's pinned AITER version from `v0.1.22.post1` to
[`v0.1.23`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/releases/tag/v0.1.23) (released
2026-09-26), AITER's regular bi-weekly release. Follows the same pattern as
prior bumps (#56885, #55968, #52826).

## Duplicate-work check

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "aiter v0.1.23"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "AITER_BRANCH"
```

title: [ROCm][MLA] Add an AITER ASM round-robin decode route for DCP multi-token verify
body:
## Purpose

Adds an opt-in AITER ASM route for decode context parallelism (DCP) combined with speculative decoding on ROCm gfx950.

With DCP, each rank holds a round-robin shard of the KV cache (token `t` on rank `t % dcp_world_size`). A causal verify step of `qlen > 1` cannot run on the ordinary decode kernel, because that kernel applies causality on local indices, which is wrong over a round-robin shard. Today these steps are served by the segmented route (#51705), which expands each verify group into one single-query row per token and runs the Triton decode kernel.

This PR adds the AITER round-robin (`cprr`) ASM decode as an alternative. It keeps the verify group as one row of `qlen` queries and rebuilds each token's global position in-kernel from `g_kv_indptr`, `cp_rank` and `cp_world_size`, so the causal window is applied inside the kernel.

`VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY` selects the route (validated by `env_with_choices`):

- `segmented` (default): existing behavior.
- `asm`: opt-in AITER round-robin ASM decode.

### Per-batch routing

The metadata builder selects exactly one route per decode batch and stores it in the decode metadata:

| route | when |
|---|---|
| PLAIN | `qlen == 1`, or a non-causal block |
| CPRR | causal, `qlen >= 3`, `asm` selected, gfx950, DCP with interleave size 1, speculative decoding |
| SEGMENTED | every other causal `qlen > 1` batch, including `qlen == 2` |

There is no `cprr` kernel below `qlen == 3`, so a `qlen == 2` batch (configured `num_speculative_tokens=1`, or a larger configuration clamped at runtime) uses segmented MLA under `asm` as well. The plain kernel never serves a causal `qlen > 1` batch.

The `cprr` kernels exist only at the native DCP-gathered head counts (16, 32, 64, 128). Other counts are padded up (96 → 128). The output is sliced back as a view; a post-kernel copy would race the symmetric-memory all-to-all combine.

### Non-causal DCP drafts

`supports_non_causal_multi_token_dcp = True` lets a non-causal draft (for example a DSpark draft with `dflash_config.causal = false`) run under DCP. Such a batch takes the PLAIN route: each rank attends its whole local shard without a mask, and the per-row LSE merge across ranks is exact, because non-causal attention needs no cross-shard causal window. This does not depend on `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY` and was validated end to end on the default `segmented` route (below).

### KV split cap (CPRR only)

When CPRR is selected, `max_split_per_batch` is capped at the device CU count. At low batch size, splitting the KV axis is the main source of parallelism; without a cap, AITER's reduction scratch can reach about 9.35 GiB. Scratch sizing, metadata generation, and the kernel launch all use the same cap, so the buffers they share cannot disagree. The default segmented route is unchanged.

## End-to-end validation

Same build, model, and hardware for every row. Only `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY`, `num_speculative_tokens`, and (last row) the draft's causality change.

- 8× MI355X (gfx950), TP8, DCP8, fp8 KV cache
- `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (MXFP4) + `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` draft, probabilistic drafting, block rejection sampling
- Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-dee37d89115db4c94a820a79a78a7828e141c910` (AITER 0.1.21.post1) with this PR's `vllm/envs.py` and `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py` applied

Serve command:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY={asm|segmented} \
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --dcp-comm-backend a2a --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors --moe-backend auto \
  --language-model-only --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' \
  --enable-prefix-caching --prefix-cache-retention-interval 12288 \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","max_cudagraph_capture_size":128,"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated","+situ_and_mul"]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":N,"attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_MLA","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}'
```

### Accuracy: GSM8K

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=16,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,trust_remote_code=True \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5
```

5-shot, all 1319 questions. Standard error is about ±0.005.

| route | `num_speculative_tokens` | strict-match | flexible-extract | acceptance rate | acceptance length |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| asm | 7 | 0.9666 | 0.9659 | 0.418 | 3.92 |
| segmented | 7 | 0.9606 | 0.9606 | 0.418 | 3.93 |
| asm (qlen 2 → segmented fallback) | 1 | 0.9613 | 0.9613 | 0.937 | 1.94 |
| segmented | 1 | 0.9606 | 0.9598 | 0.937 | 1.94 |
| segmented, **non-causal draft** | 7 | 0.9606 | 0.9606 | 0.446 | 4.12 |

All routes are within one standard error, and acceptance is unchanged by the route, as expected: only the target's attention kernel differs.

### Performance: `vllm bench serve`, ISL 100K, OSL 256

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code \
  --dataset-name custom --dataset-path longctx_code_100k.jsonl \
  --custom-output-len 256 --skip-chat-template --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency C --num-prompts max(8, 2*C) --num-warmups 1 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
```

The dataset is 16 distinct prompts of 99.9K–100K tokens of real source code (vLLM's own Python sources), so the draft sees natural text. Random-token prompts give near-zero acceptance and are not meaningful for this comparison. Acceptance comes from the server's `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters, differenced around each run.

`num_speculative_tokens=7` (target verify at qlen 8):

| C | route | output tok/s | mean TPOT ms | p99 TPOT ms | acceptance rate | acceptance length |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | segmented | 21.7 | 22.10 | 27.74 | 0.215 | 2.50 |
| 1 | asm | **28.6** | **10.92** | 14.38 | 0.208 | 2.46 |
| 2 | segmented | 51.1 | 36.05 | 50.16 | 0.186 | 2.30 |
| 2 | asm | **120.2** | **14.56** | 17.03 | 0.169 | 2.18 |
| 4 | segmented | 66.5 | 53.13 | 64.58 | 0.182 | 2.28 |
| 4 | asm | **200.8** | **15.59** | 25.25 | 0.229 | 2.60 |
| 8 | segmented | 36.8 | 179.18 | 312.60 | 0.180 | 2.26 |
| 8 | asm | **57.9** | **110.10** | 223.37 | 0.183 | 2.28 |

Mean TPOT improves 2.0× at batch 1, 2.5× at C=2, 3.4× at C=4 and 1.6× at C=8. At C=1 the output throughput gain is smaller than the TPOT gain because each 256-token request also pays a ~6 s 100K-token prefill. At C=8 both routes' TPOT includes decode steps that share the batch with other requests' 100K-token chunked prefills.

`num_speculative_tokens=1` (every verify step at qlen 2, so `asm` falls back to segmented):

| C | route | output tok/s | mean TPOT ms | acceptance rate |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | asm | 24.4 | 17.00 | 0.650 |
| 1 | segmented | 24.6 | 16.69 | 0.675 |
| 4 | asm | 104.7 | 33.56 | 0.598 |
| 4 | segmented | 106.5 | 32.70 | 0.613 |

The two settings match within noise, as they should when both serve qlen 2 on the segmented kernel.

### Routes actually taken

Counted from the per-batch route in the decode metadata (local instrumentation, not part of this PR):

- `asm`, N=7: target (96 heads) and draft (64 heads) verify batches all on CPRR; PLAIN only for qlen 1 warmup.
- `asm`, N=1: about 6,600 target verify batches at qlen 2 on SEGMENTED, plus a qlen 3 batch on CPRR in the same server, so the mixed CPRR/segmented path runs end to end under `asm`.
- `segmented`, N=7: all verify batches on SEGMENTED.
- `segmented`, non-causal draft: draft batches (qlen 7, non-causal) on PLAIN, target on SEGMENTED.

### ROCm 7.2 nightly

Re-validated on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098` (ROCm 7.2, AITER 0.1.22.post1, which ships the `cprr` kernels) with this PR applied. Same hardware, model, serve command and datasets as above.

| route | `num_speculative_tokens` | GSM8K strict-match | GSM8K flexible-extract | acceptance length (GSM8K) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| asm | 7 | 0.9613 | 0.9613 | 4.34 |
| segmented | 7 | 0.9651 | 0.9651 | 4.37 |
| asm (qlen 2 → segmented fallback) | 1 | 0.9636 | 0.9636 | 1.95 |

| C | route | output tok/s | mean TPOT ms | p99 TPOT ms |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | segmented | 21.2 | 23.23 | 32.44 |
| 1 | asm | **29.3** | **10.26** | 12.32 |
| 4 | segmented | 66.8 | 53.95 | 66.00 |
| 4 | asm | **204.4** | **15.31** | 21.16 |

Accuracy is within one standard error across routes, and mean TPOT improves 2.3× at batch 1 and 3.5× at C=4, consistent with the ROCm 10 results. Under `asm`, all N=7 verify batches took CPRR; at N=1, about 6,000 qlen-2 batches took the segmented fallback.

Note: on this image, Kimi-K3 with a DSpark draft and CUDA graphs fails during startup on either route, independent of this PR. The draft caches its KV-cache pointers during CUDA graph memory profiling, which runs against a throwaway KV cache that is freed before the real one is allocated. These runs include a small fix that refreshes those pointers when the allocation changes; it will be sent as a separate PR.

## Test Plan

```bash
# routing and selection (CPU)
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py

# real metadata builder + real ASM kernel (gfx950 + AITER)
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py

# pre-existing AITER MLA split suite
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py

pre-commit run --files vllm/envs.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py
```

## Test Result

On MI355X (gfx950), images `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098` (ROCm 10) and `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098` (ROCm 7.2), each with this PR applied, with identical results:

| file | result |
|---|---|
| `test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py` | 22 passed |
| `test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py` | 65 passed |
| `test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py` | 4 passed |

`pre-commit` passes on all changed files.

The numerics tests drive the real `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder.build()` and ASM kernel for each of 8 simulated DCP shards at 128 gathered heads (native) and 96 (padded to 128), check each shard against an exact torch reference, check that the LSE merge reproduces full-context attention, and include a positive control: telling the kernel the wrong `cp_rank` must break the result.

**AITER requirement.** Needs an AITER build that ships the round-robin MLA decode kernels (ROCm/aiter#4521).

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve caller parameters in offline pooling
body:
## Purpose

`LLM.encode()` writes its internal pooling task into the caller's `PoolingParams`. Reusing `PoolingParams(use_activation=False)` first with an `embed` LLM and later with a separate `token_embed` LLM fails before inference:

```text
You cannot overwrite param.task='embed' with pooling_task='token_embed'!
```

Each instance keeps its own configured task. The problem is the first call leaving that task in the shared parameter object.

Clone each request's parameters before assigning the task in the base offline IO processor, and before calling the plugin's `merge_pooling_params()`. BGE-M3 and ColBERT change the parameters during that merge, before reaching the base processor. The existing check for an explicitly conflicting task stays unchanged.

I checked existing issues and PRs for parameter reuse and task mutation and found no matching fix. #50884 handles `SamplingParams` seeds and does not change this path.

## Test Plan

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 \
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_io_processor.py \
  tests/test_pooling_params.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_late_interaction_serving.py \
  -q -p no:cacheprovider

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/pooling/base/io_processor.py \
  vllm/entrypoints/pooling/pooling/io_processor.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_io_processor.py

pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/pooling/base/io_processor.py \
  vllm/entrypoints/pooling/pooling/io_processor.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_io_processor.py
```

## Test Result

- **20 passed** across the three existing test files.
- Local checks using the BGE-M3 and ColBERT merge methods reproduced caller-parameter mutation before the plugin fix. All four checks pass afterward (shared parameters and parameter lists for each plugin), preserving the plugin's internal settings.
- Pre-commit checks and mypy 3.12 pass.

Validation used the Python sources on CPU with `--noconftest` to skip the global test fixtures. The local plugin checks stub preprocessing; no model weights were loaded.

title: [Perf][Model Loader] Fault in mmap'd weight pages before host-to-device copies on integrated GPUs
body:
## Purpose

Addresses #58726.

On integrated GPUs (DGX Spark / GB10), the shared weight loaders copy each checkpoint tensor to the GPU with `param.copy_(loaded_weight)` straight from the safetensors mmap view. For a contiguous, same-dtype source, PyTorch passes that pageable pointer directly to the driver copy, so the page faults happen inside the copy. On GB10 that is several times slower than faulting the same pages on the CPU first: 1.7–3.0 ms vs 0.08–0.64 ms per 800 KiB tensor in #58726. `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` has at least 140k such tensors, and its main weight load takes 452 s from NFS and 475 s from local NVMe.

This adds `copy_weight_(dst, src)` to `vllm/model_executor/utils.py`. On an integrated GPU it touches one byte per page of `src`, then runs `dst.copy_(src)`. It is used at the 26 copy sites of the shared loaders: `linear.py` (8), `parameter.py` (6), `routed_experts.py` (8), `vocab_parallel_embedding.py` (2) and `default_weight_loader` (2).

- **Gate:** `current_platform.is_integrated_gpu()` for a CUDA destination, cached per device. On a discrete Ada Lovelace GPU the same micro-benchmark shows the plain copy is fastest in every cache state, and the touch adds 0.022–0.028 ms per tensor, so it stays off there. When off, the extra checks cost ~0.46 µs per call (0.91 vs 0.45 µs for a 16-byte CPU copy), about 0.14 s per 300k tensors.
- **Only contiguous, same-dtype CPU sources are touched.** Non-contiguous or dtype-converting copies already go through a CPU temporary in PyTorch (`copy_requires_temporaries` in `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Copy.cu`), which faults the pages on the CPU.
- **Why at the copy site rather than in `safetensors_weights_iterator`** (discussed with @gitbisector in #58726):
  - Under TP each rank touches only the slice it copies. A prefault in the iterator read whole tensors: ~287 GiB per rank on DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4, and a slower load at the default `read_ahead_kb=128`.
  - The touch runs right before the copy, so a consumer that buffers the weight stream can't have the pages evicted in between.
  - Tensors a model serves from the mapping (#58439) are never copied, so they are never touched, and no size cap is needed.
- **Not covered:** model-specific loaders that call `.copy_()` or `.to(device)` themselves keep today's behaviour until they call the helper.
- **Measured only on GB10** (TP=1 below, TP=4 by @gitbisector). Other integrated devices, such as Jetson Orin / Thor, will take the touch path but are untested. I haven't checked what GH200 reports as `is_integrated`; if it reports 0, nothing changes there.

## Test Plan

- New tests in `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py`:
  - `test_copy_weight_prefault_copies_exact_bytes`: with the gate forced on, the helper accepts 0-d, empty, bf16, fp8 and dim-1-narrowed sources and copies them byte for byte. CI has no integrated GPU, so this is the only coverage of that path.
  - `test_copy_weight_prefault_maps_the_mmap_view`: after the call, every page of a safetensors view is mapped (`/proc/self/smaps` Rss of the file mapping). With the touch disabled it fails: 64 KiB mapped vs 4 MiB.
- Existing CPU-runnable loader tests, before and after the change.
- `pre-commit` on the changed files, including `mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual`.
- Boot A/B on a DGX Spark.

```bash
# CPU only, repo on PYTHONPATH inside vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 (torch 2.13.0+cu130), no GPU
docker run --rm -v $PWD:/w:ro -e PYTHONPATH=/w -w /w --entrypoint bash vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 -c \
  "uv pip install --system -q tblib pytest && python3 -m pytest -q \
   tests/model_executor/test_utils.py \
   tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py tests/kernels/moe/test_fp8_tp_loading.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_tying.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_gpt_oss_weight_loading.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py"

pre-commit run --files <changed files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed files>
```

## Test Result

- `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py`: 18 passed (12 existing, 6 new).
- Loader tests: 216 passed, 5 skipped. 38 tests fail with and without the change, the same set on both, all because the container has no GPU:
  - 18 error at setup with `Failed to infer device type`.
  - 18 `test_reload` cases fail because `current_platform.device_count` is `None`.
  - 2 `test_fp8_tp_default_keeps_refined_layout[*-triton]` cases can't confirm the Triton kernel, so the layer pads its TP shard instead of refining the block shape.
- `pre-commit` and `mypy-3.12` passed.

### Boot A/B, DGX Spark (GB10), TP=1

Nine full server boots of `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, interleaved, with the client page cache for the checkpoint dropped before each one.

- **Build:** the image is vLLM v0.30.0 plus out-of-tree patches, not `main`. The helper is copied from this branch and applied to v0.30.0's copies of the same files (25 sites; v0.30.0's `_load_w2` has no chunk loop). It predates a cleanup that renamed the gate function and dropped a redundant `numel() > 0` check, which doesn't change behaviour here. A counting wrapper, not part of this PR, logged the gate and how many copies were touched.
- **Out-of-tree patches on in every arm:** the expert-name index (= #58720, merged), an MTP name prefilter, and the PLE table served from the mapping (never copied).
- **Storage:** NFS with the client's `read_ahead_kb` at 16384, or local NVMe at the default 128.

| loader | storage | main load (s) | MTP load (s) | start → `/health` (s) | swapped out, start → KV profile (GiB) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| stock | NFS | 451.8 | 36.1 | 584 | 4.4 |
| this PR (3 boots) | NFS | 25.9 / 27.0 / 28.0 | 0.8 | 124–129 | 3.6–4.3 |
| stock | NVMe | 475.2 | 31.7 | 609 | 4.2 |
| this PR (2 boots) | NVMe | 46.4 / 54.5 | 2.6–2.9 | 149–153 | 3.2–4.0 |
| *out-of-tree, for reference: `pread` tensors ≤ 64 MiB in the iterator, clone / chunked copy above that* | NFS / NVMe | 21.0 / 88.5 | 1.2 / 1.3 | 113 / 179 | 0 / 0 |

- The gate logged `cuda:0 = True` in every boot with this PR. By the counter's last line (140,000 calls), 139,965 copies (63.4 GiB) had been touched. The other 35 were copies PyTorch stages through a CPU temporary anyway.
- Greedy outputs (5 prompts × 400 tokens, temperature 0) and first-token logprobs are identical in all nine boots, and decode speed is unchanged. No accuracy eval was run: the touch only reads the source, so the loaded weights are byte-identical (unit test above).
- Swap: loading from mmap views pushes 3.2–4.4 GiB of other memory to swap on this 128 GB machine, and stock loading does it as much as this PR. The pread variant doesn't map the files and doesn't swap. vLLM counts the swapped-out memory as free when it sizes the KV cache. I haven't looked into why the kernel swaps here.
### TP=4 (from @gitbisector, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#issuecomment-5852543296))

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` on four GB10s, this PR ported to a v0.28.1-based build (25 of the 26 sites), load-only boots, page cache dropped before each, arms interleaved. Times are `Model loading took` on the slowest rank.

| `read_ahead_kb` | boots | stock | this PR | read per rank vs stock |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 3 + 3 | 192–195 s | 156–161 s (−18%) | +0–8 GiB |
| 128 | 3 + 3 | 205–207 s | 149–151 s (−27%) | +0–8 GiB |
| 1024, consumer that sorts the stream | 1 + 1 | 248 s | 225 s | +2–10 GiB |

At 128 the iterator-level prefault made this load slower (202 → 241 s) because every rank read whole tensors (~287 GiB); at the copy site each rank reads about what stock reads. Most of the gain is the slowest rank catching up: in stock, the ranks holding slices 0 and 2 lag by 25–60 s on small same-dtype slices (expert scales, FP8 attention rows). The routed experts there are `I8` loaded into `uint8` params, a converting copy that PyTorch already stages on the CPU, so the helper touches 5.6 of 72.3 GiB per rank.

## Duplicate-work check

- No open PR references #58726; searches for "prefault", "integrated gpu weight loading" and "mmap page fault copy" found none that change these copy sites.
- #49991 (ROCm, clones in the iterator behind an env flag, for a KFD copy-on-write issue) and #50794 (Ascend, clones before the H2D copy to avoid a DMA hang) handle the same copies on other platforms, for different causes.
- #57973 (safetensors prefetch loader) and #55985 (fastsafetensors fit planner) are alternative load paths.
- #58857 / #58782 remove the `sorted()` buffering in the DeepSeek-V4 VL wrappers; complementary to this.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted (Claude Opus 5.5): implementation, tests, the boot A/B scripts, and a draft of this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and boots above on my own machines.

title: fix(mla): support NoPE head sizes by zeroing RoPE tail in SM120 backend
body:
NoPE architectures with `qk_rope_head_dim=0` and `head_size=512` failed under `fp8_ds_mla` cache lines because the underlying kernel expects a 64-dim RoPE tail to preserve the packed 656-byte cache ABI. Zero-padding `k_pe` to 64 elements during `do_kv_cache_update` satisfies the hardware memory layout without requiring kernel modifications or cross-architecture fallbacks. This enables native SM120 sparse MLA execution for models without positional embeddings while leaving standard 576-dim paths intact.

Fixes #55773.

title: [Bugfix] Keep FlashAttention sparse ahead of FlashInfer SM90 for NoPE-512 MLA
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #56564.

`_get_backend_priorities` inserts `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` at the **front** of the SM90 sparse list whenever `head_size == 512`:

```python
sparse_tail = [FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE, FLASHMLA_SPARSE]
if head_size == 512:
    sparse_tail.insert(0, FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90)
```

GLM-5.3-Flash is NoPE MLA (`kv_lora_rank=512`, `qk_rope_head_dim=0`), so `head_size = 512` and the condition fires. The first four non-sparse candidates are rejected (the model requires sparse), which makes the winner whatever leads `sparse_tail`. Once FlashInfer >= 0.6.18 satisfies `has_flashinfer_sm90_nope_mla()` (the `ckv_scale_arr` kwarg check), the SM90 FlashInfer sparse backend is selected by default.

The reported measurements on H100 (#56564) put that backend **36% behind `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` at concurrency 1 and 70% behind at concurrency 8** (output 754 → 230 tok/s), with **identical MTP acceptance length** — so the gap is the per-step attention kernel, not the drafting path. The issue reporter re-confirmed on nightly `7f1a539` / FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1 that the priority is unchanged and the workaround is still an explicit `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE`.

## Change

Drop the `head_size == 512` special case: NoPE-512 and DeepSeek-576 now share one SM90 sparse order, with `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` kept last as a fallback for hosts where the FlashAttention sparse path is unavailable. No behavior change for 576, for SM100/SM120, or for the non-sparse lists.

Two things that previously argued for keeping FlashInfer first no longer do:

- The `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` TMA-descriptor log spam (#56563) was fixed by #55385.
- There is an open CUDA illegal-memory-access report against the FlashInfer SM90 sparse backend for this exact model (#55626), which is a further argument against making it the default on sm_90.

If the intent behind #53906's `insert(0, ...)` was a specific configuration where the FlashInfer path does win on Hopper (FP8 KV in-kernel dequant halving HBM traffic is a plausible one), a narrower gate on that configuration would be preferable to a blanket head-size rule — happy to rework it that way, but there is currently no published benchmark on sm_90 supporting the inversion while there is one against it.

## Test

`tests/v1/attention/test_flashmla_nope_sm90_backend_selection.py` gains two cases (both pure priority-table logic, no GPU needed):

- `test_sm90_sparse_priority_prefers_flash_attn[nope512|ds576]` — `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` leads the SM90 sparse list for both head sizes, and `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` remains present but behind it
- `test_sm90_sparse_priority_identical_across_head_sizes` — `head_size` does not reorder the SM90 sparse list

The existing SM100/576 invariants in that file are untouched and still pass unchanged (they assert `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` leads on SM100, which this diff does not affect).

cc @jtatum (reporter)

title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix Qwen4Exp MTP buffer placement, config parsing, and Triton warmup
body:
## Purpose

This PR addresses three Qwen4Exp issues found during model bring-up. It places the MTP hidden buffer on the configured device, handles two config compatibility cases (M-RoPE keys and Transformers' `layer_types` spelling), and includes Qwen4Exp in the existing Qwen Triton warmup dispatch.

## Changes

### The MTP hidden buffer's device

`torch.empty` for the spec-decode hidden buffer passes no `device`, so the buffer follows the ambient default instead of `vllm_config.device_config.device`. The NVIDIA and AMD backends carried the same allocation.

Both now call `make_mtp_hidden_buffer()` in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/mtp.py`, which keeps the existing condition (`speculative_config.method == "mtp"` on the last pipeline stage), shape (`max_num_batched_tokens x hc_count * hidden_size`) and dtype, and passes the configured device.

### Config parsing

- **M-RoPE keys.** Qwen4Exp uses `mrope_section` and `mrope_interleaved`, which transformers' rope validator does not know for `rope_type="default"`, so it reports them as unrecognized during config loading. Both are added to `ignore_keys_at_rope_validation` on the text config and on the outer config that mirrors its `rope_parameters`; other unknown keys still warn.
- **`layer_types` spelling.** transformers' Qwen4Exp config canonicalizes `full_attention` entries to `qwen_sparse_attention`, so checkpoints re-exported through it serialize that name, and vLLM — which keys on `full_attention` plus `indexer_n_heads` — does not classify those entries as QSA layers. The spelling is mapped back at config construction.

### Triton warmup

`qwen_triton_warmup` covers the gated RMS norm, the causal conv, the post-conv preparation and the decode state update. For Qwen4Exp, these remain Triton kernels regardless of the selected prefill backend, but `qwen4_exp` and `qwen4_exp_text` are not in `_QWEN_MODEL_TYPES`, so the warmup returns at the gate. Without the dispatch entry, these kernels can compile on first use.

`qwen4_exp_mtp` is not added: `kernel_warmup` passes `worker.vllm_config.model_config`, which is the target model's.

## Notes

The device test allocates on `meta`, which is never the ambient default, so it catches an implicit allocation without requiring CUDA. The warmup test stops at the dispatch gate; the kernels themselves are covered by the existing CUDA test in the same file.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py -q
pytest tests/model_executor/test_qwen_triton_warmup.py -q
```

| Area | Test |
|---|---|
| MTP buffer device | `test_mtp_hidden_buffer_is_allocated_on_the_configured_device`, `test_mtp_hidden_buffer_is_absent_without_mtp_speculation` |
| Config parsing | `test_rope_validation_accepts_mrope_keys_and_still_warns_for_unknown_keys`, `test_text_config_normalizes_transformers_sparse_attention_spelling` |
| Triton warmup | `test_qwen_triton_warmup_dispatch_gate` |

Each was checked by reverting its production hunk and confirming the test fails.

## Test Result

```
tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py             15 passed
tests/model_executor/test_qwen_triton_warmup.py    6 passed
```

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `git diff --check` are clean on the changed files. `mypy` (Python 3.10) reports three diagnostics — `rope_parameters` in `qwen4_exp/config.py` and `_tower_model_names` in the two `model.py` files — the same three, in the same files with the same messages, that it reports on the base commit.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Profile and validate kv_cache_memory_bytes instead of skipping the profile
body:
## Purpose

`--kv-cache-memory-bytes` never checked the size it was handed. The branch returned before `memory_profiling` ran, logged "skipped memory profiling", and passed the number straight through. Nothing compared it against what the model needs for itself, so a size that is too large starts fine, serves short requests, and then OOMs in the middle of one once traffic reaches the activation peak.

The same measurement gap exists under `gpu_memory_utilization`, but it stays hidden there: the KV size is derived from a budget that is only a fraction of the device, so whatever the profile missed lands in the part the utilization fraction left unallocated. A pinned size has no such slack — the operator sized it to use what was free — so the pinned cache and the unprofiled activation peak compete for the same free memory.

There is a second half to it. Even when the profile does run, it forwards with `skip_attn=True`, because there is no KV cache yet to attend against. The attention activations, and the device memory those kernels take the first time they launch, are simply not in the figure. Harmless where slack absorbs it; not harmless when the cache was pinned to that figure.

## What this changes

Run the profile for a pinned size too, and check the value against the result. If it does not fit, fail at startup and report the largest size admitted by this profile. Refusing rather than quietly capping is deliberate: a pinned size is an explicit capacity decision, and silently reducing it hides the one number this option exists to control. Starting anyway is worse — the bytes are spent either way, and the failure just moves to a request.

When a size is pinned, extend the profile with attention: build the same minimal KV cache the CUDA graph profiling already uses, run a short ladder of batch widths through it, then tear it down. The ladder is not redundant with its widest rung, since the caching allocator keeps whole segments per size class and a served mix of widths costs more than the widest one alone. Then account for what the allocator holds beyond the live peak — `memory_profiling` measures `allocated_bytes.all.peak`, which is the right call where slack absorbs the difference and the wrong one where there is none.

All of it sits inside the pinned branch; the `gpu_memory_utilization` path is untouched.

## What it deliberately does not do

The reported figure is an upper bound, not a safe setting, and the error message says so. The profile forwards against a *minimal* KV cache, so peaks that scale with context length are still outside it. For the serve described below, the unmargined bound was 3.53 GiB. A pinned size at that bound still OOMed under four concurrent requests, while 3.07 GiB completed the workload without failure. I did not measure where the real boundary between those two is, so no margin is applied here — the number is what the profile can account for, and the operator is told to leave room under it.

A percentage margin was the first thing I tried, and I dropped it. The shortfall scales with the model's activation footprint rather than with the cache, so a fraction of the cache size wastes memory wherever the cache is large; and a fraction fitted to a single measurement is not evidence, it just reproduces that measurement.

## Test Plan

Two-rank pipeline-parallel serve with an unbalanced layer split and the KV cache pinned. The rank carrying the larger share is the one that runs out. Workload: text prompts from 1.6k to 259k tokens, images from 360 to 14k tokens, and mixed batches at concurrency 3 and 4.

## Test Result

Profiled non-KV usage on that rank, against an observed non-KV peak of 59.24 GiB under the same workload:

| profile | non-KV |
| --- | --- |
| before this change (figure from a later probe, since nothing was measured) | 57.52 GiB |
| with attention in the profile | 58.28 GiB |
| with allocator overhead as well | 59.11 GiB |

A pinned 4.1 GiB that used to start and OOM later is now refused at startup:

```
ValueError: kv_cache_memory_bytes=4400000000 (4.1 GiB) does not fit on this rank. Of 62.93 GiB free at startup the model needs 59.11 GiB for weights, persistent workspaces and its activation peak, 0.21 GiB for CUDA graphs and 0.08 GiB the caching allocator holds beyond that peak, leaving 3.53 GiB. Set --kv-cache-memory-bytes=3785959936 or lower, or give this rank more room (fewer layers on it, a smaller max_num_batched_tokens or max_model_len). That figure is an upper bound, not a safe setting: the profile runs against a minimal KV cache, so peaks that scale with context length are not in it. Leave headroom below it.
```

At a pinned size below the bound the same serve finishes the whole workload with no failures, including a 258,953-token prompt and four concurrent image requests.

`ruff check` and `ruff format` pass. The `mypy` hook reports five errors in this file; all five are present on the unmodified file at the same base and none are on the added lines.

All results above come from local runs on one two-GPU host.

title: [Spec Decode][Qwen4Exp] RecoverSSM for Qwen GDN and the PLE short conv
body:
## Purpose

Speculative decoding on Gated DeltaNet today snapshots the full recurrent state after every draft position, and
reserves one Mamba block per draft position. This PR brings the **RecoverSSM** protocol that Kimi-K3 KDA already uses
to the Qwen GDN layers of Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next), plus its PLE dilated short conv:

- **Verify** runs from a read-only checkpoint and stores a small per-token replay record
  `[correction (V), normalized key (K), gate (1)]` in fp32.
- **Commit** (after sampling) replays only the accepted tokens and writes the recurrent state once, plus the
  block-boundary state in align mode. The PLE short conv compacts its accepted window with the same plan.
- `num_speculative_blocks = 0`: no per-draft Mamba blocks.

Enabled like KDA's: `--use-replayssm` together with speculative decoding. Qwen4Exp (CausalLM, ConditionalGeneration,
MTP) declares `SupportsReplaySSM`; without spec decoding the flag is rejected on Qwen4Exp (there is no plain ReplaySSM
path for its GDN/PLE layers). Requires the V2 model runner for align mode, the Triton mamba backend and PP=1 (the same
checks as KDA). The RecoverSSM builders declare `AttentionCGSupport.NEVER`, so the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` falls
back to PIECEWISE with the usual warning. That fallback needed one fix: with breakable CUDA graphs (auto-enabled on
this setup; they split at attention with an empty `splitting_ops`, with or without torch.compile) it dropped to NONE
(no CUDA graphs at all); it now resolves to PIECEWISE there. FULL graph support for RecoverSSM is a follow-up.

Two commits:
1. `[Mamba] Share RecoverSSM commit kernels and helpers across models`: the commit-plan and conv-compaction kernels
   move from `models/kimi_k3` to `model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/recoverssm.py` (Kimi keeps its private names as
   aliases; kernel source unchanged); `mamba/recoverssm_utils.py`; generic request-mapping helpers in
   `v1/attention/backends/recoverssm_metadata.py`; `CacheConfig.use_kda_recoverssm` → `use_recoverssm`. No functional
   change for Kimi-K3.
2. `[Spec Decode][Qwen4Exp] RecoverSSM for Qwen GDN and the PLE short conv`: GDN verify/commit kernels
   (`mamba/gdn/recoverssm_gdn.py`), metadata builders (`gdn_recoverssm.py`, `ple_recoverssm.py`), the layer and model
   integration. The verify reads strided q/k/v views of the conv output and writes straight into the layer output.
   The generic Mamba metadata builder no longer allocates the Mamba2 ReplaySSM ring-buffer workspaces when
   `--use-replayssm` selects RecoverSSM (the PLE short conv uses that builder).

Related: #49887 and #56466 (ReplaySSM for GDN) take the ring-buffer route; this PR reuses the merged RecoverSSM
protocol instead (discussed in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56466#issuecomment-5845393579).

## Test Plan

- `tests/kernels/mamba/test_recoverssm_gdn.py`: verify bit-identical to the native fused kernel (checkpoint untouched);
  commit vs the native per-token states (accepted 1–4); align boundaries (8 cases, incl. exact-boundary and crossing);
  mixed prefill/decode mapping and non-contiguous request rows; extreme gates × 3 seeds; strided q/k/v views + `out=`
  (uniform and ragged windows 4/1/3) and the layer's view/fallback decision; BF16 recurrent state (verify exact; commit
  rounds once: within one BF16 ulp of the FP32 reference and no further from it than the native path);
  malformed-input rejection.
- `tests/kernels/mamba/test_recoverssm_ple.py`: spec conv + commit vs the stock token-by-token decode (accepted 1, 2,
  full window; 4 align cases; non-contiguous request rows), bit-identical states and outputs.
- `tests/config/test_recoverssm_config.py`: selection through the real validator (target and the MTP drafter's derived
  config), runtime-check rejections, no spec decoding, unsupported architectures, PIECEWISE fallback declaration.
- Server: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (NVFP4 experts, FP8 GDN), one DGX Spark GB10 (sm_121), MTP K=3, align mode + prefix
  caching, 2 starts per arm: output hashes, cache-hit replay, decode and agent-loop timing.

## Test Result

Tests on GB10 (sm_121): GDN + PLE kernel tests 72 passed, config tests 18 passed. ruff, mypy (tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.12), typos: clean.

Server, native GDN spec decode (align) vs RecoverSSM (align), 2 starts per arm
([data](https://github.com/jschmied/qwen38-flash-next-gb10/blob/55687ace78c09d05892bb0663b92838c06459166/notes/speed-of-light.md#L661-L695)):

| | native (align) | RecoverSSM (align) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 decode, ms per verify cycle | 55.71–56.65 | 54.37–54.38 | −1.3…−2.3 ms |
| c=4 decode, ms per verify cycle | 105.07–105.41 | 99.59–99.91 | −5.2 % |
| agent loop (8 dependent turns), s/turn | 1.31 | 1.10 | −16 % |
| prefix-cache hit rate | 77.4 % | 82.1 % | +4.7 pp |
| KV tokens in the same 4 GiB | 75,678 | 103,953 | +37 % |

- Node trace ([§4u](https://github.com/jschmied/qwen38-flash-next-gb10/blob/55687ace78c09d05892bb0663b92838c06459166/notes/speed-of-light.md#L696-L735)):
  the per-draft state write-back is gone (GDN `out_proj` 101 → 74 µs, no dirty-L2 aftershock); the commit runs at the
  DRAM floor (224 GB/s).
- The zero-copy verify adds −1.2…−1.6 % at c=1 with identical outputs
  ([§5g](https://github.com/jschmied/qwen38-flash-next-gb10/blob/55687ace78c09d05892bb0663b92838c06459166/notes/speed-of-light.md#L1031)).
- Output: cache-hit replay reproduces the first pass 8/8 in every run. Text differs from the native path at the size of a
  reduction-order change (first greedy divergence at a median of 26 tokens, vs 31 for a pure reduction-order change),
  because the recurrent state is now accumulated per commit instead of per token.
- This PR's final shape on the same box (one start each): `--use-replayssm` with explicit PIECEWISE: c=1 21.22 ms/tok,
  output hashes and cache-hit replay identical to the validated reference; default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`: resolves to
  PIECEWISE, c=1 21.31 ms/tok, c=1 and c=4 hashes identical to the reference, cache-hit replay 8/8.
