title: [Distributed] Enable custom all-reduce under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
body:
Fixes #50136 ## Problem `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` forces custom all-reduce off and runs every TP all-reduce through NCCL pinned to one channel. Custom all-reduce cannot simply be re-enabled because `should_custom_ar()` picks the backend by tensor size, and the tensor is `[num_tokens, hidden]`: ```mermaid flowchart LR A["all-reduce [tokens, hidden]"] --> B{"bytes < 8 MiB?"} B -- "yes (decode, small prefill)" --> C["custom kernel
fp32 accumulate, round once"] B -- "no (large prefill batch)" --> D["NCCL
rounds to bf16 at every tree step"] ``` The same request is reduced by different summation orders depending on what else the scheduler batched with it. Measured on 4xH100, TP=4, bf16: NCCL and the custom kernel disagree in 33% of output elements. End to end (Qwen2.5-1.5B, bs=1 vs bs=24, custom all-reduce on): 24/24 prompts diverge, starting at position 0. ## Fix Under batch invariance, make the backend choice size-independent and keep the custom kernel on a fixed reduction order: 1. Stop forcing `disable_custom_all_reduce` (`config/parallel.py`). 2. `should_custom_ar()` ignores the size threshold; `all_reduce()` reduces inputs above `max_size` in `max_size` chunks. The 1-stage kernel sums each element independently in rank order 0..N-1, so chunking is bit-exact (`custom_all_reduce.py`). 3. Pin `VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO=1stage` in `override_envs_for_invariance()`. The 2-stage kernel rotates the rank order per slice, which is size-dependent (fp32: 20-30% of elements differ between sizes). 4. Gate AITER all-reduce and QuickReduce off under batch invariance, next to the existing FlashInfer gate. Without the forced disable they would become reachable on ROCm, and neither has a fixed reduction order (`cuda_communicator.py`). Chunking is chosen over sizing the IPC buffer to `max_num_batched_tokens x hidden` at init: no extra memory, no model info needed in the communicator, and it works for any all-reduce shape (vision towers, MoE). Outside batch invariance nothing changes. Latency inside a CUDA graph, bf16, TP=4 H100, per all-reduce: | Size | custom 1-stage | NCCL (pinned, current BI path) | |---|---|---| | 24 KiB (decode) | 5 us | 39 us | | 8 MiB | 81 us | 693 us | ## Test plan All on H100, TP=4 unless noted. - New `test_custom_allreduce_chunked[2,4]`: 3-chunk 17.6 MiB input matches the fp32 sequential reference bitwise, eager and inside a CUDA graph. New unit test for the size gate under batch invariance. Full `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py`: 19 passed, 1 skipped (SM100-only). - `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py` with `VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4`: 22/22 pass (all attention backends), custom all-reduce now active. - `tests/v1/determinism/test_online_batch_invariance.py` with `VLLM_TP_SIZE=4`: 3/3 pass. - VLM (`Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct`, image inputs) bs=1 vs bsN at TP=4 with batch invariance: bitwise identical. - Standalone bs=1 vs bs=24 on Qwen2.5-1.5B with prefix caching off: 24/24 diverge before, 0/24 after.

title: [Perf][Core] Restore compact prefix-cache entries after duplicate eviction
body:
## Purpose

When a prefix-cache hash has multiple physical copies, `BlockHashToBlockMap` promotes its value to a dictionary. Eviction currently retains that dictionary even when only one copy remains. Subsequent lookups can repeatedly scan its deleted entries, and its allocation remains live.

Restore the existing direct `KVCacheBlock` representation when eviction leaves one copy. Extend the existing mapping test to cover re-insertion, an unknown block ID and final removal, and update the pool-eviction expectations. Block identity, reference counts, cache contents and KV-event behavior are preserved.

The state is reachable through repeated `prompt_logprobs` requests followed by cache pressure. The benefit applies when the surviving prefix is subsequently reused; ordinary cache hits need not encounter this state. Checked the actual diffs of #55092 and #48933, which change removal-event semantics/counts and retain singleton dictionaries, and #40459, which adds an optional Rust pool without fixing this Python mapping. This follows the compact-representation approach introduced in #24830.

## Test Plan

Current CPU validation uses Python sources at `fff03267dae61d03615225c2f48a06082d842e2d` plus this patch:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_priority_preemption_bug.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload -q --durations=10
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py
```

## Test Result

- **649 passed, 2 skipped**; the two skips are the CUDA/ROCm-only simple-offload worker/integration modules on CPU. All applicable pre-commit checks passed. The compact-representation assertion was first shown to fail on the original implementation.
- CPU environment: AMD Ryzen 7 9700X, WSL Ubuntu, Python 3.12.3, torch 2.13.0+cpu. CPU extensions are from nightly `29468dde8`, not an exact current-main binary build.
- Prior GPU validation used base `a4eb3f25` with its exact CUDA wheel and the same production patch: RTX 4090, Qwen3-0.6B revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, FP16, seed 0, V1/MRV2, eager, single GPU. Four baseline–patch–patch–baseline runs passed. All 211 completed requests per run had identical generated tokens, generated-token logprobs and cache-hit counts. Active-request reset/recomputation and cancellation checks passed; all non-null blocks were released. The model workload reached 16 copies → one and released 5,056 bytes of inner dictionaries for its eight target hashes. This GPU validation has not been rerun on the newer base.

Earlier real-`KVCacheManager` CPU lookup measurements at `a4eb3f25`, for a 4,096-token prefix after duplicate eviction (1,000 queries × 7 repeats, median):

| Original copies → one | Baseline / patch, µs | Inner dictionary storage, baseline / patch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 → 1 control | 84.71 / 85.38 | 0 / 0 bytes |
| 2 → 1 | 102.69 / 83.61 | 57,344 / 0 bytes |
| 32 → 1 | 106.25 / 84.19 | 299,008 / 0 bytes |
| 128 → 1 | 122.26 / 85.49 | 1,200,128 / 0 bytes |

The 128-copy case is a constructed CPU workload, not the GPU workload. These are dictionary allocation sizes, not process RSS or GPU memory savings.

A further CPU comparison on the current base included duplicate creation, pressure eviction and subsequent hot-request query/allocation/free costs in one timed phase. With two copies → one, followed by 8 or 32 normal requests, wall-time medians were 1.844 → 1.489 ms and 5.352 → 4.805 ms respectively. This used a 4,096-token prefix, one CPU, enabled GC, two warmups and 30 alternating repetitions; manager/request construction and model execution were excluded.

There is a tradeoff: continuously cycling one ↔ two copies **without prefix reuse** reallocates dictionaries. The isolated insert/pop pair took 0.369 versus 0.279 µs. In a separate real-manager repeated-scoring workload, the 4,096-token query-entry/allocation/free cycle measured 303.70 versus 276.68 µs, with substantial sample variation. These costs remain relevant; the optimization is workload-dependent.

Production prevalence, long-running RSS/GC behavior and a statistically significant serving-throughput improvement have not been established. Multi-GPU, quantization and speculative decoding were not model-tested. Prefix-query savings must not be multiplied by generated-token count; admission retries/recomputation can add queries, but their real frequency was not measured.

<details>
<summary>CPU lifecycle/lookup reproducer (run on the base and patched checkout)</summary>

Save the following as a temporary script and run it using the checkout's `.venv/bin/python` with the checkout on `PYTHONPATH`. It uses normal cache-manager APIs and performs no model execution.

```python
"""CPU cache-manager lifecycle and timing; no simulated GPU/model result."""
import json
import platform
import statistics
import sys
import timeit

import torch
import vllm.v1.core.block_pool as block_pool_module

from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams
from vllm.utils.hashing import sha256
from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_manager import KVCacheManager
from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import get_request_block_hasher, init_none_hash
from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import FullAttentionSpec, KVCacheConfig, KVCacheGroupSpec
from vllm.v1.request import Request


def request(name, tokens, scoring=False):
    return Request(request_id=name, prompt_token_ids=tokens,
                   sampling_params=SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, prompt_logprobs=1 if scoring else None),
                   pooling_params=None, block_hasher=get_request_block_hasher(16, sha256))


def run(copies, num_blocks):
    num_tokens = num_blocks * 16
    tokens = list(range(num_tokens))
    manager = KVCacheManager(
        KVCacheConfig(num_blocks=copies * num_blocks + 1, kv_cache_tensors=[],
                      kv_cache_groups=[KVCacheGroupSpec(["layer"], FullAttentionSpec(
                          block_size=16, num_kv_heads=1, head_size=64, dtype=torch.float16))]),
        max_model_len=num_tokens + 16, scheduler_block_size=16, hash_block_size=16,
        enable_caching=True,
    )
    # Prompt logprobs require recomputation, so distinct physical copies of
    # identical prefixes accumulate even for sequential scoring requests.
    for i in range(copies):
        req = request(str(i), tokens, scoring=True)
        computed, hit_tokens, _ = manager.get_computed_blocks(req)
        assert hit_tokens == 0
        allocated = manager.allocate_slots(req, num_tokens, hit_tokens, computed)
        assert allocated is not None
        manager.free(req)
    # An unrelated request consumes older copies under ordinary cache pressure.
    evicted = manager.block_pool.get_new_blocks((copies - 1) * num_blocks)
    probe = request("probe", tokens)
    computed, hit_tokens, _ = manager.get_computed_blocks(probe)
    assert hit_tokens == num_tokens - 16
    assert len(computed.blocks[0]) == num_blocks - 1
    assert all(b.ref_cnt == 0 for b in computed.blocks[0])
    values = manager.block_pool.cached_block_hash_to_block._cache.values()
    dict_bytes = sum(sys.getsizeof(v) for v in values if isinstance(v, dict))
    lookup = lambda: manager.get_computed_blocks(probe)
    for _ in range(50):
        lookup()
    samples = timeit.repeat(lookup, number=1000, repeat=7)
    # Cache hits remain usable, and releasing requests restores the pool.
    assert manager.allocate_slots(probe, 16, hit_tokens, computed) is not None
    manager.free(probe)
    manager.block_pool.free_blocks(evicted)
    assert manager.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks() == copies * num_blocks
    return dict(copies=copies, prefix_tokens=num_tokens, cached_tokens=hit_tokens,
                retained_dict_bytes=dict_bytes,
                lookup_us_median=statistics.median(samples)*1000,
                lookup_us_samples=[s*1000 for s in samples])


init_none_hash(sha256)
print(json.dumps({"python": sys.version, "platform": platform.platform(),
                  "source": block_pool_module.__file__,
                  "torch": torch.__version__, "warmup": 50, "iterations": 1000,
                  "repeats": 7, "records": [run(c, b) for b in (16, 256) for c in (1, 2, 32, 128)]}, indent=2))
```

</details>

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation and validation.

title: [Bugfix][V1] Restore hybrid GDN prefix-cache hits under MTP spec decoding
body:
## Purpose

On **Qwen3.5-122B-A10B** with MTP speculative decoding, a replay of a cached prompt never reaches the depth the prefix cache could give it, and prompts whose length is a multiple of the hash unit get **no hit at all**. Measured live before this change, with a 1072-token GDN page and `--prefix-match-unit 67`:

| prompt | cached tokens on replay | ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| 1072 | **0** | 938 |
| 2000 | **0** | 1876 |
| 2144 | **0** | 2010 |
| 3000 | 1072 | 2881 |
| 3500 | 2144 | 3417 |

### Root cause

Three rules compose badly. A lookup caps at `prompt_len - 1`, because the last token must be recomputed for logits. The MTP/EAGLE drafter then rewinds the hit one hash unit (67) further. But the producer publishes the GDN state at the prompt's own tail boundary, `prompt_len // 67 * 67`, which is at or above the cap — so the recurrent group cannot resume where the rewind lands, and the coordinator intersects the two groups down to the previous full page (or to zero).

The same cap breaks the full-attention side whenever `prompt_len` is a multiple of 67 — and every page multiple is, since `1072 = 16 × 67`. Its partial-tail entry is registered at `prompt_len // 67 * 67 == prompt_len`, which the `- 1` cap excludes, so full attention itself matches nothing below the page boundary and the hybrid hit collapses to 0. That is the `1072 → 0`, `2144 → 0` row above.

### Fix

Write-side only, all of it gated on MTP/EAGLE plus fine-grained hashing being active:

- `mamba_state_cache_position(num_tokens, block_size, hash_block_size)` in `kv_cache_utils.py`: `unit = min(hash_block_size, block_size)`, returns `(num_tokens - 1 - unit) // unit * unit` — the position a replay actually lands on.
- `Scheduler._mamba_block_aligned_split` stops a prefill chunk there, so that state exists to be published. It is an **extra** stop; the existing block-aligned stops stay. Replacing them lets intermediate chunks end off-grid and re-triggers the state poisoning of #43559 (14 tests in `test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py` fail that way).
- `MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block` publishes the GDN state there instead of at the prompt tail.
- `FullAttentionManager._cache_partial_tail_block` additionally publishes `(prompt_len - 1) // 67 * 67`, the deepest tail a replay can reach. The unshifted tail is kept, because requests that *extend* this prompt have a higher cap and can still match it.
- `MambaManager` reports a block-aligned prompt end as unreachable through a new `reachable_block_mask()` argument, so that state is not cached in any retention mode: no lookup can land at or past a prompt's own end, and the rewound state below it is where consumers land. Guarded on the latter being cached. The rewound position is read from one `MambaManager` helper rather than recomputed per caller, and keys off whether the engine runs a drafter rather than the per-group `use_eagle` bit, which is only set on groups that take the drop.

Without the last item the page multiples stay at 0 no matter where the GDN state sits: the producer had the state at 938 / 2010 / 3082, but full attention offered nothing below 1072 / 2144 / 3216 for the intersection to meet.

## Test Plan

```bash
# unit
pytest tests/v1/core -q

# e2e: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, 4x B200, MTP 3 tokens, sub-page hashing
vllm serve $QWEN35_122B --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-chunked-prefill \
    --spec-method mtp --spec-tokens 3 --prefix-match-unit 67 --port 8110
```

Hit depth is read from the `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` delta of a replay: a token-id prompt of an exact length is sent three times and the second and third deltas are the cached length. 132 lengths from 1 to 15k were swept — every page multiple with its `+1`, `+unit-1`, `+unit`, `+unit+1` neighbours, plus scattered lengths. Two further passes cover the configurations where the patch must do nothing, and quality was checked on top of real hits.

## Test Result

(1) Hit Length Boundary

All 132 lengths land exactly on the replay ceiling `(P - 1 - 67) // 67 * 67`. Page-boundary neighbourhoods, where the old code either missed entirely or fell back a full page:

| prompt | position | before | after | replay ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1072 | k*1072 | 0 | 938 | 938 |
| 1073 | k*1072 + 1 | 0 | 1005 | 1005 |
| 1138 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 0 | 1005 | 1005 |
| 1139 | k*1072 + unit | 0 | 1005 | 1005 |
| 1140 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 0 | 1072 | 1072 |
| 2144 | k*1072 | 0 | 2010 | 2010 |
| 2145 | k*1072 + 1 | 1072 | 2077 | 2077 |
| 2210 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 1072 | 2077 | 2077 |
| 2211 | k*1072 + unit | 1072 | 2077 | 2077 |
| 2212 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 1072 | 2144 | 2144 |
| 3216 | k*1072 | 0 | 3082 | 3082 |
| 3217 | k*1072 + 1 | 2144 | 3149 | 3149 |
| 3282 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 2144 | 3149 | 3149 |
| 3283 | k*1072 + unit | 2144 | 3149 | 3149 |
| 3284 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 2144 | 3216 | 3216 |
| 5360 | k*1072 | 0 | 5226 | 5226 |
| 5361 | k*1072 + 1 | 4288 | 5293 | 5293 |
| 5426 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 4288 | 5293 | 5293 |
| 5427 | k*1072 + unit | 4288 | 5293 | 5293 |
| 5428 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 4288 | 5360 | 5360 |
| 10720 | k*1072 | 7504 | 10586 | 10586 |
| 10721 | k*1072 + 1 | 9648 | 10653 | 10653 |
| 10786 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 9648 | 10653 | 10653 |
| 10787 | k*1072 + unit | 9648 | 10653 | 10653 |
| 10788 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 9648 | 10720 | 10720 |

Other lengths:

| prompt | before | after | ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|
| 500 | 0 | 402 | 402 |
| 999 | 0 | 871 | 871 |
| 2000 | 0 | 1876 | 1876 |
| 3000 | 1072 | 2881 | 2881 |
| 3500 | 2144 | 3417 | 3417 |
| 5000 | 3216 | 4891 | 4891 |
| 7777 | 6432 | 7705 | 7705 |
| 12345 | 10720 | 12261 | 12261 |
| 14999 | 12864 | 14874 | 14874 |

`before` comes from a CPU replica driving the real splitter and the real managers on the base commit; on the patched build that replica reproduces the end-to-end numbers length by length, so the two columns are comparable.

Configurations where the patch must be inert: re-running the same 132 lengths without `--prefix-match-unit` (both groups sit at 1072, so `hash_block_size == block_size` and sub-page hashing is off) gives `((P - 1) // 1072) * 1072 - 1072` on every length, and the CPU replica shows this build and the base commit agreeing on all 132. `mamba_cache_mode=all` cannot be exercised on this model — it is not in `SupportsMambaPrefixCaching`, so vLLM falls back to `align`.

Unit tests: `tests/v1/core` 492 passed. The one failure and two errors are GPU-exclusive e2e cases (`Free memory on device cuda:0 ... less than desired`) blocked by the serving process on the same box, and reproduce without this change. `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py` is updated so the replay landing position counts as a legal intermediate chunk end alongside the partial-tail boundary.

(2) Model Quality Test

GPQA Diamond Score for Qwen/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B : 85.9% (match official score 86.6%)

GSM8K 5-shot, 300 questions: 0.890 / 0.853 with 0.0% / 1.3% invalid on this build, against 0.847 / 0.830 with 1.7% / 2.7% invalid on the base commit. Run-to-run spread is larger than the gap, so this is "no regression", not an accuracy claim.

Output quality on top of a real hit: an English passage of 700 / 1500 / 2400 / 3500 words, sent cold and then replayed (hits of 670 / 1608 / 2613 / 3819 tokens), returns byte-identical text at `temperature=0` in all four, twice over — no truncation, no repetition, no garbling.

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

## Reproduce Low KVCache Hit Length with Qwen3.5

(1) Launch

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B \
    --served-model-name Qwen3.5-122B-A10B \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --enable-chunked-prefill \
    --spec-method mtp \
    --spec-tokens 3 \
    --prefix-match-unit 67 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8110
```

(2) Send the same prompt twice

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json, random, re, urllib.request

N = 2144
BASE = "http://localhost:8110"

def hits_total():
    metrics = urllib.request.urlopen(f"{BASE}/metrics").read().decode()
    return float(
        re.search(r"^vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total\{[^}]*\} (\S+)", metrics, re.M).group(1)
    )

random.seed(N)
body = json.dumps({
    "model": "Qwen3.5-122B-A10B",
    "prompt": [random.randint(1000, 100000) for _ in range(N)],
    "max_tokens": 1,
    "temperature": 0,
}).encode()

for attempt in (1, 2):
    before = hits_total()
    urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(
        f"{BASE}/v1/completions", body, {"Content-Type": "application/json"}))
    print(attempt, int(hits_total() - before))
EOF
```

(3) Check the second request's cache length

Before the fix it is 0, after the fix it is 2010.

title: [Bugfix] Fix AOT caching for decorated forward methods
body:
## Purpose

The Transformers backend can fail to save its AOT artifact when a model's
`forward` is wrapped by decorators. The artifact may reference a function from
the `__wrapped__` chain which is no longer importable by identity, so standard
pickle fails with errors such as:

```text
Can't pickle <function Qwen3Model.forward ...>: it's not the same object as
transformers.models.qwen3.modeling_qwen3.Qwen3Model.forward
```

This makes every warm start compile again even when the rest of the compile
cache is warm.

This PR uses PyTorch's `external_data` support to save and restore the
non-canonical functions in a decorated `forward` chain. The external keys
include a deterministic fingerprint of the whole chain, including defaults,
keyword defaults, and supported immutable closure state, so an artifact is not
reused when decorator configuration changes.

The mapping is all-or-nothing and unsupported state falls back to the existing
save/load behavior. The existing PyTorch 2.10 call path is unchanged;
`external_data` is only passed on PyTorch 2.11+.

This addresses the AOT warm-start cache failure identified in #50128. It does
not claim to eliminate or fully explain the remaining Transformers-backend
startup gap tracked by that issue.

## Test Plan

- Added unit coverage for decorated-forward resolution, deterministic chain
  fingerprints, unsupported state, canonical inner functions, inherited
  forwards, invalid/cyclic chains, and PyTorch 2.10 API compatibility.
- Added real AOT compile/save tests for the unsupported-state non-fatal path.
- Added cross-process tests for cold save + forced warm load and for fingerprint
  mismatch in normal and forced-load modes.
- Ran the complete AOT compile test file with the configuration that executes
  the functorch test instead of conditionally skipping it:

```bash
VLLM_USE_MEGA_AOT_ARTIFACT=0 pytest -q tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py
ruff check vllm/compilation/decorators.py tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py
ruff format --check vllm/compilation/decorators.py tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py
git diff --check
```

- Ran fresh-process cold + three warm-start checks on an NVIDIA L20 with
  PyTorch 2.13.0+cu129 and Transformers 5.15.0. Warm runs used
  `VLLM_FORCE_AOT_LOAD=1` so a failed load could not silently recompile.

## Test Result

```text
71 passed, 16 warnings in 178.91s
ruff check: passed
ruff format --check: passed
git diff --check: passed
```

The warnings are existing dependency deprecations from PyTorch JIT (14) and
CUDA Python (2).

Fresh-process results:

| Model | Cold init | Warm init median | Warm compile median | Improvement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 38.391 → 38.704 s | 25.737 → 17.632 s | 8.28 → 0.13 s | 31.5% |
| TinyLlama-1.1B | 29.360 → 29.056 s | 19.739 → 13.837 s | 5.80 → 0.12 s | 29.9% |
| Qwen3-14B | 50.103 → 50.033 s | 36.520 → 24.792 s | 11.36 → 0.13 s | 32.1% |

Values are `before → after`. All after-fix forced warm runs loaded the AOT
artifact with `compiles=0, loaded=1`.

<details>
<summary>Raw runs and AOT counters</summary>

| Model | Revision | Warm init runs | Warm compile runs | Cold counters | Warm counters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | Before | 25.755 / 25.737 / 25.571 s | 8.28 / 8.40 / 8.26 s | `1/0/0` | `1/0/0` |
| Qwen3-0.6B | After | 17.403 / 17.632 / 17.757 s | 0.13 / 0.12 / 0.13 s | `1/1/0` | `0/0/1` |
| TinyLlama-1.1B | Before | 19.807 / 19.739 / 19.723 s | 5.80 / 5.82 / 5.77 s | `1/0/0` | `1/0/0` |
| TinyLlama-1.1B | After | 13.962 / 13.800 / 13.837 s | 0.12 / 0.12 / 0.12 s | `1/1/0` | `0/0/1` |
| Qwen3-14B | Before | 36.307 / 36.520 / 36.533 s | 11.36 / 11.41 / 11.33 s | `1/0/0` | `1/0/0` |
| Qwen3-14B | After | 25.005 / 24.754 / 24.792 s | 0.13 / 0.14 / 0.13 s | `1/1/0` | `0/0/1` |

Counters are `compiled/saved/loaded`. Before the fix, every warm process
compiled again because artifact saving failed. After the fix, every forced
warm process loaded the artifact without compiling.

</details>

For every model, cold and warm runs produced identical token IDs.

## AI Assistance

Developed with assistance from OpenAI Codex. I reviewed all changes and
verified the reported tests and benchmarks.

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Fall back for high-rank MoE LoRA
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55158.

`LoRAConfig` accepts `max_lora_rank` values above 128, but the non-fully-sharded
MoE LoRA dispatch unconditionally selected the one-shot Triton kernel, whose
rank dimension is limited to 128. This caused engine initialization to fail
during CUDA graph warm-up even when the loaded adapter's actual rank was only
4, because the MoE LoRA buffers are padded to the configured maximum rank.

This change:

- keeps ranks up to 128 on the existing one-shot fast path;
- routes larger ranks to the existing two-kernel shrink/expand path;
- lets that fallback preserve the existing `add_inputs=False` contract used by
  dual-stream and other MoE LoRA callers; and
- retains the one-shot assertion as a defensive kernel-local guard.

Rank tiling could extend the one-shot kernel in the future, but the existing
fallback is a smaller correctness-first fix and avoids changing the kernel's
register-pressure/performance characteristics.

## Duplicate check

No exact open issue or fix PR was found after searching for the assertion text,
function name, `max_lora_rank=256`, and MoE LoRA rank fallback. PR #42290's
review did identify both the missing rank fallback and the dual-stream risk,
but those comments were not addressed before merge and current main still has
the mismatch. Related issues and PRs are listed in #55158.

## Test Plan

```bash
uvx --from ruff==0.15.12 ruff format --check \
  vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py \
  tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py

uvx --from ruff==0.15.12 ruff check \
  vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py \
  tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py

uv run --no-sync pytest -q \
  tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py \
  -k large_rank_fallback
```

The targeted numerical test compares the Triton result with a PyTorch
reference across:

- rank 128 (one-shot boundary) and 256 (fallback);
- `add_inputs=True` and `False`; and
- one and two LoRA slices, covering both TMA descriptor layouts on supported
  GPUs.

An end-to-end check starts the public Nemotron MoE model from #55158 with
`--max-lora-rank 256` and verifies that CUDA graph warm-up completes and a LoRA
request returns HTTP 200.

## Test Result

- Ruff format: passed.
- Ruff lint: passed.
- Python syntax and custom-op real/fake signature checks: passed.
- Targeted numerical test on an NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB: passed
  (`8 passed, 417 deselected`). This covers rank 128/256,
  `add_inputs=True/False`, and one/two LoRA slices.
- End-to-end test on 2x NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB with TP=2: passed. At commit
  `29a6af589`, the public Nemotron MoE model and rank-4 dummy adapter started
  with `--max-lora-rank 256`; both PIECEWISE and FULL CUDA graph capture
  completed, `/health` returned HTTP 200, and a request to the `dummy` LoRA
  model returned HTTP 200.

GPU test environment: PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA runtime 13.0, compute
capability 8.0.

## AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex assisted with code-path analysis, drafting the patch and tests,
and duplicate-work research. The human submitter reviewed every changed line,
validated the design, and verified the reported GPU test results.

title: [ROCm] Enable fused QK-norm+RoPE+gate Triton kernel for Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5
body:
## Purpose

`Qwen3NextAttention` fuses the gated QKV split + QK-RMSNorm + (partial) NeoX RoPE + gate copy into a single Triton kernel (`fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate`, added in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44176). The kernel is pure Triton and backend-agnostic, but it is gated behind `current_platform.is_cuda()`, so ROCm falls back to the slow multi-op eager path, even though the kernel runs correctly and fast on AMD GPUs.

This PR relaxes that one-line guard to `is_cuda_alike()` so ROCm gets the same fusion. It affects the whole `Qwen3NextAttention` family: Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, Qwen3.5-MoE

Measured on MI325X (gfx942), bf16, against the model's real eager branch
(`GemmaRMSNorm` + the `rotary_emb` custom op), 300 timed iters after 50 warmup:

| 64 | 281.7 | 33.9 | 8.32× |
| 512 | 277.4 | 33.7 | 8.22× |

Note: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47719 is an opt-in AITER path that additionally fuses the KV-cache write.

## Test Plan

## Test Result

### Benchmarks

Measured on MI325X (gfx942), Qwen3.5-4B with `--language-model-only` (bf16). Fused path confirmed active on all 8 full-attention layers vs. off.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Fix race on AITER MLA FP8 prefill scheduling metadata under async scheduling
body:
Fixes #58886

## Purpose

**Type:** bugfix. **Backend:** `ROCM_AITER_MLA`, FP8 KV cache, gfx950 (FP8 ASM prefill path).
**Affected:** MLA models served with async scheduling on this path. Reproduced with Kimi-K3
(TP8, MI355X).

`AiterMLAMetadataBuilder._build_fp8_prefill_ps_metadata` passes one set of persistent device
buffers to `aiter.get_ps_metadata_v1`. That function plans on the host and writes the plan
back with blocking `hipMemcpy`, which is not ordered on the current stream. With async
scheduling, step N+1's metadata is built while step N's prefill kernels
(`mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd` and `mla_reduce_v1`, one launch per layer) are still queued, so
step N can run with step N+1's work/reduce maps. The existing `.item()` sync on
`reduce_indptr[-1]` happens after the rewrite, so it does not prevent this.

Symptom: `Memory access fault by GPU ... Write access to a read-only page` during serving, at
a deterministic point for a given request stream. When the stale indices stay in bounds, the
prefill attention output is silently wrong instead.

This PR plans into pinned host buffers (two slots) and copies them to the device with
`copy_(non_blocking=True)` on the current stream, so the update is ordered after previously
launched kernels. A slot is reused only after its previous copy completes (CUDA event). As a
side effect, `num_partial_tiles` is read from the host plan, which removes a GPU sync per
prefill step. No AITER change is needed. The AITER-side hazard (stream-less copies in the host
planner) is tracked in [ROCm/aiter#5879](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/5879).

## Test Plan

Kimi-K3 TP8 on MI355X, ROCm 10 nightly (`29468dde`), FP8 KV cache,
`max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, `max_num_seqs=256`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, async scheduling.

1. Crash: `sglang.bench_serving`, random 8k/1k, on request streams that fault without the fix,
   before vs after.
2. Performance: same benchmark at concurrency 4 and 32, before vs after.
3. Accuracy: `niah_single_2` (real weights) at 4k (concurrency 4/32/64) and at 64k/128k
   (concurrency 32), before vs after.
4. Plan equivalence: `get_ps_metadata_v1` with pinned host outputs produces byte-identical
   plans to device outputs (5 batch shapes, including the crash batch; checked once on MI355X).

## Test Result

**Crash.** Every stream that faults without the fix completes with it:

| Request stream (8k/1k) | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| concurrency 32, 1024 prompts | fault at request 111 (also with `--enforce-eager`) | 1024/1024 |
| concurrency 32, 2048 prompts | fault at request 79 | 2048/2048 |
| concurrency 64, 1024 prompts | fault at request 61 | 1024/1024 |
| concurrency 32, 1024 prompts, other seed | fault at request 117 | 1024/1024 |

Isolating the cause (before, no fix): the fault disappears with the FP8 ASM prefill path
disabled, with `--no-async-scheduling`, or with a `torch.cuda.synchronize()` just before
`get_ps_metadata_v1`.

**Not Kimi-K3 specific: DeepSeek-V3.** `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3` on the same ROCm 10 nightly,
TP8 (128 heads, 16 per rank, so no head padding), dummy weights, same server flags (FP8 KV
cache, async scheduling, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, `max_num_seqs=256`) without the
Kimi-K3-specific parser options, same 8k/1k benchmark at concurrency 32, 1024 prompts:

| Request stream | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| seed 4 | fault at request 111 | 1024/1024 |
| seed 5 | fault at request 117 | not run |

The engine dump at the fault shows the same crash batch as with Kimi-K3: one new 8175-token
prefill with 32 running requests.

**Performance.** No change:

| 8k/1k | Output tok/s (before / after) | Median ITL (before / after) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| concurrency 4 | 236.05 / 236.05 | 15.49 / 15.50 ms |
| concurrency 32 | 1083.0 / 1082.6 | 18.14 / 18.14 ms |

**Accuracy.** No regression (single runs):

| `niah_single_2` | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4k, concurrency 4 / 32 / 64 | 0.974 / 0.954 / 0.970 | 0.974 / 0.978 / 0.984 |
| 64k, concurrency 32 | 0.922 | 0.928 |
| 128k, concurrency 32 | 0.888 | 0.888 |

**Reproducing on ROCm 7.2.** The bug is not ROCm 10 specific. Use the ROCm 7.2 image of the
same nightly (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-29468dde…`), the same `vllm serve` and benchmark
commands as above, and add one HIP runtime variable to the server:

| ROCm 7.2 server env | Benchmark stream | Without this PR | With this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| none (defaults) | any above | no crash | no crash |
| `DEBUG_HIP_DYNAMIC_QUEUES=1` | 1024 prompts, `--seed 5` | crash at request 117 (x3, on 2 machines) | 1024/1024 |
| `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=16` | 1024 prompts, `--seed 4` | crash at request 111 (x2, on 2 machines) | 1024/1024 |

The crash is `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`, on the same kind of
batch as on ROCm 10: one new ~8.1k-token prefill plus ~30 decodes.

**Why these variables expose it.** `get_ps_metadata_v1`'s first copy is tiny (1 KiB), so HIP
runs it as a small copy kernel on the default stream's hardware queue. Hardware queues run in
order, and with more streams than queues (default 4) several streams share one. With default
settings, ROCm 7.2 happens to put vLLM's prefill stream on the same queue as the default
stream. The plan copy then waits behind the running prefill, which hides the race. Both
variables change how streams are assigned to hardware queues, so the copy stops waiting and
lands while the prefill is still reading the plan, as it always does on ROCm 10. So ROCm 7.2
is protected by an accident of queue assignment, not by any ordering guarantee. This PR orders
the copy explicitly on every version.

With this PR, the ROCm 7.2 build with default settings also completes 1024/1024 (8k/1k,
concurrency 32), so the change does not regress 7.2. A standalone single-GPU reproducer is
attached to #58886.

Not related to #58814 (DSpark startup fault): that fault reproduces with this PR applied and is
fixed by #58814 alone.

This description and the experiments behind it were produced with help from a Cursor agent.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] Re-enable the fused combine_topk_swa_indices on gfx950
body:
## Purpose

`combine_topk_swa_indices` runs V4.1's mixed-prefill path through ordinary Torch indexing. The fused Triton kernel inherited from V4 is still in the file but unused, after it misbehaved on the warmup batch. This puts prefill back on the kernel: one launch in place of the ninety elementwise and indexing ops the Torch path builds.

## What changes

The kernel needs one thing the Torch path already did — clamp both lengths at zero:

```python
topk_len = tl.maximum(tl.minimum((pos + 1) // COMPRESS_RATIO, TOP_K), 0)
swa_len = tl.maximum(tl.minimum(pos + 1, WINDOW_SIZE), 0)
```

`combined_lens` is stored unmasked, so a length derived from a negative `pos` reaches the output and the sparse prefill reads it. That is the whole kernel diff; everything else here is the wrapper calling the kernel instead of building the Torch path, plus tests.

The layers with `compress_ratio == 0` reach it with `topk == 0`, so `TOP_K` is zero there and `COMPRESS_RATIO` takes a `max(., 1)` to keep the constexpr off a `// 0` at JIT time. The Torch path divided by that zero and leaned on the clamp to discard the result.

## Tests

`tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py` compares the kernel against the Torch path it replaces, copied over unchanged so the reference cannot drift toward the kernel, across the inputs that path accepts: `seq_len` below `query_len`, `compress_ratio == 0`, and windows 64/128/256.

```bash
pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py
```

```
gfx950 (MI355X)   73 passed,  0 skipped, 0 failed
gfx942 (MI300X)   61 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed
```

61 + 12 matches the 73 collected on gfx950; the skips are the sparse decode partials that stay gfx950-only. The tests take a marker that matches what the kernel needs, so they run wherever the kernel runs rather than on gfx950 alone.

## Measurements

MI355X, TP4, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-cd10ed6f`. Arm A is the Torch path as shipped, arm B is this branch, nothing else differs. Each arm is a fresh server, the first repetition is discarded as process warm-up, and five are recorded.

```bash
# server, one per arm
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
vllm serve DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --port 8200 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --moe-backend aiter \
  --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-seqs 16 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'

# one repetition; discard the first, record seeds 21..25
vllm bench serve --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8200 \
  --model DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts 4 --max-concurrency 1 --seed $SEED \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,e2el --metric-percentiles 90,99
```

**8192 in / 1024 out**, prefix caching off:

| metric, conc. 1 (n=5/arm) | A (Torch) | B (kernel) | delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TTFT median (ms) | 301.0 ± 2.4 | 261.9 ± 1.9 | **−13.0 %** |
| E2E median (ms) | 9785.4 ± 5.6 | 9767.2 ± 4.8 | −0.2 % |
| total token throughput (tok/s) | 899 ± 95 | 901 ± 96 | +0.2 % (overlaps) |

TTFT has non-overlapping ranges: A [298.3, 304.8] against B [259.6, 264.4].

The TTFT saving is real and repeatable; at a thousand output tokens it amortizes away end to end, which is the honest bound on what this buys.

**Why it is faster.** Profiling `combine_topk_swa_indices` alone, four requests,
identical inputs on both paths, counting device kernels under `torch.profiler` with `ProfilerActivity.CUDA` after three warm-up calls:

| num_tokens | Torch launches | kernel launches | device time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2048 | 90 | 2 | 286 us → 8 us |
| 8192 | 90 | 2 | 399 us → 16 us |
| 16384 | 90 | 2 | 543 us → 27 us |

The Torch launch count does not move with the token count — it is a fixed sequence of ops — which is why it shows up as fixed cost in TTFT.

**On a real workload.** An agentic multi-turn trace replay (long inputs, high
prefix reuse), same two arms, one 900 s run each — one run per arm, so this is corroboration rather than the measurement:

| | requests | TTFT median (ms) | E2E median (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| conc. 1, ISL p50 129k / OSL p50 345 | 103 | 417.6 → 357.3 (−14.4 %) | 2304.0 → 2208.1 (−4.2 %) |
| conc. 8, ISL p50 85k / OSL p50 257 | 285 | 285.2 → 233.6 (−18.1 %) | 1780.8 → 1585.1 (−11.0 %) |

Those are the conditions this kernel is for: long inputs, short outputs, and a prefix cache that makes the fixed launch cost a large share of what is left.

GSM8K, 1319 questions, 8-shot: 0.912.

title: fix(parser): keep fenced code examples out of qwen3 tool calls
body:
keep fenced code examples out of qwen3 tool calls

Fixes #57541

## what happens

qwen3 models document the tool call format inside markdown fences. the parser has no fence state at all, so it reads the example XML as a real call header and emits a phantom bash tool call while swallowing most of the answer text

the reporter measured it at chunk sizes 1, 7 and 10000, all agree. on v0.29.0 and on the #56661 backport the content comes back as 59 of 149 chars and the parser reports a tool call named Bash that the model never made. i reproduced it verbatim on master at 4c6c1a4 with their CPU-only snippet, same output, no gpu needed

## the fix

a FENCE terminal on the qwen3 config plus a FENCED engine state. a fenced span runs from the first ``` to the next ``` and everything in between is emitted as plain text, streaming and non streaming

- (CONTENT, FENCE) enters FENCED and re-emits the fence itself as text
- (FENCED, FENCE) returns to CONTENT the same way
- FENCED has no tool transitions, so XML inside it can never promote
- an unterminated fence settles back to CONTENT in finish(), it never turns into a call

```xml
<tool_call>
<function=Bash>
<parameter=command>ls -la</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
```

stays exactly the text you see there. a real call right after a fenced example still parses, and backticks inside a parameter value never open a fence (TOOL_ARGS content is untouched)

## why this is not duplicating an existing PR

- search for PRs referencing #57541: 0 hits
- #56658 and #56661 fix a different case, a bare <tool_call> in prose with no fence. the reporter measured their case still broken with #56661 applied
- no open PR touches fenced example handling (157 open qwen3 and parser PRs scanned by title and by fence keyword searches)

## why engine/ changed

the vllm/parser AGENTS.md says keep model fixes in the model file and change engine/ only when the behavior is wrong for every parser. the fence semantics live in the shared state machine: FENCED is a new ParserState with a default content_events row, and finish() normalizes it like the other non-final states. without the state in engine/, the FENCE transitions cannot exist in a declarative config

## tests

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3_fenced_examples.py -q
# 8 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/ tests/parser/test_parse.py tests/parser/test_streaming.py tests/parser/test_include_reasoning.py tests/parser/test_harmony.py -q
# 4447 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/ -q -k qwen
# 88 passed, 2 skipped
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/reasoning/ -q
# 432 passed
.venv/bin/ruff check <changed files>      # clean
.venv/bin/ruff format --check <changed files>   # clean
.venv/bin/mypy <changed source files> --ignore-missing-imports   # Success
```

the new tests cover the reported case non streaming and streaming at chunk sizes 1 and 7, full text equality, the unfenced promotion staying intact, a real call after a fenced example, backticks inside a parameter value, and a fenced example right after </think>

no model evaluation was run. the change is parser level, the serving-level effect is that text the model meant as documentation stays in content instead of becoming a tool call. the reporter's serving validation showed the same defect through the full serving stack

## AI assistance

i used an AI agent to build this change, i reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above

title: [ROCm][Perf] Default DeepSeek V4.1 MoE to a4w4 (FP4 activations) on AITER
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek V4.1's MXFP4 MoE runs AITER's a4w4 (FP4-activation) kernel by
default as of the first commit on this PR. That commit forced a4w4 via
AITER's `_q_dtype_a` override but kept vLLM's existing `GateMode.INTERLEAVE`
weight shuffle. AITER's INTERLEAVE stage-1 GEMM has no tuned FlyDSL config
for fp4x2 activations at this shape and silently falls back to a heuristic
kernel that produces degenerate output end-to-end — AITER's own
`op_tests/test_moe_2stage.py` cosine-similarity check (used to validate the
first commit) does not catch this, but real-model GSM8K does (near-chance
accuracy, garbled reasoning traces).

The second commit fixes that by switching a4w4 to ATOM's `GateMode.SEPARATED`
gate/up weight layout instead, which AITER validates for fp4x2 activations on
this checkpoint. It's a single `is_guinterleave=False` flag flip in AITER's own
`shuffle_weight`/`shuffle_scale` — no new shuffle function needed — gated on
the same `FusedMoEConfig.use_mxfp4_w4a4_dsv4` flag that already gates the
forced a4w4 activation dtype. a8w4 (default for every other MXFP4 model on
this code path) is untouched.

The third commit **scopes the auto-detection to DeepSeek V4.1 only**
(`deepseek_v41`/`deepseek_v41_text`). DeepSeek V4 shares the same MoE shape
and dispatch path but has not had the same GSM8K/AgentX validation yet — see
the separate untested/draft follow-up in #58869.

## Test Plan & Result

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py -v
pre-commit run --files vllm/envs.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/config.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py \
```

title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix M-RoPE offset double-count in Qwen3-Omni
body:
get_mrope_input_positions treated PlaceholderRange.offset as the index of the modality-start token (<|vision_start|>/<|audio_start|>), but the prompt replacement machinery only replaces the pad token, so offset points at the first pad token and the start token is already covered by the preceding text segment. The extra bos slot emitted per media item made the assembled positions one slot longer than the token span: prompts ending with a media item always hit the "Position ids length mismatch" RuntimeError (fatal to EngineCore), and prompts with trailing text got silently misaligned M-RoPE positions from the first pad token onward.

Drop the redundant bos slot and fix the st advancement in each media branch (image/audio/video/audio-in-video) so the emitted position count always equals seq_len. Add unit tests covering media-at-prompt-end for each modality and exact positions for media followed by text.



## Purpose

`Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerForConditionalGeneration.get_mrope_input_positions` misinterprets `PlaceholderRange.offset`: the prompt replacement machinery only replaces the pad token, so `offset` points at the first pad token and the modality-start token (`<|vision_start|>` / `<|audio_start|>`) is already covered by the preceding text segment. The function instead treats `offset` as the modality-start index and emits an extra bos slot per media item, making the assembled positions one slot longer than the token span:

- Prompts ending with a media item (e.g. custom/transcription-style chat templates) always hit `RuntimeError: Position ids length mismatch with input ids length`, which is fatal to EngineCore.
- Prompts with trailing text (stock chat template) don't crash, but every M-RoPE position from the first pad token onward is silently misaligned by one slot — a correctness bug on all multimodal requests.

This drops the redundant bos slot and fixes the `st` advancement in each media branch (image/audio/video/audio-in-video) so the emitted position count always equals `seq_len`. The audio-in-video value structure (shared bos/eos positions) is preserved, consistent with the Qwen2.5-Omni behavior in HF.

Follow-up to GHSA-328w-h674-qp56 (per maintainer feedback, the crash path requires an operator-chosen chat template; this PR fixes the offset handling itself).

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni_mrope.py -v
```

New unit tests use synthetic input_ids + `MultiModalFeatureSpec` (no GPU/weights needed):
- `test_mrope_positions_{image,audio,video,audio_in_video}_at_prompt_end`: prompt ending exactly at the modality-end token must yield `positions.shape == (3, seq_len)`.
- `test_mrope_positions_image_then_text`: media followed by text must produce the exact expected per-position values.

## Test Result

Before the fix: all 5 tests fail — the 4 media-at-prompt-end cases raise `RuntimeError: Position ids length mismatch` (the engine-death path), and the image-then-text case fails on misaligned position values.

After the fix: all 5 tests pass.

```
tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni_mrope.py::test_mrope_positions_image_at_prompt_end PASSED
tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni_mrope.py::test_mrope_positions_audio_at_prompt_end PASSED
tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni_mrope.py::test_mrope_positions_video_at_prompt_end PASSED
tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni_mrope.py::test_mrope_positions_audio_in_video_at_prompt_end PASSED
tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni_mrope.py::test_mrope_positions_image_then_text PASSED
```

title: [Fast Start] Add `/health` endpoint for the weight cache daemon
body:
## Purpose

Add an HTTP `/health` endpoint to the weight cache daemon parent process.

The endpoint reports `starting` while daemon ranks are loading, `ready` after all expected target and draft ranks are available, and `failed` if a daemon process exits. This allows external service management systems to distinguish daemon startup from readiness.

Stacked on #58370. Will rebase once #58370 is merged.

cc: @Isotr0py @liusy58

## Test Plan

Test `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py` with both target-only and target-plus-draft configurations.

Verify that the daemon reports the expected health state after all ranks are ready, and that IPC weight loading and generation complete successfully.

## Test Result

The tests confirm correct health reporting and successful IPC weight loading for both configurations.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Retry Mooncake bootstrap registration on timeout
body:
## Purpose

Worker registration created `httpx.AsyncClient()` with no explicit timeout, inheriting HTTPX's 5s default. The bootstrap server runs inside the global rank 0 prefiller process, which also registers the Mooncake host memory segment, so a large segment blocks responses past that default. Only `ConnectError` was retried, so the resulting `ReadTimeout` was re-raised, the sender listener exited before setting its ready event, and the unbounded `ready_event.wait()` hung startup. This adds a configurable timeout, retries `TimeoutException` with capped backoff, makes `/register` idempotent for identical payloads, and bounds the readiness wait so failures propagate. Now an identical repeat registration returns 200 instead of 400 and a same-rank registration at a different address still returns 400.

Fixes #55729.

## Repro

Configuration:

```
tensor-parallel-size=2
pipeline-parallel-size=4
MOONCAKE_GLOBAL_SEGMENT_SIZE=21474836480
```

On main:
```
T+5.37s   7 worker ranks log "Error registering ... with bootstrap server:" 
          with an empty message, since str(ReadTimeout) is empty
T+12.68s  rank 0 finishes registering its 20 GiB segment and returns 200 OK
T+60s+    43 consecutive "No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds" records
```

On this branch the seven ranks retry and register once rank 0 responds.

## Test Plan

```
pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py
pre-commit run -a
```

New tests cover a client that times out twice then succeeds, one that always times out and idempotent repost plus conflicting address. `test_register_worker_recovers_from_slow_bootstrap_server` runs a real uvicorn bootstrap server whose first `/register` response is delayed past the configured timeout so the client raises a `httpx.ReadTimeout` on the wire then retries and registers. It also exercises the idempotent path, since the server records the first request before the client gives up. Reverting the retry arm to `except httpx.ConnectError` makes this test fail confirming it catches the reported bug.

```
79 mooncake connector tests passed
pre-commit run -a passed
```

## AI Assistance

Claude Opus 5 assisted with drafting the change.

title: [Bugfix][Model Loader] Restore kernel state post model loading via `TensorizerLoader`.
body:
This PR targets issue https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55198 about the `TensorizerLoader`. Particularly, the current implementation of `TensorizerLoader` fails to run post-loading processing on the model weights, and also skips computing any state required for the kernel backends to execute the model. As mentioned in the issue, `TensorizerLoader` fails to call either of `process_weights_after_loading` and `finalize_layerwise_processing`, and also fails to return the model in `.eval()` mode.

The reproduction code mentioned in the issue is not very helpful; it only tracks the actual function calls by constructing the call graph. For a minimal reproduction of the issue, I've only focused on the following:

- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-FP8`
- Revision: `e5be08033360965ceca7b0ffd72d521a51331ce0`
- Quantization: block-scaled FP8
- Linear backend: Marlin

Here are my hardware/other specs:

- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050, 6144MiB VRAM
- Ubuntu 22.04
- vLLM checkout: `v0.28.0`

Note that the issue persists in two "paths": one is the raw checkpoint path, where the `TensorizerLoader` is used to load raw checkpoint weights, and is supposed to run post-processing + computing the state. The second path is the "native" vLLM path: here, post-processing is already run, and the loader just needs to compute the state required by the kernels. For this PR, the focus is only on the native vLLM path, since it is trickier.

## Reproduction

Here is the reproduction script that I used (with an actual model). It has two modes: `load` and `save`. Use the `save` mode first to load raw weights and save the model via the tensorizer. Then, the `load` move exposes the error:

```python
"""
    .venv/bin/python issue-55198-lab/reproduce_native_fp8.py save
    .venv/bin/python issue-55198-lab/reproduce_native_fp8.py load

Before native Tensorizer runtime state is restored, the load phase is expected
to fail because the deserialized Marlin layers do not have a workspace.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

os.environ["VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING"] = "0"

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path('/home/codetalker7/vllm')))

MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-FP8"
REVISION = "e5be08033360965ceca7b0ffd72d521a51331ce0"
PROMPT = "The capital of France is"


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("phase", choices=("save", "load"), default="save")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--directory",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("issue-55198-lab/native-qwen-fp8"),
        help="Directory containing the native checkpoint and baseline tokens.",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

    directory = args.directory.resolve()
    # directory = Path("issue-55198-lab/native-qwen-fp8")

    checkpoint = directory / "model.tensors"
    baseline = directory / "baseline_token_ids.json"

    options = dict(
        model=MODEL,
        revision=REVISION,
        dtype="bfloat16",
        tensor_parallel_size=1,
        linear_backend="marlin",
        enforce_eager=True,
        max_model_len=128,
        max_num_seqs=1,
        max_num_batched_tokens=128,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.5,
        seed=0,
    )
    if args.phase == "load":
        if not checkpoint.is_file() or not baseline.is_file():
            parser.error(
                "Run the save phase first: the native checkpoint and baseline "
                f"must exist in {directory}"
            )
        options.update(
            load_format="tensorizer",
            model_loader_extra_config={
                "tensorizer_uri": str(checkpoint),
                "num_readers": 1,
            },
        )

    # Native reload can fail during engine startup profiling, before LLM(...)
    # returns. Preserve that traceback because it identifies missing state.
    llm = LLM(**options)
    outputs = llm.generate(
        PROMPT,
        SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=8),
        use_tqdm=False,
    )
    output = outputs[0].outputs[0]
    token_ids = list(output.token_ids)
    print(f"{args.phase} generation: {output.text!r}", flush=True)

    if args.phase == "save":
        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        llm.collective_rpc(
            "save_tensorized_model",
            kwargs={
                "tensorizer_config": {
                    "tensorizer_uri": str(checkpoint),
                }
            },
        )
        baseline.write_text(json.dumps(token_ids) + "\n")
        print(f"Native checkpoint saved: {checkpoint}", flush=True)
        print(f"Baseline token IDs saved: {baseline}", flush=True)
    else:
        expected = json.loads(baseline.read_text())
        assert token_ids == expected, (token_ids, expected)
        print("Native round trip passed: generated token IDs match", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
%autoindent
%env VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0
# for normal mode, DefaultModelLoader is the model loader
# for tensorized mode, TensorLoader is the model loader

%debug llm = (...)
"""
```

As it can be seen, the `TensorizerLoader` never constructs the `workspace` object needed by the Marlin kernel. This is because `process_weights_after_loading` was never called.

## Purpose

The PR aims to fix the above error. There is something to note, however: `process_weights_after_loading` is not idempotent for the native path. Particularly, if a checkpoint has already been saved via the native path, then the tensors in the file are already processed. Running `process_weights_after_loading` on those tensors will result in errors.

Instead of calling `process_weights_after_loading`, our solution introduces a new function to the class design: `initialize_runtime_state_after_loading`. This function does a subset of what `process_weights_after_loading` does; particularly, it only computes the state needed for the backend execution. For the case of the Marlin kernel, this function will compute the linear workspace (see the diff in the class `MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`). Similar to the design for the `process_weights_after_loading`, we use dynamic dispatch for the introduced function.

However, I'd love to discuss with the maintainers if this is a good design choice (or if they'd like something else to be done). I can also potentially extend the scope of this PR (to involve more linear backends) if the maintainers agree that the proposed solution is good.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Replace torch.topk in DSA candidate block selection
body: ## Summary `select_candidate_blocks` picks the top-k blocks per row with `torch.topk`, which runs a multi-pass radix select (`computeBlockDigitCounts`, `computeBlockwiseWithinKCounts`, `gatherTopK`). That does two things this caller does not need: - **It orders the results.** The only consumer is `_candidate_flags_kernel`, which does `flags[block] = 1`. Nothing downstream reads the ranking or the scores — only the *set* of selected block ids matters. - **It scans the whole padded workspace.** The logits workspace is padded to `max_model_len`, so `nblocks` is `max_model_len / block_size` no matter how short the context is. Past a row's end every block scores `-inf` and can never win a slot, but `torch.topk` has no way to express a per-row extent, so it reads all of it. This PR replaces that select on ROCm with a Triton kernel: - Each score and its index are packed into one order-preserving `int64` key, so `tl.topk` returns both at once and the separate `_store_candidates_kernel` pass disappears. The float bits are sign-transformed so IEEE order becomes unsigned order, and the index rides inverted in the low bits so ties resolve to the smaller index, matching `torch.topk`. - Each row is bounded by its own `end`, which is the part `torch.topk` cannot do. At 4K context in a 256K workspace this skips ~98% of the columns. - Decode rows are `batch * next_n`, only 1–640, which is too few to fill the GPU one program per row. Rows are split across programs and merged, with the split size computed **on device** from each row's live extent — a host-side bound would need a sync, and sizing from the padded width instead measured 6.3x → 2.0x at low concurrency. **The CUDA path is unchanged**; the new kernel is behind `current_platform.is_rocm()`. ## Not a duplicate Checked open PRs touching this area: - **#57858** is the only other open PR touching `candidate_blocks.py`, but it optimizes **prefill consumer-layer scoring** (`candidate_mqa_logits`, scoring only candidate columns). The producer-side block select this PR rewrites is untouched there. The two are complementary. Note #57858 also flips `_store_candidates_kernel`'s NaN handling (`!=` → `>`); the ROCm path here bypasses that kernel entirely, so the behaviors do not collide. - **#48726** (LiteTopk) is the indexer's *token* top-k, a different kernel and stage. - **#50470**, **#46172**, **#56944** touch `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` only (AITER dispatch, indexer optimization, prefill row sharding), not block candidate selection. No open PR optimizes `select_candidate_blocks`. ## Correctness The new path must select the same block *set* as the existing path. Verified against the unchanged path across 27 configurations — contexts 512 to 262144, rows 1 to 640, ragged per-row ends, non-zero `row_ks` starts, `row_repeat` decode grouping, `topk_blocks > nblocks`, and NaN scores: ``` 27 cases, 0 mismatches ``` Two cases this caught during development, both now handled: - `torch.topk` ranks NaN *highest*, and `_block_scores_kernel` can emit NaN during warmup, so keys force NaN above `+inf`. - When `nblocks < topk_blocks` the internal `K_PAD` shrinks below the output width, leaving tail columns unwritten; they are now `-1` filled. ## Tests ``` $ pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_candidate_mask.py -q 9 passed, 14 warnings in 4.23s $ pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py exit=0 (no failures) ``` ## Kernel performance (MI355X) Full `select_candidate_blocks`, CUDA-graph timed, swept over the decode shape space: concurrency 1–128 x spec-decode depth 1–5, `max_model_len=262144`, `block_size=8`, `k=64`. All 120 points are faster. | context | median | range | | --- | --- | --- | | 4096 | 4.16x | 3.97–5.08x | | 16384 | 3.99x | 3.27–4.70x | | 65536 | 2.94x | 1.64–3.15x | Representative points (microseconds): | context | conc | next_n | rows | before | after | speedup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 4096 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 47.55 | 11.20 | 4.24x | | 4096 | 32 | 1 | 32 | 58.00 | 13.96 | 4.16x | | 4096 | 128 | 5 | 640 | 293.54 | 67.86 | 4.33x | | 16384 | 32 | 1 | 32 | 59.19 | 14.31 | 4.14x | | 16384 | 128 | 5 | 640 | 299.65 | 91.67 | 3.27x | | 65536 | 32 | 1 | 32 | 60.31 | 19.30 | 3.13x | | 65536 | 128 | 5 | 640 | 330.51 | 185.83 | 1.78x | These shapes are TP-independent: the DSA indexer is replicated across ranks (`index_n_heads` is not divided by `tp_size`, unlike the main attention heads), so TP2 and TP4 run identical selections and one sweep covers both. ## Notes The kernel is still well above the bandwidth roofline (~45x at the largest shapes, more at small ones where it is latency-bound on two launches), so there is headroom left. `TILE=512` is a compromise: 1024 would take 65536-context from 2.36x to 2.79x but drop 4096-context from 23.8x to 14.4x. A context-aware tile choice could get both. Benchmarks used uniform context per batch; heavily ragged batches are bounded by their longest row. ## End-to-end serving Measured on MI355X TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, dspark MTP (5 speculative tokens, acceptance pinned at 3.51 so acceptance variance cannot contribute). Both arms are the **same build** differing only by an env toggle on the selection path, run concurrently on separate 4-GPU sets, after a warmup pass over every shape so Triton JIT and graph capture are paid before measurement. snapshot of trace: Before: After: **There is no measurable end-to-end difference, and none should be expected.** Output throughput, ISL 4096 / OSL 128: | concurrency | baseline tok/s | this PR tok/s | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 259.4 | 257.1 | | 8 | 1287.7 | 1282.4 | | 32 | 1068.9 | 1070.3 | | 128 | 1253.8 | 1254.8 | Repeating a single configuration three times shows run-to-run spread of 1112–1191 tok/s on baseline and 1142–1166 on this branch, with the sign of the difference flipping between repeats. The noise floor is several percent, while the expected effect is about 0.2%: the selection saves roughly 45 us per step against a 14.6 ms inter-token latency. The kernel win is real but it is a sub-1% slice of step time, so it cannot show up above noise in serving throughput. Median ITL, the most stable metric here, is unchanged (14.59-14.64 ms baseline vs 14.61-14.73 ms this branch). This PR should therefore be read as removing a hotspot that is prominent in kernel traces and cutting its cost 2-5x, not as an end-to-end throughput win. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used for this change.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Recover locally invalidated pull peer metadata
body:
## Summary

Recover a pull peer whose **local NIXL metadata is missing**, while Prefill is
still alive with the same engine ID. Otherwise, the cached `_remote_agents`
entry and prepared dlists can keep later requests on the stale path.

- On receive failure, query local metadata existence without descriptors.
  A transfer failure alone is not treated as evidence that Prefill is dead.
- Defer native metadata checks while background handshakes are in flight;
  defer cleanup until the affected peer's receive handles finish, using the
  existing `_engines_with_inflight_transfers()` guard.
- Reuse existing cleanup, so a fresh request can handshake again. Preserve
  healthy peers; never replay a failed request's old remote block IDs.

Only `nixl/pull_worker.py` changes production behavior. Tests extend the existing
connector suite and initialize the HMA fixture. No new router API,
configuration, push-mode behavior, or successful-path native metadata query.

## Related Work

Related to #49238. #50047 also cleans peer state, but on a broader
dead-peer/address-replacement basis. This patch requires positive local
metadata absence and handles unchanged producer identity. There is cleanup
overlap, not a claim that the two proposals are unrelated. This narrower scope
is explained in the [#49238 discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49238#issuecomment-5552206777). @YannikHinteregger, I would appreciate
your feedback on the overlap with #50047 and whether consolidation is preferable.

#52232 is a separate, necessary HMA fail-closed fix and is **not included here**.
Recovery alone does not prevent a failed HMA request from generating invalid
output. The integration experiment tested both changes, with attribution to
Tyler Michael Smith, and a small API terminal-error follow-up. #54689 (TTL)
and NIXL #1987 (native UCX race) are outside this patch's scope.

## Validation

### Maintainer simplification (2026-09-26)

Cherry-picked @njhill's [`7dc2a0e`](https://github.com/njhill/vllm/commit/7dc2a0eb49dbc62fdfc329885e663a672160cdec)
as `0cc7293ab1`, preserving Nick Hill's authorship and sign-off. The resulting
source tree is identical to his commit (`git diff 7dc2a0e HEAD --exit-code`).

- Reuse main's in-flight-transfer guard instead of maintaining a second
  request-to-engine map. Main retains receive metadata until all reads settle;
  the test that manually removed that metadata is therefore removed.
- Only transport failures schedule a local-metadata check; already-invalid
  peer rejection and KV expiry do not inflate the transport-failure counter.
- Keep handshake gating and cleanup ordering while removing redundant locking.

Local verification on macOS: 17 recovery cases passed using the existing
external source-AST harness with mocked NIXL boundaries. Ruff check/format,
`compileall`, `git diff --check`, and applicable pre-commit hooks (including
mypy) passed. This is **not** a new full-import vLLM, native NIXL, GPU, or
model-serving run. The September 23 results below remain historical results
from before this simplification.


### Rebase onto main (2026-09-23)

Rebased onto `8d16ca6cc21931481f6c6f9ec0365874a80c6bb2` without conflicts.
Initialized the three recovery fields in main's new HMA `region_pull_worker`
test fixture after full-import testing exposed the omission. This rebase adds
no production-code changes to the September 20 version. Recovery runs from
`get_transfer_results()` (also covering the legacy `get_finished()` wrapper).
The failure override forwards the current failure set, metric flag, and boolean

Real serving validation used isolated TP1 P/D, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731,

Important limits: the recovery-only failed request still emitted 32 invalid

This is controlled failure-path validation, not general accuracy, natural
transport-failure reproduction, RDMA/NVLink, or multi-rank native-race coverage.
Stuck reads/handshakes defer recovery; they are not forcibly released.
Native cleanup exceptions are not swallowed; this patch does not add recovery
from a failed native resource release.

title: [Perf][Attention] Remove D2H sync from FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA plan under async scheduling
body:
## Purpose

With async scheduling, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` did a blocking D2H copy on every metadata build. FlashInfer bakes each row's `kv_len` into its schedule on the host, and `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` is optimistic under async spec decode, so the builder copied `positions` / `seq_lens` back to get exact lengths. With MTP that happens on every draft step too. On GLM-5.3-Flash this made async scheduling *slower* than `--no-async-scheduling` (11.1 vs 7.7 ms TPOT at c=1).

How it works:

1. **Plan on the CPU with the upper bound plus slack.** The host bound, padded by 32 tokens and capped at the max valid count, is available without touching the GPU, so there's no sync.
2. **Clamp on the GPU.** FlashInfer keeps the plan in its int workspace as a list of work items with `kv_start`/`kv_end`. A small Triton kernel (`_clamp_work_kv_end`) computes each row's exact valid count on device from `seq_lens` / `query_start_loc` / `req_id_per_token` (same formula as before) and clamps every work item's `kv_end` to it. The FA3 kernel never reads past `kv_end`, so the slack (and the `-1` tail of the index buffer) is never touched.
3. **Reuse the plan across steps.** Contexts grow by a few tokens per step and the slack absorbs that, so while the new bounds still fit, `wrapper.plan()` is skipped and only the clamp runs. This is also why no-async gets slightly faster.

```
before:  GPU seq_lens --(blocking D2H)--> CPU exact lens --> plan --> run
after:   CPU upper bound + 32 --> plan (usually reused)
         GPU: clamp kv_end to exact lens (Triton, no sync) --> run
```

Notes:
- This reads `wrapper._plan_info` and the planned int workspace (the `MLAPlanInfo` layout from `scheduler.cuh`). The plan-info length is asserted, and the per-work capacity is read from the layout rather than hardcoded.
- With adaptive verification the host query split may not match the device one, so the host bound falls back to the batch max for every row.
- The exact (syncing) path is only used when there's no host upper bound.
- Only affects `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (Hopper; the default sparse backend for NoPE models such as GLM-5.3-Flash).

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs touching this backend. #55222 fixes the fp8 plan dtype and indexer workspace sizing, and #58260 chunks plan/run for >16k-row steps. Neither addresses the sync. #58260 does touch `plan()` / `build()`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase; I'm happy to do it.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests: `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py` on H100. I updated the existing tests to the new `plan()` signature and added two GPU tests against real FlashInfer. One checks that an upper-bound plan plus the device clamp matches an exact plan (including MTP-style multi-query rows around `index_topk` and a batch spanning several clamp blocks). The other checks that the plan is reused across growing contexts without replanning.
- E2E: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, TP8 on H100, fp8 KV cache, MTP with 5 speculative tokens, `max-model-len 32768`. Benchmark: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 --ignore-eos` at concurrency 1/8/32, at least 32 prompts, each point run twice, no profiler.
- Accuracy: `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` (1319 questions, 5-shot).
- Syncs: a torch profiler trace on the patched server shows no blocking sync left in the draft-step metadata build (before: 13 per ~5 steps, ~79 ms total, at `_kv_lens_host`).

All E2E runs, baseline included, have the fp8 plan-dtype fix from #55222 applied locally, since fp8 KV on this backend fails without it.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 18 passed.

Mean TTFT / median TTFT / mean TPOT (ms), average of 2 runs:

| | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, async | 136.6 / 138.8 / 11.09 | 226.2 / 188.6 / 21.87 | 338.2 / 319.9 / 45.04 |
| **this PR, async** | 128.1 / 126.9 / **6.86** | 188.0 / 152.7 / **17.36** | 283.7 / 251.5 / **37.04** |
| main, no-async | 129.8 / 128.8 / 7.70 | 189.2 / 157.8 / 18.20 | 258.9 / 175.5 / 42.71 |
| this PR, no-async | 124.2 / 123.8 / 7.47 | 177.2 / 152.0 / 17.95 | 254.7 / 170.6 / 41.72 |

With async scheduling, TPOT drops 38% / 21% / 18%, and async is now faster than no-async at every concurrency.

GSM8K is unchanged: 0.913 → 0.921 (async), 0.911 → 0.917 (no-async). MTP mean acceptance length stays ~4.2. The random-token bench has ~no draft acceptance, so its TPOT is close to the worst case for spec decode.

title: [Security] Reject short Voxtral Realtime audio before the encoder
body:
## Summary

A Voxtral Realtime chat or transcription request can carry an `input_audio` clip of only a few mel frames (about 10–80 ms at 16 kHz). The realtime feature extractor does not pad streaming audio, and `embed_multimodal` then trims the mel spectrogram and the conv output to a multiple of the block pool. When that trim empties the tensor, a reachable assertion in the worker kills EngineCore and the API server.

This rejects those clips while the multimodal processor is still building the request, so the client gets a 400 and the engine stays up. If a short waveform still reaches the worker, `embed_multimodal` returns empty embeddings instead of asserting, which is the same non-fatal path already used when realtime audio is missing.

## Changes

- `vllm/model_executor/models/voxtral_realtime.py`: reject waveforms that cannot produce a pooled encoder row (centered STFT pad, even mel trim, conv stride, block pool). Apply that check in `VoxtralRealtimeMultiModalProcessor` and, as a backstop, return empty embeddings from `embed_multimodal` instead of running the encoder.
- `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_voxtral_realtime_audio.py`: cover the reported 800-sample clip, the 1280-sample minimum, processor rejection before tokenization, and the worker backstop.

## Codepath coverage

- `POST /v1/chat/completions` (`input_audio`) → renderer → `VoxtralRealtimeMultiModalProcessor`: rejected.
- `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` → `render_cmpl_async` → the same processor: rejected.
- `WS /v1/realtime` → `render_cmpl_async` → the same processor: a short frame is rejected; frames that already meet the pool size are unchanged.
- Offline `LLM.generate` runs the same processor before the engine step.
- Worker `embed_multimodal` if a short waveform is still scheduled: returns empty embeddings and does not assert.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open and merged PRs for `voxtral_realtime`, `_truncate_left`, and short-audio handling, and read the diffs that touch this file:

- #39229 fixes mixed-batch `embed_input_ids` shape, not encoder truncation.
- #54516 caps transcription length after the prompt. Its "audio is too short" error is a max-token check, not this encoder trim.
- #58251 is a typing change around `forward_conv`.
- #40072 is a scheduler `max_model_len` guard.

None of those diffs reject a short waveform before `_truncate_left`.

## Tests

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_voxtral_realtime_audio.py -v
5 passed
```

`pre-commit` `ruff-check` and `ruff-format` passed on the changed files.
