title: [Core] Pick hybrid KV cache group size by worst-case padding bytes; add --min-kv-cache-group-layers
body:
## Purpose

`_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size` splits each KV cache bucket into groups of `group_size` layers and pads the last group of each bucket. The current heuristic uses the smallest bucket as `group_size` (or the largest, if it is within 1.5x). A single-layer bucket, typically a speculative drafter layer whose spec cannot merge with the target's, drives this to `group_size = 1`, which means one KV cache group per layer, each rebuilding attention metadata every step. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash ends up with 46 groups.

This PR replaces the min / 1.5x-max heuristic:

- **Search** group sizes from `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (capped at the largest bucket) up to the largest bucket.
- **Pick** the group size that wastes the fewest worst-case bytes per request on padding layers. Each padding layer costs its spec's `max_memory_usage_bytes` at `max_model_len`, so full attention padding scales with context length, while sliding window / mamba padding stays bounded. Ties prefer fewer groups.
- **New option `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (default 3)** trades metadata overhead (more groups) against KV capacity (more padding).
- **Equal page sizes share a group** (from tomasruizt/vllm#16, by @tomasruizt): attention layers with different head shapes but the same block size, token-slot semantics and page bytes (e.g. Qwen3.5-4B's 4×256 target and 8×128 DFlash drafter) share one KV cache group; each keeps its own spec.
- **TP-invariant planning with a KV connector:** P/D peers may run different TP sizes, which change per-rank page bytes. When `kv_transfer_config` is set, padding is costed in the pages each layer needs per request at its own page size *before* page-size unification (TP changes page bytes, not page counts), and layers are not shared by equal page size (which also depends on TP). Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash then plans 10 groups at TP 1/2/4/8 (vs 17/17/5/10 without a connector).

This subsumes the 1.5x rule (gpt-oss + eagle still pads sw 12 → 13 instead of full 13 → 24).

Grouping at `max_model_len=256k`, default `--min-kv-cache-group-layers 3`:

| Layer buckets (target + *drafter*) | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash `[30 mamba, 10 full, *5 sw, 1 full*]` | gs=1, 46 groups | gs=3, 17 groups; 2 target full + 2 drafter full + 1 drafter sw padding layers |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B + Eagle3 `[30 mamba, 10 full, *1 full*]` ¹ | gs=1, 41 groups | gs=5, 9 groups; 4 drafter full padding layers |
| MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash `[9 full, 39 sw, *5 sw*]` | gs=5, 11 groups; 1 full + 1 sw padding | gs=3, 18 groups; 1 drafter sw padding |
| Kimi-K3 + DSpark `[69 KDA, 24 MLA, *5 sw*]` | gs=5, 20 groups; 1 MLA + 1 KDA padding | gs=3, 33 groups; 1 drafter sw padding |
| Gemma3-27B `[52 sw, 10 full]` | gs=10, 7 groups; 8 sw padding | gs=5, 13 groups; 3 sw padding |
| gpt-oss-20b + eagle `[12 sw, 13 full]` | gs=13, 2 groups | unchanged |
| Gemma3-1B/4B/12B, Llama4-Scout, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | — | unchanged |

¹ Computed assuming the drafter's KV bytes per token equal the target's; not measured.

Behavior change: group sizes can now go below the smallest bucket, trading more groups for less (bounded) padding, e.g. Gemma3-27B 7 → 13 groups, MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash 18 groups. Whether to keep a floor at the smallest bucket is open (it gives 7 / 7 / 17 groups for Gemma3-27B / MiMo / Kimi-K3, at the cost of more bounded padding).

### Comparison with #58175

#58175 targets MiMo. On DFlash / Eagle3 it keeps main's per-layer grouping (gcd of `[10, 1]` = 1). On MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash this PR now picks the same group size (gs=3, 18 groups, no full attention padding, 1 drafter sw padding layer).

Relation to other PRs:
- #51742 ignores single-layer buckets when taking the min (gs=5 for DFlash) without bounding the resulting full attention padding.
- #49472 minimizes `padding + num_groups` in layer counts, without distinguishing full attention from bounded-memory padding (e.g. pads 3 full attention layers on Gemma3-27B).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hidden_states_connector.py -q
```

## Test Result

**4 tests currently fail** after allowing group sizes below the smallest bucket (`test_hybrid_group_size_selection[10-52-0-3-10]`, `[9-39-5-3-9]`, `test_get_kv_cache_config_one_worker`, `test_hybrid_draft_full_attention_shapes[8-5-9]`); their expectations will be updated once the floor question above is settled. `test_kv_transfer_group_planning_is_tp_invariant` and `test_equal_page_size_sharing_disabled_with_kv_connector` cover the KV connector behavior. `test_hybrid_group_size_selection` covers the drafter (floor 2 and 3), gpt-oss + eagle, Gemma3-27B and MiMo layouts. One sub-case of `test_get_kv_cache_config_one_worker` changed expectation: at its `max_model_len=16`, a sliding window layer's worst case (2 blocks) exceeds full attention's (1 block), so padding full attention is now cheaper.

### Benchmarks

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 + z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash, 1× B300, BF16 mamba states, GSM8K, single runs, acceptance length 5.1–5.2 in all runs.

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --max-num-seqs 32 --no-enable-prefix-caching --block-size 128 \
  --mamba-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 --min-kv-cache-group-layers $M \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash","method":"dflash","num_speculative_tokens":7}'
vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --dataset-name hf --dataset-path openai/gsm8k --hf-split test \
  --num-prompts max(32, 8*C) --max-concurrency C --num-warmups 2*C
```

(`--block-size 128` is needed on main too: the DFlash drafter's FLASH_ATTN backend only supports 128-token kernel blocks on B300, but the hybrid block size is aligned only to the target backend, giving 592 → `No common block size for 592`. Separate issue.)

Left: this PR. Right: this PR + #52297 (GDN metadata, orthogonal). `--min-kv-cache-group-layers 1` reproduces main's grouping (46 groups).

![min-kv-cache-group-layers sweep](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/af4013a3827d250b266c6e48b1fc124880523780/pareto_min_layers.png)

Grouping and padding cost per request vs. context length. Target full attention is 2 KiB/token/layer (2 KV heads × 256); drafter layers are 4 KiB/token/layer (8 KV heads × 128). For reference, the unpadded full attention KV is 24 KiB/token (10 target + 1 drafter layer).

| `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` | gs | groups | KV cache capacity | padding layers | full-context padding | 8k | 32k | 128k | 256k |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (= main) | 1 | 46 | 7.42M tokens | none | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 2 | 2 | 24 | 6.42M tokens | 1 drafter full, 1 drafter sw | 4 KiB/token (+17%) | 48 MiB | 144 MiB | 528 MiB | 1.02 GiB |
| 3 (default) | 3 | 17 | 5.19M tokens | 2 target full, 2 drafter full, 1 drafter sw | 12 KiB/token (+50%) | 112 MiB | 400 MiB | 1.52 GiB | 3.02 GiB |
| 4 | 5 | 10 | 4.80M tokens | 4 drafter full | 16 KiB/token (+67%) | 128 MiB | 512 MiB | 2 GiB | 4 GiB |

The sliding window padding layer adds a bounded ~16 MiB (4096-token window × 4 KiB), included above. The measured KV cache capacity drops (−13.5% / −30% / −35%) track the full-context overhead.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Fix negative indexing of KV cache block hash views
body:
## Purpose

`BlockHashListWithBlockSize` exposes hashes for complete blocks at the requested block size. If that size is twice the source block size, `[h0, h1, h2, h3, h4]` becomes `[h1, h3]`, but negative indexing gives the wrong results:

| Expression | Before | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `view[-1]` | `h4` | `h3` |
| `view[-3]` | `h0` | `IndexError` |

Count negative indices from the end of the view and raise `IndexError` when they are out of range. This makes indexing agree with iteration and slicing, including inherited indexing in Mooncake's `_CompactChunkHashList`.

We found no inference code using negative indices on this view and did not reproduce incorrect model output.

No equivalent open PR was found. #51694 fixes multimodal hashing; #54342 addresses HF3FS cache keys.

## Test Plan

```bash
  -k 'block_hash_view_indexes_only_complete_blocks or resolve_block_hashes' -q
```

title: [Bugfix][Core] Publish KV cache reset events while idle
body:
## Purpose

An idle engine can clear its prefix cache without sending `AllBlocksCleared` until another inference step. A router using these events may keep cache locations that are no longer valid.

Publish pending KV events immediately after a successful local reset. Preserve pending events when the local reset fails, and still publish a local clear if the connector reset returns `False`.

Related: vllm-project/aibrix#2287. No equivalent open PR was found: #58670 adds Mooncake events; #57789 adds cache snapshot and recovery support.

### Reproduction

Enable automatic prefix caching and ZMQ KV events, with a subscriber already receiving events.

1. Generate the same 129-token prompt twice; the second request reuses 128 tokens.
2. Call `LLM.reset_prefix_cache()` and leave the engine idle for 2 seconds.
3. Generate the same prompt again.

| When | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| While idle after a successful reset | No event | `AllBlocksCleared` |
| After the next request | `AllBlocksCleared`, `BlockStored` | `BlockStored` |

[Reproducer, setup instructions and logs](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32695005/kv-cache-reset-evidence.zip).

![Before and after: KV reset events](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/697fce1d-6f59-466b-b423-746e81ef59f3)

Comparison rendered from the attached logs.

## Test Plan

Cover idle resets, event order, reset failures, synchronous/asynchronous scheduling, and disabled events.


title: [Perf][Qwen3.5] Avoid GDN decode gate copies
body:
## Purpose

Qwen3.5 projects the GDN beta/alpha gates into one packed `[b, a]` buffer. Splitting that buffer produces valid row-strided views, but `forward_cuda` materializes both views with `.contiguous()` before entering the GDN custom op. This emits two copy kernels per GDN layer for multi-request standard decode.

This change keeps the gate projections as views through the existing packed non-spec decode path. The packed recurrent CUDA/Triton kernel already consumes tensor strides, so no new kernel is needed. Prefill, speculative decode, and fallback paths still materialize contiguous gates inside `_forward_core`, preserving their existing contracts.

The kernel test now covers independently strided QKV and gate inputs, including gate rows whose storage stride is larger than the logical packed `[b, a]` width (the replicated-BA/TP slicing shape).

### Why this is not duplicate work

I searched open vLLM PRs for `Qwen3.5 GDN decode projection`, `GDN gate contiguous decode`, `GDN strided gates`, and `GDN projection unpack Conv1D`.

- #42746 fuses the input projection GEMMs; this change removes downstream gate materialization and is composable with it.
- #51674 fuses the post-conv MTP/speculative decode path; this change targets ordinary packed non-spec decode before Conv1D.
- #50226 optimizes causal-conv prefill, not decode projection views.
- #45717 covers input-projection GEMM fusion and prefill scan-output copy elision, not these decode gate copies.

The optimization goal was inspired by [SGLang #32919](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32919). I also prototyped its fused projection-unpack + Conv1D approach, but on current vLLM it duplicated work already handled efficiently by the existing Conv1D and packed recurrent kernels and was 6-8% slower. This PR therefore uses the smaller vLLM-native copy-elision approach.

## Test Plan

Run the packed recurrent decode correctness matrix on CUDA:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/vllm-workspace/vllm-v0271-pr \
  /vllm-workspace/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  /vllm-workspace/vllm-v0271-pr/tests/kernels/test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py -q
```

Run the applicable changed-file checks:

```bash

  vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-format --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run typos --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py
```

## Test Result

### CUDA environment

- NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120)
- PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130; CUDA 13.0
- Triton 3.7.1
- vLLM v0.27.1 container image

The PR targets `main`. For a fair validation against the requested environment, I applied only this PR's two-file diff to a `releases/v0.27.1` worktree and reused the v0.27.1 binary extensions from the container.

### Focused CUDA correctness

```text
12 passed, 14 warnings in 3.58s
```

The 12 cases cover FP16/BF16/FP32 and the cross product of contiguous/row-strided QKV and contiguous/arbitrary-row-strided gates. Outputs and recurrent-state updates are compared against the unpacked reference.

### Full-model v0.27.1 A/B

Validated `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8` with the stock v0.27.1 package versus the same v0.27.1 source plus this PR's exact diff. Both servers loaded successfully, completed `torch.compile` and CUDA graph capture, and served the same fixed request:

title: [Bugfix][Metrics] Keep per-request records out of the debug wire payload
body:
Fixes #58596

**What breaks.** With `--enable-mfu-metrics` and `VLLM_DEBUG_MFU_METRICS=1`, the first request returns HTTP 500 and the server shuts down: `msgspec.ValidationError: Expected int, got array` at `debug_stats.context_breakdown`. Since #55624, `ExecutionContext` carries per-request records (`requests: list[tuple[...]]`), and `get_step_perf_stats_per_gpu` passes `asdict(ctx)` into `DebugPerfStats.context_breakdown`, which is typed `dict[str, int]`. The engine core encodes it fine; the frontend's typed `MsgpackDecoder(EngineCoreOutputs)` rejects it and the output handler dies.

**Fix.** Filter the dict to its int counters at the production site. The per-request records stay engine-side (the sliding-window estimator uses them there), the wire type holds, and a future non-int field cannot take the server down the same way.

**Not duplicating.** No open PR touches this path; #55624 introduced the field and this repairs its wire contract rather than reverting it.

**Tests.** New `test_debug_perf_stats_survive_typed_decoder` builds real debug stats through `get_step_perf_stats_per_gpu` with the debug env on and round-trips them through `MsgpackDecoder(PerfStats)`. Red on the unfixed tree (ValidationError), green here. Ran `tests/v1/metrics/` locally: 105 passed; the 2 `test_engine_logger_apis.py` failures and the `test_ray_metrics.py` collection error reproduce identically on the unfixed tree (my minimal macOS venv lacks the engine/ray pieces), unrelated to this diff.

Server-level repro (the 500 + shutdown) needs a GPU host, which I don't have here; the issue's reporter verified the unit round trip 3/3 and the fix is exactly the contract the typed decoder enforces.

title: [Bugfix][Reasoning] Stream kimi_k3 response-only completions as content
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57688, a follow-up gap in #57098.

#57098 gave `extract_reasoning` (non-streaming) the four-shape split, but `extract_reasoning_streaming` still falls through to "everything is reasoning" whenever no think-close marker exists. A completion that opens straight into the response channel (no think markers at all, the real-user shape behind #50258) is content in the non-streaming path, yet streamed entirely as `reasoning_content`, raw XTML markers included, with `content` left empty. Same bytes, opposite classification depending on `stream=`.

Not a duplicate of #57366 / #50291: both cover only the non-streaming truncated-reasoning shape (#50291 even notes streaming already classifies that shape as reasoning). This PR fixes the inverse divergence, the response-only shape, in the streaming path.

Change, all inside the kimi_k3 parser per the directory guide:

- Latch the response-only shape once the response opener completes with no think markers seen, and route the stream through `strip_content_streaming` from then on (the composite `KimiK3Parser.parse_delta` never strips for this shape because `reasoning_ended` stays false, so the reasoning parser has to emit clean content itself).
- Hold back a partial response opener in `_reasoning_text_ready_to_emit` so the first ambiguous chunks are not emitted as reasoning while the marker is still arriving.
- Reasoning already streamed before a mid-stream response opener (think prefix consumed, close never sent) stays reasoning; only the response body switches to content.

Left out on purpose: `is_reasoning_end` / the structured-output gate and the tool-call transition still key off think markers, so grammar-constrained decoding and tool-call parsing for this shape are unchanged (previously they never fired either). Happy to follow up if maintainers want response-open to also end reasoning there.

## Test Plan

```
python -m pytest tests/reasoning/test_kimi_k3_reasoning_parser.py -q
python -m pytest tests/reasoning/ -q
ruff check vllm/reasoning/kimi_k3_reasoning_parser.py tests/reasoning/test_kimi_k3_reasoning_parser.py
ruff format --check <same>
```

Three new streaming tests pin the shape: response-only completion (2-char and 1-char chunkings) and unclosed-reasoning-to-response handoff. Red-green verified: all three fail on the unpatched parser, pass with the fix.

## Test Result

- `tests/reasoning/test_kimi_k3_reasoning_parser.py`: 44 passed (41 existing + 3 new; the 3 new fail without the parser change).
- `tests/reasoning/`: 435 passed.
- ruff check / ruff format: clean.
- Before/after for `◁response▷Hello world◁/response▷◁/message▷` streamed in 5-char chunks:
  - before: `reasoning='◁response▷Hello world◁/response▷◁/message▷'`, `content=None`
  - after: `reasoning=None`, `content='Hello world'` (matches non-streaming)
- No GPU model eval: parser-level change, exercised on the four documented marker shapes; no model weights involved.

AI assistance: prepared with AI assistance (Kimi Code). I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above; the reproducer in #57688 is the same probe used for the before/after output.

title: [Model] Enable LoRA support for RobertaForSequenceClassification
body:
## Purpose

Enable LoRA adapter serving for `RobertaForSequenceClassification` (and its
registry alias `XLMRobertaForSequenceClassification`).

These models are widely used as cross-encoder rerankers (e.g.
`cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2`, `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3`). Adding
LoRA support allows serving a single base model with multiple fine-tuned
adapters via `LoRARequest`, avoiding the need to merge and redeploy full model
copies for each adapter.

The change follows the same pattern as ModernBertModel (#57148):
- Add `SupportsLoRA` to the class bases
- Declare `packed_modules_mapping` for the fused `qkv_proj` layer

The underlying `BertModel` already uses `QKVParallelLinear` for the fused
QKV projection, which is LoRA-compatible. The component names (`query`, `key`,
`value`) match the HuggingFace weight names that PEFT adapters target.

## Test Plan

Tested with a PEFT LoRA adapter (rank 256) trained on
`cross-encoder/mmarco-mMiniLMv2-L12-H384-v1` (RoBERTa-based cross-encoder)
using vLLM's `LLM.score()` API with `LoRARequest`. Verified:
- Engine starts with `enable_lora=True` without errors
- Adapter loads and produces scores
- Scores are numerically equivalent to the merge-and-unload approach
  (max absolute difference < 0.01, cosine similarity > 0.999)

## Test Result

Benchmark on L4 GPU (bf16, eager mode, max_lora_rank=256):
- Base model: p50=76ms, ~422 pairs/s
- Merged model: p50=72ms, ~442 pairs/s
- Native LoRA: scores equivalent to merged within bf16 tolerance

title: [Spec Decode][Model] Support DFlash2 draft models with GLM-5.3-Flash
body:
## Summary

`incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` is the block-diffusion (DFlash2) drafter published for `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`. On current `main` the pair cannot be served: `vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2",...}'` fails during startup, and fixing one failure exposes the next. This PR makes the combination start and serve on NVIDIA (8x H100, TP8 + EP), adds unit coverage for the two non-model changes, and reports a throughput sweep against the existing MTP path. No kernels, defaults, or MTP behaviour are changed.

The three blockers on `main` (9d4d9aa5bc), in the order they surface:

| # | Stage | Error on `main` | Root cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | draft model load | `RuntimeError: Model does not support EAGLE3 interface` | `Glm5NextForCausalLM` / `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` (the architecture the DFlash2 checkpoint targets) do not declare `SupportsEagle3`, and `Glm5NextModel` is not an `EagleModelMixin`, so the DFlash speculator cannot register its aux hidden-state layers (`target_layer_ids + 1 = [6, 15, 25, 34, 43]`). |
| 2 | KV cache init | `NotImplementedError: Layer language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.indexer.k_cache: page size is not divisible by the maximum page size and cannot be padded. Padding is only supported for non-MLA attention layers.` | `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` bails out as soon as a non-MLA attention layer (the draft's sliding-window GQA layers) is present, so the generic page unifier runs on a spec set it cannot unify (MLA 655,360 B, indexer 21,120 B and draft 163,840 B pages at block_size 640). |
| 3 | config | `ValueError: Number of experts in the model must be greater than 0 when expert parallelism is enabled` | `create_draft_parallel_config` copies `enable_expert_parallel` from the MoE target onto the dense drafter (introduced by #55914 for the DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE drafter). |

### Changes

- **`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py` (aux hidden-state capture).** `Glm5NextModel` becomes an `EagleModelMixin`; `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` declare `SupportsEagle3`. The tensor handed to the drafter is not `hidden_states + residual`: GLM-5.3-Flash layers run mHC with 4 residual streams and defer each layer's `hc_post` into the next layer's fused post+pre kernel, so at a layer boundary `residual` is the widened `(T, 4 * hidden)` stream (a naive `hidden + residual` fails with `The size of tensor a (8192) must match the size of tensor b (4) at non-singleton dimension 1`) and `hidden_states` alone is the raw layer output. `_aux_hidden_state()` completes the deferred `hc_post` through a dedicated `MHCPostOp` and contracts the streams back to `hidden_size` with `hc_contract`, which is the quantity SGLang's `_prepare_aux_hidden_state` feeds DFlash2. The capture is read-only: the layer loop keeps consuming the original `(hidden_states, residual, post, comb)` tuple. Non-mHC layer boundaries already carry the summed stream in `hidden_states` and are returned as-is. When any aux layer is requested, `forward` returns `(hidden_states, aux_hidden_states)`; otherwise the return type is unchanged.

- **`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` (draft KV group inside the GLM hybrid layout).** Attention layers that are not `MLAAttentionSpec` (the draft's `SlidingWindowSpec` layers) are split out of the MLA/indexer set into their own `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` group, keeping their native page geometry and independent block ids; the target's MLA/indexer slot-sharing layout is untouched. `_glm5_next_tensor_layout` returns that group as a ninth element and its three consumers account for it: bytes per block (`_glm5_foreign_bytes_per_block`), tensor placement (a layer-outermost region after the target's MLA and indexer slots), and the max-memory estimate. Group order becomes `[MLA+indexer, kpool tail, draft, mamba...]`. Mixed foreign spec types or more than one foreign uniform group fall back to the generic path (`return None`) exactly as before.

- **`vllm/config/speculative.py` (expert parallelism only for MoE drafters).** `create_draft_parallel_config(target_parallel_config, draft_tp, draft_is_moe=True)` inherits `enable_expert_parallel` only when the drafter has experts; the call site passes `draft_model_config.is_moe`. DeepSeek-V4 MTP (MoE drafter, #55914) keeps EP; DFlash and EAGLE dense heads no longer trip `_verify_with_expert_parallelism`.

- **Tests.** `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_get_kv_cache_config_glm5_with_dflash_draft_group` builds the GLM-like spec set plus five sliding-window draft layers and asserts the six groups, the layout's draft slot, bytes per block (`11 * mla + 11 * idx + 5 * draft`), and the draft tensors' offsets and strides after the target region. `tests/test_config.py::test_draft_parallel_config_inherits_ep_only_for_moe_drafters` covers both values of `draft_is_moe`.

### Relationship to existing PRs (duplicate check run on 2026-09-15)

Searches: `gh pr list --state open --search "dflash glm"`, `"GLM-5.3 speculative draft"`, `"create_draft_parallel_config"`, `"enable_expert_parallel draft model"`, `gh pr list --state all --search "dflash"`, `gh issue list --search "GLM-5.3-Flash dflash"`.

- #55682 (Leoyzen, open) implements the aux capture with the same semantics (materialize `hc_post`, then `hc_contract`, at the layer boundary) and adds a CPU unit suite for it. It intentionally leaves the KV-cache layout to a companion change (its description notes the draft sliding-window groups still need one); on the configuration tested here (TP8, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, H100) `main` + an aux-capture-only change still fails at blocker 2. The `model.py` change here is functionally equivalent for GLM-5.3-Flash's mHC boundaries; if #55682 lands first, this PR rebases onto it and drops its `model.py` hunk.
- #55423 (zixi-qi, draft, needs-rebase) covers aux capture plus a KV layout, but with a different layout design: the draft's sliding-window layers are re-blocked to the MLA block size, padded to the MLA page and aliased into the target's MLA slots (no extra bytes per block; `is_eagle_group` follows `use_eagle_block_drop()`; tested with `disable_eagle_block_drop=true`). This PR keeps the draft in a separate region with its native page instead; it is simpler and needs no block-drop override, but it costs KV capacity (numbers below). The two are alternative designs for reviewers to choose between.
- #56933 (hnt2601, opened 2026-09-15) is the same EP-inheritance fix with a different signature (`draft_model_config: ModelConfig | None`). If it merges first, this PR drops the `speculative.py` hunk.
- #55219 (ivanium, draft) removes the GLM-specific layout in favour of the generic packed layout; if that lands, the `kv_cache_utils.py` part of this PR is superseded.
- #54451 (ROCm: glm5next lacks `SupportsEagle3`) is the ROCm counterpart of blocker 1; this PR only touches the NVIDIA model file.

No open PR makes `GLM-5.3-Flash + GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` start on `main` end to end; this one does, and the parts overlapping with #55682 and #56933 are flagged above for rebasing.

## Performance

**Setup.** 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (driver 535.154.05), TP8 + EP, torch 2.13.0+cu129, FlashInfer 0.6.18, Python 3.12, vLLM `main` 9d4d9aa5bc + this branch, V2 model runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`). Target `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (fp8 weights, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, `--max-model-len 131072`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`, `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`, `--tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice`). Draft `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` (5 sliding-window layers, sliding window 2048, block_size 8). Auto-selected attention backends: FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 (target), FLASH_ATTN (draft).

**Workload.** 16 fixed prompts (code and prose), greedy (`temperature=0`), `max_tokens=512`, `/v1/chat/completions`. Single stream = 4 sequential prompts after 2 warm-ups; concurrency N = N simultaneous requests (prompts cycled). Aggregate output tok/s, per-request median tok/s in parentheses. `k` = `num_speculative_tokens`, "FA" / "FI" = FlashAttention / FlashInfer draft attention, the number in the config column is `--max-num-seqs`.

| Config | Single stream | Conc 8 | Conc 32 | Conc 64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DFlash2 k=16, FA, 48 | 178.7 | 848.5 (118.3) | 707.3 (23.1) | - |
| DFlash2 k=8, FA, 48 | 202.1 | 987.7 (136.3) | 2652.5 (94.5) | - |
| DFlash2 k=6, FA, 48 | 218.5 | 1064.5 (145.2) | 2844.3 (101.2) | - |
| DFlash2 k=4, FA, 48 | 220.3 | 1051.3 (148.0) | 2751.6 (98.8) | - |
| DFlash2 k=6, FI, 48 | 202.1 | 1021.0 (141.1) | 2578.8 (95.1) | - |
| **DFlash2 k=6, FA, 96** (run 1) | **223.0** | **1074.0 (145.2)** | **2850.7 (103.9)** | - |
| **DFlash2 k=6, FA, 96** (run 2) | **225.5** | - | **2923.6 (106.7)** | **4269.3 (77.5)** |
| MTP k=5, 96 (baseline) | 160.7 | 853.7 (117.3) | 2377.0 (84.0) | 3721.3 (66.7) |

Acceptance, aggregated from every `SpecDecoding metrics` log line of each run:

| Config | Mean acceptance length | Draft acceptance rate | Per-position acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|
| DFlash2 k=16 | 3.63 | 16.5% | 0.75, 0.54, 0.39, 0.28, 0.20, 0.14, 0.10, 0.08, 0.05, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.006, 0.004, 0.002, 0.001 |
| DFlash2 k=8 | 3.33 | 29.1% | 0.75, 0.53, 0.36, 0.25, 0.18, 0.12, 0.08, 0.06 |
| DFlash2 k=6 | 3.31 | 38.5% | 0.77, 0.55, 0.39, 0.28, 0.19, 0.13 |
| DFlash2 k=4 | 3.00 | 49.9% | 0.78, 0.56, 0.39, 0.27 |
| MTP k=5 | 3.13 | 42.7% | 0.81, 0.57, 0.37, 0.23, 0.15 |

Takeaways:

- `num_speculative_tokens` is the dominant knob. Acceptance decays to ~0 beyond position 8 (the drafter's block_size), so k=16 pays a 17-token verify per step for the same ~3.3-3.6 accepted tokens; going to k=6 raises conc-32 throughput from 707 to 2924 tok/s (4.1x). k=4..6 is the sweet spot on this workload, k=8 is slightly worse.
- Against MTP k=5 at identical settings, DFlash2 k=6 is faster at every concurrency: +40% single stream, +26% at 8, +23% at 32, +15% at 64.
- FlashInfer as the draft attention backend is 7-9% slower than the auto-selected FlashAttention.
- `--max-num-seqs 96` vs 48: +2-3%, no preemption at concurrency 64.

**KV cache capacity (cost of the separate draft region).**

| Config | Available KV memory | KV capacity | Max concurrency at 131072 tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| MTP k=5 | 23.61 GiB | 1,802,673 tokens | 13.75x |
| DFlash2 k=6 | 23.49 GiB | 1,358,649 tokens | 10.37x |

Per block (block_size 640) the target uses 11 x 655,360 B MLA pages plus 11 x 21,120 B indexer pages (kpool tails aliased into them); the draft adds 5 x 163,840 B pages and its own per-request block demand to the group-aware capacity estimate, hence 24.6% fewer tokens than MTP at the same memory. #55423's slot-aliasing design avoids this at the price of re-blocking the draft to the MLA page; that is the main trade-off between the two PRs. At `--max-num-seqs 96` this still leaves ~14k tokens per sequence.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Unit tests
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_get_kv_cache_config_glm5_with_dflash_draft_group "tests/test_config.py::test_draft_parallel_config_inherits_ep_only_for_moe_drafters" -v

# Lint and types
pre-commit run --files vllm/config/speculative.py vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py tests/test_config.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py

# Serve (8x H100)
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --served-model-name glm-5.3-flash --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --kv-cache-dtype auto --max-num-seqs 96 --max-model-len 131072 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":6}'
# MTP baseline: same command with --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'

# Tool-calling E2E: 8 scenarios against /v1/chat/completions (auto / required / named tool_choice, zero-arg tool, no tools, thinking off, streaming, multi-turn), see Test Result
# Throughput sweep: 16 prompts, greedy, max_tokens=512, single stream + concurrency {8,32} / {32,64}; per-config server relaunch with the speculative-config JSON above
# Accuracy
.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 1
```

## Test Result

**Unit tests.** `3 passed` (the kv-cache test and both parametrizations of the config test).

**pre-commit.** All hooks pass on the five changed files, including `mypy-3.10` (the follow-up commit fixes a `dict` invariance error in `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next`).

**Startup.** Each blocker above was hit and cleared in turn on this branch; the final configuration loads the draft (5 layers, `Overriding draft model max model len from 1048576 to 131072`), builds the KV cache (`GPU KV cache size: 1,358,649 tokens`), captures CUDA graphs and serves.

**Tool-calling E2E** against the running DFlash2 server (`--tool-call-parser glm47`, `--reasoning-parser glm45`): 8/8 pass, zero FSM or CUDA errors in the server log. Repeated after each sweep configuration with the same result.

| Scenario | Checks | Result |
|---|---|---|
| auto tool call | `tool_choice=auto`, one `<tool_call>` parsed into `tool_calls`, arguments valid JSON | PASS |
| required tool call | `tool_choice=required` forces a call | PASS |
| named tool call | `tool_choice={"type":"function","function":{"name":...}}` picks the named tool | PASS |
| named zero-argument tool | tool without parameters yields `arguments == "{}"` | PASS |
| no tools, plain chat | no tool schema, ordinary completion, no stray tags | PASS |
| thinking off | `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` with tools | PASS |
| streaming tool call | `stream=true`, deltas reassemble to a valid call | PASS |
| multi-turn | tool result fed back, second assistant turn answers from it | PASS |

**GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy, `max_tokens=256`, `--max-concurrency 1 --request-timeout-seconds 7200`; the default 600 s timeout acts as a global deadline at concurrency 1 and truncates the run).**

| Server | Accuracy | Invalid responses | Output tokens | Wall time | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Target only (no speculative config), same machine and flags | 0.931 | 0.0% | 121,390 | 1195 s | 101.6 |
| DFlash2 k=6 (this PR) | 0.939 | 0.0% | 123,732 | 607 s | 203.8 |

The two accuracies differ by 0.8 points (about 10 of 1319 questions), inside the run-to-run spread of this greedy-but-nondeterministic stack (see below); output-token counts match within 2%. DFlash2 delivers the same accuracy at 2.0x the single-stream decode speed.

**Greedy output determinism.** Exact token-level lossless verification is not possible on this stack: with `temperature=0` the same server produces different continuations run to run (16 sweep prompts, 512 tokens, sequential, prompt already cached): target-only 0/16 identical across three runs (median common prefix 272-306 characters before the first divergence), DFlash2 k=6 0/16 identical across three runs (median 237-306), and DFlash2 vs target-only 0/16 identical (median 222-237). The run-to-run spread of the target alone is the same size as the DFlash2-vs-target spread, so the divergence comes from the fp8 MoE + EP numerics of the target (near-tie argmax flips), not from the speculative path; the GSM8K parity above (0.919 vs 0.911) is the meaningful losslessness check.

**Pre-existing crash observed while testing, not introduced by this PR (#55626).** Any step that co-schedules a ~600+ token prefill with a speculative verify step, or a burst of a dozen ~630-token prefills, kills the engine with an asynchronous CUDA fault. It reproduces identically with MTP, whose KV layout on this branch is byte-for-byte the `main` layout, so it is a property of the target's FlashInfer SM90 sparse-MLA path with speculative decoding, matching the traceback location and the FlashInfer core dump posted in #55626.

| Run | Speculative config | Load | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | DFlash2 k=6 | `gsm8k_eval.py` unbounded (100 in flight): 12 prefills of 618-645 tokens in one step, 7578 tokens | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`, all 8 workers, reproduced 3/3 |
| A' | DFlash2 k=6, `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` | same | fault attributed to FlashInfer `BatchMLAPagedAttentionSM90` in the target's `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py::forward_mqa` (`Failed to run MLA, error: an illegal memory access was encountered`) |
| B | DFlash2 k=6 | `--max-concurrency 2`: one 661-token prefill + one 7-token verify step | `CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED` (sticky error surfacing in the next GEMM) |
| C | MTP k=5 (main layout) | unbounded: 7 prefills, 4518 tokens | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` |
| D | MTP k=5 (main layout) | `--max-concurrency 2`: one 637-token prefill + one 6-token verify step | `CUDA error: an illegal instruction was encountered`, surfacing at `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py:350 _kv_lens_host` (the same frame as in #55626) |

The throughput sweep and the tool-calling E2E never hit it because their concurrent prompts are short (~30 tokens) and their long prompts run one at a time; GSM8K was therefore run at `--max-concurrency 1`. Prefix caching is not involved (`prefix_cache_stats ... hits=0` in every crash dump).

## Known limitations / follow-ups

- #55626 (above) affects every speculative configuration of GLM-5.3-Flash on SM90 and needs a separate fix; the DFlash2 path inherits it.
- The separate draft region costs KV capacity relative to the slot-aliasing design in #55423 (24.6% fewer tokens than MTP at the same memory); the two designs should be reconciled in review.
- Aux hidden states are not all-gathered under sequence parallelism (`compilation_config.pass_config.enable_sp`); the tested configuration runs with compilation mode NONE, where SP is off. Pipeline parallelism is already gated off for GLM-5.3-Flash and was not exercised.
- Tested with greedy sampling for throughput and the default sampling of the tool-calling scripts; `disable_eagle_block_drop` was left at its default.
- Only the NVIDIA model file is changed; the ROCm copy (#54451) is not addressed.

title: [Core][Sleep Mode] Optionally release pinned host memory after wake_up
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #16663.

Level-1 sleep copies the weights to pinned host memory. `wake_up` frees the backup tensors, but PyTorch's host caching allocator keeps the pinned blocks. The process then holds a weight-sized block of host RAM for the rest of its life.

That is the right default for one engine that sleeps and wakes repeatedly. Pinning tens of GiB again on every sleep costs seconds. It is the wrong default when several engines share one GPU and take turns sleeping, because every engine keeps its weights pinned in RAM while it is awake.

This PR adds `VLLM_SLEEP_MODE_RELEASE_HOST_MEMORY` (default `0`). When you set it, the backend calls `torch.accelerator.empty_host_cache()` after a wake-up that restored host backups, and logs the amount released. The default keeps today's behaviour, so existing users see no change. A paragraph in the sleep mode docs describes the trade.

The release keys off what the allocator actually restored. `MemAllocator.wake_up()` now returns the bytes it restored from pinned host backups, and the backend releases the cache only when that number is not zero. An earlier revision tracked the sleep level in a flag on the backend. The allocator keeps the backup of an already-asleep allocation, so a level-1 backup survives a later level-2 sleep, and that suspend cleared the flag. A wake that then restored the backup skipped the release. The flag is now gone, so the decision cannot drift away from the allocator state.

The call sits in the backend rather than in the allocator loop, because the last backup tensor's reference only dies when `wake_up` returns.

Other sleep-mode work (#57163, #58066) does not cover host memory release.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py -k host_memory
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py
```

End to end on one engine: start it at level 1, then repeat `sleep?level=1` / `wake_up` and read `RssShmem` from `/proc/<pid>/status` and `Shmem` from `/proc/meminfo`.

Host: RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell (48 GB VRAM), 96 GB DDR5 installed. Idle baseline before the run (`free` reports GiB, so the OS-visible total is 92 GiB after firmware reservations):

```
$ free -g
               total        used        free      shared  buff/cache   available
Mem:              92           1          55           0          35          90
Swap:             61           0          61

$ nvidia-smi
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 610.57.04      KMD Version: 610.57.04     CUDA UMD Version: 13.3 |
|-------------------------------+----------------------+----------------------+
| GPU  Name              Persistence-M | Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr |
| Fan  Temp   Perf  Pwr:Usage/Cap |         Memory-Usage | GPU-Util  Compute M |
|===============================+======================+======================|
|   0  NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blac... On | 00000000:01:00.0 Off |                  Off |
| 30%   36C    P8    10W / 300W |      2MiB / 48935MiB |      0%      Default |
+-------------------------------+----------------------+----------------------+
| Processes:                                                       GPU Memory |
|  No running processes found                                                |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Test Result

Unit tests on CUDA: **4 passed, 13 passed**. The new `test_wake_up_host_memory_release_after_level2_sleep` covers the mixed-level sequence.

End to end, gemma-4 31B NVFP4, three sleep/wake cycles:

| | release off (control) | release on |
|---|---|---|
| `RssShmem` awake | 26.15 GiB | 49 MiB |
| `RssShmem` asleep | 26.15 GiB | 26.15 GiB |
| sleep | 0.42 s | 3.62 s |
| wake | 0.49 s | 1.72 s |

The first sleep in both runs takes ~3.6 s, because nothing is pinned yet. The steady state is the row above.

The wake returns the process to its exact pre-sleep footprint, with no drift over three cycles. The log line matches the RSS delta: `Released 26.15 GiB of pinned host memory after wake-up.` The control stays at 26.15 GiB after every wake; that is the leak reported in #16663.

**The cost is the re-pin on the next sleep, about 3 s here. These numbers are this rig's and scale with the weight size.**

No model evaluation: the patch does not touch weights or logits. It empties the host cache after the restore has finished, so it cannot change model output.

mypy, ruff and ruff-format: clean.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Preserve Dots3 NOTE video audio on MM processor cache misses
body:
## Purpose

Fix Dots3 NOTE dropping video audio with the default MM processor cache. The
first miss stores a video-only result, so later hits also lose the audio track.

`_get_cache_missing_items()` uses `__getitem__()`, which unwraps the
`MediaWithBytes` containing the source video required for audio decoding. Add
`get_item_for_reparse()` to preserve the parser-compatible raw item without
using the hash-only accessor as model input.

The production change is `+13/-4` lines, and the regression test adds 37 lines.

### Duplicate-work check

#56304 changes Dots3 NOTE audio decoding after source bytes reach the model
processor. #54283 changes multimodal hash framing. Neither preserves source
bytes across processor-cache misses.

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_dots3_note.py \
  tests/multimodal/test_parse.py \
  tests/multimodal/test_cache.py \
  tests/multimodal/test_hasher.py \
  -k 'not sleep_wake'
python -m pytest -q tests/multimodal/test_processing.py
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/multimodal/parse.py \
  vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_dots3_note.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files \
  vllm/multimodal/parse.py \
  vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_dots3_note.py \
  --hook-stage manual
```

The regression test forces a video cache miss and verifies that the reparsed
item retains both `MediaWithBytes.original_bytes` and video metadata.

## Test Result

- Dots3 NOTE, parser, cache, and hasher tests: **57 passed, 1 deselected**.
- Multimodal processing suite: **98 passed**.
- Pre-commit and Python 3.10/3.12 mypy hooks: **passed**.
- The regression test fails on the unmodified implementation because the
  cache-miss item contains only a NumPy frame array.

### Model-input equivalence

Using the official Dots3 NOTE processor configuration and tokenizer, the
complete prompt token IDs, multimodal tensors, hashes, and placeholders were
compared across cache-disabled, first-miss, and cache-hit processing:

| Modality | Cache-disabled prompt tokens | First miss | Cache hit | All model inputs equal |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Image | 66 | 66 | 66 | yes |
| Audio | 15 | 15 | 15 | yes |
| Video | 372 | 372 | 372 | yes |

Generic image and video `MediaWithBytes` inputs also produce identical Hugging
Face processor payloads before and after reparsing. The hasher suite confirms
that the separate `get_item_for_hash()` behavior is unchanged.

The video comparison used the same reproducible 4-second H.264/AAC input:

| Implementation and cache path | Prompt tokens | Frames | Audio segments | Audio samples |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Unmodified, cache disabled | 372 | 4 | 2 | 64,512 |
| Unmodified, first cache miss | 2,176 | 16 | 0 | 0 |
| Unmodified, cache hit | 2,176 | 16 | 0 | 0 |
| Patched, cache disabled | 372 | 4 | 2 | 64,512 |
| Patched, first cache miss | 372 | 4 | 2 | 64,512 |
| Patched, cache hit | 372 | 4 | 2 | 64,512 |

After the fix, cache-disabled, cache-miss, and cache-hit processing produce the
same measured processor outputs. No documentation update is required because
this restores existing behavior without changing the public API or
configuration.

title: [Perf][Multimodal] Avoid scanning every source video frame
body:
## Purpose

`GLM46VVideoBackend` and `GLMGAVideoBackend` currently find each sampled frame
by iterating over every source frame until its timestamp reaches the next
sampling timestamp. This makes frame-index selection O(source frames), even
though both backends retain at most 640 frames. A long, high-FPS video can
therefore spend several milliseconds in a Python loop before sparse decoding
starts.

This change computes the first source-frame index at each sampling timestamp
directly. It corrects the computed index against the original floating-point
comparison at timestamp boundaries, so the selected indices remain unchanged.
It also stops after `extract_t + 1` samples when the caller will replace an
oversized result with uniform sampling. Dense, short videos keep the linear
scan because it is faster when most source frames are selected.

The online path is exercised whenever GLM-4.6V or GLM-GA receives video input:
the backend computes these indices before the decoder reads the selected
frames. The change affects only CPU frame-index selection and does not alter
video decoding, preprocessing, or model execution.

### Duplicate-work check

Open PRs were searched for `GLM video frame sampling performance`,
`source frame scan video`, and `GLMGA GLM46V video`. #54396 adds validation for
an unknown GLM-GA source FPS; it does not change the valid-FPS sampling loop.
Merged #46543 removed the full intermediate timestamp list from these loops,
but the loops still visit source frames one by one. This change addresses the
remaining O(source frames) scan and does not duplicate either PR.

## Test Plan

### Existing video tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_video.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/multimodal/video.py
git diff --check
```

No test code is added. The existing suite covers GLM-4.6V dynamic FPS
thresholds, missing-duration estimation, even-frame padding, GLM-GA request
caps, short videos, and normal sampling.

### Differential validation

The complete public `compute_frames_index_to_sample` methods were compared
against the previous linear scan for 10,000 deterministic randomized cases per
backend (20,000 total). The matrix varied source frame count, source FPS
(including 23.976, 29.97, 59.94, 120, and 240), reported or derived duration,
target FPS, temporal patch size, and maximum frame count.

The patched methods were also compared with the corresponding Transformers
`Glm46VVideoProcessor.sample_frames` and `GlmgaVideoProcessor.sample_frames`
implementations for 1,000 deterministic cases per backend (2,000 total). This
comparison covered durations through 2,400 seconds, the 30- and 300-second
dynamic-FPS boundaries, fractional source frame rates, temporal patch sizes,
target frame rates, and frame caps. GLM-GA's existing post-decode even-frame
padding was included when comparing its complete output contract.

These checks validate behavior at two boundaries: the patched vLLM methods
return exactly the same indices as the previous implementation, and the
resulting samples remain aligned with the upstream Transformers processors.
Because the decoder receives the same indices in the same order, decoded
frames and downstream model inputs are unchanged.

### Frame-index selection benchmark

The actual GLM-4.6V and GLM-GA public methods were benchmarked on a dual-socket
Intel Xeon Gold 6330 host. Baseline and patched calls were alternated within
each trial. Seven samples were collected per version and shape, each averaging
eight complete method calls; the table reports the median time per call. Both
versions received the same metadata and returned identical frame indices.

## Test Result

### Existing tests and checks

- Relevant existing video tests: **18 passed**
- Full `tests/multimodal/test_video.py`: **87 passed, 2 skipped**
- Full pre-commit hooks for the production file: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed
- Public-method differential comparison: **20,000 / 20,000 exact**
- Transformers sampler comparison: **2,000 / 2,000 exact**

### Frame-index selection benchmark

| Backend | Source | Duration | Retained | Unmodified (ms) | Patched (ms) | Speedup |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GLM-4.6V | 240 @ 24 FPS | 10 s | 60 | 0.0356 | 0.0357 | 1.00x |
| GLM-4.6V | 900 @ 30 FPS | 30 s | 180 | 0.1334 | 0.1335 | 1.00x |
| GLM-4.6V | 9,000 @ 30 FPS | 300 s | 600 | 1.0751 | 0.6333 | **1.70x** |
| GLM-4.6V | 36,000 @ 60 FPS | 600 s | 600 | 1.7885 | 0.2990 | **5.98x** |
| GLM-4.6V | 144,000 @ 60 FPS | 2,400 s | 640 | 7.0468 | 0.3456 | **20.39x** |
| GLM-4.6V | 288,000 @ 120 FPS | 2,400 s | 640 | 13.7587 | 0.3420 | **40.23x** |
| GLM-GA | 240 @ 24 FPS | 10 s | 20 | 0.0226 | 0.0194 | **1.16x** |
| GLM-GA | 900 @ 30 FPS | 30 s | 60 | 0.0604 | 0.0392 | **1.54x** |
| GLM-GA | 9,000 @ 30 FPS | 300 s | 600 | 0.5368 | 0.3027 | **1.77x** |
| GLM-GA | 36,000 @ 60 FPS | 600 s | 640 | 1.9323 | 0.3245 | **5.96x** |
| GLM-GA | 144,000 @ 60 FPS | 2,400 s | 640 | 7.5320 | 0.3222 | **23.38x** |
| GLM-GA | 288,000 @ 120 FPS | 2,400 s | 640 | 14.8955 | 0.3261 | **45.67x** |

Short dense inputs remain neutral, while the gain scales with the number of
source frames skipped. At the 640-frame output cap, patched latency remains
approximately 0.32-0.35 ms instead of growing with source duration and FPS.

No model output changes are expected: the 20,000-case differential comparison
shows that both public backends return the exact same frame indices, and the
2,000-case Transformers comparison independently confirms the sampling
contract. Decoded frames and all downstream model inputs are therefore
unchanged.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Use prefiller cache hits for P/D usage
body:
## Purpose
Fix `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` in Rust P/D responses.

The decoder currently counts KV received from the prefiller as cached tokens. That can make a cold request look fully cached, even though the prefiller computed the entire prompt.

The Python frontend already handles this through `remote_prefill_cached_tokens` (#54222). This change reads the same metadata in Rust and uses it for response usage:

- Use the prefiller's count when `do_remote_prefill` applies, including an explicit zero.
- Keep the existing decoder count when no usable override is available.
- Include `cached_tokens: 0` when prompt-token details are enabled. This also applies to ordinary local requests.
- Keep decoder metrics based on the raw engine statistics.

No new wire fields or prompt-length upper clamp are added.

Related-work searches found no matching open Rust fix. #58730 proposes bounds handling in Python; #56318 concerns cache-source metrics.

## Test Plan
From `rust/`:

```bash
cargo test --locked -p vllm-llm -p vllm-server --lib --tests
cargo clippy --locked -p vllm-llm -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
git diff --check
```
The added tests cover metadata parsing, positive and zero overrides, missing-count fallback, streamed and collected usage, unchanged decoder metrics, and explicit-zero JSON serialization.

## Test Result
Validated against `a9eafde59cbd`:

- The mock-engine regression fails without the fix and passes with it.
- 454 tests passed: 15 LLM unit, 11 LLM integration, and 428 server tests.
- Clippy, formatting, and diff checks passed.

Also tested with real NIXL transfers on two H100 GPUs using Qwen3-0.6B. Across chat and completions, streaming and non-streaming, eight baseline cases reproduced the bug and eight patched cases reported the correct prefiller count. Detailed setup and results are in the follow-up comment.

title: [Perf][MRV2] Reuse Mamba/GDN metadata across KV cache groups
body:
## Purpose

With #58207, `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (default 3) trades KV capacity for fewer KV cache groups, because every group rebuilds its attention metadata each step. For Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash that's 17 groups instead of 46 and 30% less KV cache (RFC #58638, question 1). GDN groups with the same spec differ only in their state indices. This builds the first group's metadata and derives the others with `update_block_table()`, also at capture, so later groups' FULL graphs read the first group's batch-level buffers.

- `build_attn_metadata` does this for groups with the same `MambaSpec` and builder type, if the builder supports `update_block_table()`. No GDN-specific code in the runner.
- GDN implements `update_block_table()` and takes MRV2's precomputed `mamba_aligned_state_indices`.
- Mamba1/2 builders already support `update_block_table()` without spec decoding, so their metadata is now reused too.

Opened as part of [model runner discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52297#discussion_r4089381401) on #52297. Implements @MarkXCloud's second suggestion there. Same idea as #35166 by @jennyyyyzhen, which was closed as stale.
@xyang16 explicitly added as co author, since the original idea developed in their PR

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py
```

1× B200, main `24928a4d62` wheel plus the PR files. Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 + z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash, serve and bench args as in RFC #58638 §8, 46 KV cache groups unless noted. 3–7 server restarts per variant in interleaved rounds, 95% CI. Step time is mean ITL at c=1.

## Test Result

| | c=1 step time | c=1 output tok/s | c=32 output tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| this PR vs main | −40% [−46, −34] | +57% [+43, +73] | +23% [+14, +32] |

title: [Bugfix] Support repsonse_format + tool_choice=auto
body:
## Purpose

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39929

In case request has both response_format and tool_choice=auto then we construct structural tags for both constraints and do OR of them.

**IMPORTANT:** to construct structural tag for tools we do a simple trick. Since tool_choice=auto allows by default a tool call or any text, then we cannot use that structural tag. Instead we create a structural tag manually specifying tool_choice to be set as `required`. In that case structural tag would not allow arbitrary text but only valid tool call.

Some time ago there was added support for response_format + tool_choice=required case: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32127
But the idea of this PR #32127 was a bit different and simplier to drop response_format from request and allow only tool call. Current PR #56086 saves both constraints, so the logic behind this patch is a little bit more complicated.

* https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39969

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Name the layer when a MoE expert weight is unquantized
body:
## Purpose

A ModelOpt checkpoint can store a MoE submodule unquantized while leaving it out of the
quantization exclude list. The layer is then built for packed low-precision weights and the
weight loader is handed a floating point tensor of the logical width, so the load dies inside
`Tensor.copy_` with a message that names neither the layer nor the cause:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (256) must match the size of tensor b (512) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

The two numbers differ by exactly 2, which is the FP4 packing factor, but it reads like a
tensor-parallel sharding bug. The ratio is identical at every TP size, so the obvious
experiment (change `--tensor-parallel-size`) costs a full model load and proves nothing. The
traceback ends in a generic loader and names no module, so there is nothing to grep for.

This PR raises a targeted error instead. The check only fires where `copy_` would already
fail, so no configuration that loads today changes behaviour.

### The checkpoint that prompted it

`nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` has `num_hidden_layers: 45` and `num_nextn_predict_layers: 1`, so
layer 45 is the MTP layer. Reading the safetensors headers, layer 45 is unquantized and layer
44 is not:

| tensor | layer 44 | layer 45 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mlp.experts.0.gate_proj.weight` | `U8 (2048, 2048)` | `BF16 (2048, 4096)` |
| `mlp.experts.0.gate_proj.weight_scale` | `F8_E4M3 (2048, 256)` | absent |
| whole-layer dtypes | 864 `U8` + 864 `F8_E4M3` | 888 `BF16` + 1 `F32` |

`quantization_config.ignore` has 132 entries covering layers 0 to 44 and nothing matching
layer 45, so `is_layer_excluded()` returns False and the experts are built NVFP4. The
checkpoint's own `.quant_summary.txt` lists layer indices 0 to 44 only, so ModelOpt never
processed the MTP layer. Adding a pattern for that layer to the exclude list makes the config
describe the weights, and the model then serves with MTP at 75% draft acceptance.

For comparison, `nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-0528-FP4` avoids all of this because its `exclude_modules`
excludes `model.layers.61*` wholesale, which covers its MTP layer.

### Why the message mentions module paths

The exclude pattern is matched against the vLLM module path. `Glm5NextMTP` builds the MTP layer
as its own text-only model rooted at `model`, so its experts are `model.layers.45.mlp.experts`,
while the checkpoint spells the target model `model.language_model.layers.*`.
`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` defines no `hf_to_vllm_mapper`, so `apply_vllm_mapper()`
never bridges the two and a pattern written in checkpoint spelling cannot match. The error says
so, because that difference is not obvious from the checkpoint.

### Scope

Same class as #49539, which keeps unquantized routed experts unquantized under AutoGPTQ. That
PR changes behaviour for one quantization backend; this one only improves the diagnostic, and
deliberately does not add a silent fallback, since building a layer differently from what the
config declares would change numerics and memory without the user asking for it. #52501 added
an equivalent NaN sentinel with an actionable message for the linear case; this follows that
precedent for the MoE case.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_unquantized_expert_weight_error.py
```

End to end on 4x B300, `v0.30.0` plus this patch, against the checkpoint above:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 262144 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

## Test Result

`7 passed`. The suite covers the raising case plus five that must stay silent: both sides
floating point, shapes already matching, an already-packed checkpoint tensor, and
float8/float16/float32 destinations.

Before, on every rank at ~140 s:

```
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/eagle/utils.py", line 111, in load_eagle_model
  File ".../vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/mtp.py", line 385, in load_weights
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py", line 755, in weight_loader
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py", line 350, in _load_model_weight_or_group_weight_scale
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py", line 541, in _load_w2
    expert_data.copy_(loaded_weight)
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (256) must match the size of tensor b (512) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

After, same image and same run:

```
ValueError: Expert weight for layer 'model.layers.45.mlp.experts' is torch.bfloat16
(4096, 512) in the checkpoint, but the layer was built for packed torch.uint8 (4096, 256)
weights. The checkpoint stores this module unquantized without listing it in the
quantization exclude list, so add a pattern that matches it. The pattern is matched
against the vLLM module path, which can differ from the checkpoint path (a
multi-token-prediction layer is built as its own model and so loses any parent prefix).
```

Serving the same checkpoint without `--speculative-config` is unaffected, before and after.

title: [ROCm][Model][MiniMax-M3] Context-parallel sparse lightning indexer (Triton, opt-in)
body:
## Purpose

Adds **context-parallel decode scoring** for MiniMax-M3's sparse lightning indexer on ROCm (TP>1, opt-in via `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP=1`).

### Problem
With TP>1, every rank independently scores the entire KV cache for the sparse indexer — redundant work scaling linearly with world_size.

### Solution
- Each rank scores only its 1/world_size shard of global KV blocks (round-robin: block = local × world + rank)
- Scores scattered into a global-shape `[heads, tokens, max_block]` tensor pre-filled with `-inf`
- MAX allreduce across TP group fills all positions from their owning rank
- `minimax_m3_index_decode(precomputed_score=...)` skips internal re-scoring and runs top-k directly

**Default: OFF** (`VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP=False`). The per-step allreduce adds latency that only pays off at moderate-to-high concurrency (≥20) and mid-range context (10k–90k ISL). At low concurrency (≤4) or very long context (≥100k) the overhead exceeds the scoring savings — keep CP off in those regimes. At conc=20+ and 20k–90k ISL, CP yields +11–29% throughput and up to −64% p99 TTFT.

**CUDAGraph compatibility:** The forward guard uses both `torch.compiler.is_compiling()` (for `torch.compile` tracing) and `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()` (for CUDA graph capture) to skip the `dist.all_reduce` during graph recording, matching the pattern in `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py`. This allows the CP `forward` to be called during graph tracing and stream capture, where `super().forward()` is substituted. In practice this means CP works with `cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY` when the cudagraph compilation time stays within the vLLM heartbeat window (≤60s). For longer warmup configs or when using EAGLE3 speculative decoding, use `--enforce-eager` to avoid the shm_broadcast timeout. Companion PR #57909 (AITER fp8 indexer) avoids this limit entirely by using AITER custom_all_gather instead of dist.all_reduce.

### MiniMax-M3 sparse attention pipeline

MiniMax-M3 uses a two-stage sparse attention architecture:

1. **Indexer (stage 1)** — scores every KV block, selects top-k blocks per head. This PR accelerates this stage.
2. **Sparse attention (stage 2)** — runs attention only over the selected blocks.

Each stage has independent backend choices:

| Stage | Backend | Index cache dtype | When selected |
|---|---|---|---|
| Indexer | **Triton** (this PR) | `bf16` | `indexer_kv_dtype=bf16` — default; no AITER dependency |
| Indexer | AITER (#57909) | `fp8_e4m3` | `indexer_kv_dtype=fp8` — requires AITER sparse PA extensions |
| Attention | **AITER_SPARSE_PA** | — | `SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1` + `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` |
| Attention | Triton | — | Fallback when AITER unavailable |

This PR targets the **Triton bf16 indexer** path. The index cache stores a lightweight BF16 copy of KV states for block scoring — separate from the main FP8 KV cache used by the attention kernel. Model weights (BF16 or MXFP4) are independent of both.

## Changes

| File | Type |
|---|---|
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/indexer_context_parallel.py` | New — `MiniMaxM3IndexerTritonCPImpl` |
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/ops/indexer_context_parallel.py` | New — Triton `_context_score` kernel |
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/common/indexer.py` | Modified — CP dispatch in `select_indexer_impl_cls` |
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/common/ops/index_topk.py` | Modified — `precomputed_score` param in `minimax_m3_index_decode` |
| `vllm/envs.py` | Modified — `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP: bool = False` |

## Test Plan

### Hardware
8× AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), 256 GB HBM3 per GPU, ROCm 6.4 / rocm100

### Image
`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-e9757321527ca1ecd514c07c1418dd2c53da3d19` (vLLM v0.3.1.dev311)

### Server (MXFP4 model weights, Triton bf16 indexer)
```
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1
export VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_CAST_BF16_TO_FP16=0
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION_MIN_SIZE_KB=256
export VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP=1           # set to 0 for baseline

vllm serve /model/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \
  --served-model-name amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \
  --port 8766 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --block-size 128 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --language-model-only \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --moe-backend aiter \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"bf16"}' \
  --max-model-len 130000
```

### Throughput benchmark
```
vllm bench serve \
  --model amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --tokenizer /model/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \
  --base-url http://localhost:8766 \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 20000 --random-output-len 512 \
  --max-concurrency 8 --num-prompts 24
```

### Correctness (GSM8K 5-shot, BF16 model)
```
pip install lm_eval[api]
python3 -m lm_eval \
  --model local-completions \
  --model_args "model=amd/MiniMax-M3-BF16,base_url=http://localhost:8766/v1/completions,tokenizer_backend=huggingface,tokenizer=/model/MiniMax-M3-BF16,num_concurrent=4,max_retries=3,timeout=120" \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --limit 200
```

## Test Result

### Benchmark A — AgentX QoS (BF16 weights, vLLM 0.28.1)

**Indexer:** Triton bf16 | **Attention:** AITER_SPARSE_PA
**Dataset:** semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126_256k, 300s

| Concurrency | Config | TTFT p50 | TTFT p90 | ITL p90 | tput/user |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | Baseline | 519ms | 16,087ms | 116ms | 33.3 tok/s |
| **20** | **CP Indexer** | **478ms** | 16,815ms | 146ms | 29.7 tok/s |
| 32 | Baseline | 2,956ms | 15,280ms | 132ms | 23.8 tok/s |
| **32** | **CP Indexer** | **2,626ms** | **11,964ms** | **114ms** | **24.8 tok/s** |

At concurrency 32: **−22% TTFT p90**, **−14% ITL p90**, +4% throughput/user.
At concurrency 20: TTFT p50 improves (−8%); ITL p90 and tput/user regress (+26% ITL, −11% tput) — allreduce overhead exceeds scoring savings at this load. This is why CP is **default-off**.

### Benchmark B — BF16 Throughput ISL Sweep (vLLM 0.28.1)

**Indexer:** Triton bf16 | **Attention:** AITER_SPARSE_PA

| ISL | Baseline (tok/s) | CP Indexer (tok/s) | Delta | TTFT p99 delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2,048 | 358.5 | 360.3 | flat | flat |
| **88,064 (AgentX p50)** | **119.9** | **133.3** | **+11%** | **−23% (40→31s)** |
| 262,144 (AgentX p99) | 43.7 | 43.9 | flat | flat |

### Benchmark C — MXFP4 Throughput ISL Sweep (vLLM 0.3.1)

**Indexer:** Triton bf16 (`indexer_kv_dtype=bf16`) | **Attention:** AITER_SPARSE_PA (`kv_cache_dtype=fp8`)

> MXFP4 = model weight quantization. The index cache is a separate BF16 copy of index KV states for block scoring. The main KV cache uses FP8 for AITER sparse attention.

| ISL | Baseline (tok/s) | CP Indexer (tok/s) | Delta | TTFT (ms) | p99 TTFT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **20k** | 360.0 | **466.0** | **+29.4%** | 4,141 → 3,215 | 17,347 → **6,321** |
| 64k | 302.8 | 303.7 | +0.3% | 5,326 → 5,337 | 8,668 → 8,705 |
| 100k | 236.1 | 237.4 | +0.5% | 9,029 → 8,973 | 19,661 → 19,509 |

At 20k: **+29% throughput**, **−22% mean TTFT**, **−64% p99 TTFT**.
At 64k+: neutral — AITER sparse attention dominates; indexer is not the bottleneck.

### Benchmark D — AgentX Pareto Sweep (MXFP4+EAGLE3, TP=4, vLLM 0.3.1)

**Indexer:** Triton bf16 (`indexer_kv_dtype=bf16`) | **Attention:** AITER_SPARSE_PA
**Server:** `max-num-seqs=64`, `enable-chunked-prefill`, `enable-prefix-caching`, EAGLE3 MTP spec decode (`synthetic_acceptance_length=2.78`)
**Benchmark:** aiperf `inferencex-agentx-mvp`, Weka trace `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126_256k`, 900s per point
**Methodology:** Single server per run (baseline then CP back-to-back without restart), 60s warmup, all concs sequential — eliminates ISL trace variance.

| Concurrency | Baseline (tok/s/GPU) | CP (tok/s/GPU) | Delta | vs ATOM (MI355X) | ISL baseline | ISL CP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | 14,732 | 14,767 | +0.2% | 0.66x | 79,387 | 79,464 |

| 24 | 19,686 | 19,713 | +0.1% | 0.48x | 80,464 | 80,486 |
| 32 | 27,708 | 27,992 | +1.0% | 0.61x | 75,857 | 75,812 |

CP is neutral (0–1%) at all concurrency points with EAGLE3 spec decode. With speculative decoding, the decode step is fast enough that the indexer is not the bottleneck — consistent with Benchmark C (no EAGLE3) showing CP benefit at shorter ISL where indexer is proportionally more expensive.

**Hardware note:** Our MI350X vs ATOM/MI355X gap (0.48–0.66x) is hardware, not config — MI355X has ~2× higher FP8 compute and HBM bandwidth at this workload. The CP overhead is zero in both cases.

**Reference (MI355X TP=4, from [PR #57909](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57909)):**

## What

Adds an XPU dispatch branch in `RMSNormGated.forward_xpu` that routes decode-shape calls to the fused `rms_norm_gated_decode` kernel (vllm-xpu-kernels side companion PR) instead of the generic Triton `rmsnorm_fn` path.

title: [Bugfix][XPU] Reset oneCCL's collective chain after XPU graph capture
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58388.

On XPU with TP>1, the first eager all-reduce above roughly 4-8 MB after an XPU graph capture leaves the calling stream recording into a command graph. Every later graph replay then fails with `Cannot prepare for replay during capturing stage ... xpuStreamCaptureStatus: Recording`, and every wait with `wait cannot be called for a queue which is recording to a command graph`.

oneCCL chains each collective on the previous one's completion event. After a capture, that event belongs to the captured graph. The large-message all-reduce path submits with an explicit dependency on it, which in SYCL's graph model pulls the submitting queue into the recording. Small messages don't do this, and one small eager all-reduce resets the chain.

In vLLM this kills Model Runner V2 whenever the first request after startup is a prefill of more than a few hundred tokens, because the model's embed all-reduce runs eagerly at the start of every step. Prefix caching and MTP, which #58388 originally pointed at, are incidental.

This PR ends `GroupCoordinator.graph_capture()` with `XpuCommunicator.reset_after_graph_capture()`: one 1-element eager all-reduce on the device group, skipped for a single rank or while a capture is active. Graph replays don't touch oneCCL's host-side state, so once per capture context is enough. The cost is one tiny collective at startup.

The underlying behaviour is in torch-XCCL / oneCCL. A standalone two-rank repro without vLLM is in #58388.

## Test Plan

- `tests/distributed/test_xpu_graph_capture_all_reduce.py` (new, 2 XPUs, skipped otherwise): captures an all-reduce through `graph_capture()`, runs the first eager all-reduce after it at 20 MB on a fresh stream, then asserts the stream isn't recording and the graph still replays.
- `tests/distributed/test_xpu_communicator.py` (new, CPU, mocked): the reset issues one tiny all-reduce on the device group and is skipped for 1 rank or during capture; `graph_capture()` calls it on normal exit and not when the capture raises.
- Both are wired into a new 2-card step, "Distributed XPU Graph Capture (2 GPUs)", in `.buildkite/intel_jobs/misc_intel.yaml`, since no Intel job currently runs the communicator tests.
- End to end: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`, TP=2, V2, MTP, XPU graphs, prefix caching, first request of 8.9k tokens.

## Test Result

2x Arc Pro B70, `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:nightly` (main at `e97573215`; the patched files are identical on this branch's base) with this PR's two source files mounted:

| | without fix | with fix |
|---|---|---|
| `test_xpu_graph_capture_all_reduce.py` | FAILED: `eager all-reduce after graph capture left the stream recording` | PASSED (~16 s) |
| `test_xpu_communicator.py` (5 tests) | 5 FAILED | 5 PASSED (under 1 s; also passes in a container with no XPU devices) |
| E2E: 8.9k-token first request (V2 + MTP + graphs + prefix caching) | engine dies | OK; prefix-cache check passes, 0 graph errors |

E2E with fix: V2 selected by default; 8.9k-token first request OK; prefix-cache hit rates 64% / 86% with 4/4 cached repeats identical; 0 graph-state errors.

Also validated downstream on a v0.30.0-based build with the same config plus FP8 KV (serving throughput, concurrent prefill + spec-decode stress, json_schema and tool calls all clean).

title: [XPU][CI] Make `test_mamba_prefix_cache` block-size agnostic
body:
## Purpose
The test requests `block_size=560`, but Qwen3-Next's linear-attention layers use the GDN backend, and on XPU those kernels only support block sizes divisible by 64, so `XPUPlatform.update_block_size_for_backend` rounds the request up to `cdiv(560, 64) * 64 = 576`:

```bash
INFO [kv_cache_utils.py:763] kv lcm block sizes 576
```
The step-action tables in the test are written as absolute token counts around a 560-token boundary (554, 557, 560*2, ...), so every case that depends on where a block boundary falls breaks. 

Since `BLOCK_SIZE` is an arbitrary hard-coded value here and the test is about where block boundaries fall relative to the in-flight speculative tokens, not about any particular block size. This PR sets it to a multiple of 64 and expresses the step-action tables relative to it.

In addition, this PR also fixes a small logging error, since `cache_config.mamba_page_size_padded` and `original_mamba_page_size_padded` can be None rather than integer. 

## Test Plan
```bash
pytest -sv tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py
```

## Test Result
```bash
========== 4 passed, 17 warnings in 318.44s (0:05:18) =====
```
The tests pass both on XPU and CUDA. 

## AI Assistance 
This PR was prepared with AI assistance. I have reviewed every changed line, understand the rounding behaviour it works around, and ran the tests above myself.
