title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep resumable sessions that stop while preempted
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58776.

With async scheduling, a resumable (streaming-input) request can be preempted while a step is still in flight. That step's output is delivered as stale output, and if it hits a stop condition the request stops in `PREEMPTED` state. Two things then go wrong:

1. **The session drops out of every queue.** `_handle_stopped_request` re-enqueues the resumable request, but the stopped-while-preempted cleanup in `update_from_output` removes every occurrence from `waiting` and `skipped_waiting`, including that new entry. A `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` session is only rescheduled by staying in `skipped_waiting`, so it is never scheduled again.
2. **The fold deletes the prompt.** `_update_request_as_session` keeps `all_token_ids[num_prompt_tokens:num_computed_tokens]` and deletes the rest. After preemption `num_computed_tokens == 0`, so it deletes the whole list, while `prompt_token_ids` (a separate list) is only extended; `num_prompt_tokens` then no longer matches `all_token_ids`, and the previous turn's output is lost.

Changes:

- After the stopped-while-preempted cleanup, re-enqueue requests that did not finish, so each ends up in exactly one queue.
- In the fold, keep up to `max(num_computed_tokens, num_tokens - 1)`. On a normal stop `num_computed_tokens == num_tokens - 1`, so nothing changes; after preemption the session keeps all but the final sampled token, and `num_computed_tokens` stays 0 so everything is recomputed.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open and closed issues and PRs for this path (`stopped_preempted_reqs`, streaming/resumable + preempt, `_update_request_as_session`, session hang symptoms); none found. #58668 fixes a different case where `num_computed_tokens` is wrong at the fold (a speculative step stopping on an accepted draft). Both PRs append a test to `tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py`, so whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.

## Test Plan

```bash
# CPU
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py -k stop_while_preempted
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core tests/v1/streaming_input -q

# GPU (GB200)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/streaming_input \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler_e2e.py tests/v1/core/test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py -v
```

New tests in `tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py`, using a real `AsyncScheduler`:

- `test_session_resumes_after_stop_while_preempted` (next chunk queued before / after the stop) reproduces #58776. It asserts that the session is scheduled again, that `all_token_ids` and `prompt_token_ids` both hold the old prompt, the kept output and the new chunk, and that everything is recomputed.
- `test_non_resumable_request_stays_dequeued_after_stop_while_preempted` guards the re-enqueue: a request that finishes while preempted must stay out of the queues. It passes on main and fails if the `is_finished()` check is dropped.

## Test Result

`test_session_resumes_after_stop_while_preempted`, with each half of the fix:

| scheduler | result |
| --- | --- |
| main | both cases fail: tokens are `[20, 21]` (prompt and output lost) |
| re-enqueue fix only | both fail: same token loss |
| fold fix only | both fail: `KeyError`, the session is never scheduled |
| this PR | both pass |

- CPU, `tests/v1/core` + `tests/v1/streaming_input`: 806 passed with this PR vs 804 on main. The only difference is the two cases above; the remaining 1 failure and 6 errors need a GPU and are identical on main.
- GPU (GB200), `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py`: 14 passed.
- GPU (GB200), `tests/v1/streaming_input` + the GPU-only core tests above: 19 passed, 2 errors. The errors are `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler_e2e.py`, which fails identically on main: engine profiling hits `assert prefill_query.shape[0] == num_prefill_tokens` in the FlashInfer backend with `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM` on this machine.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find, reproduce and fix this. I reviewed every changed line.

title: [XPU][MLA] Support FlashAttnMLA backend on XPU
body:
## Summary

- Route XPU MLA through the existing `FLASH_ATTN_MLA` backend, matching the way XPU support is integrated under `FLASH_ATTN`.
- On XPU, use `vllm-xpu-kernels` `flash_attn_varlen_func` for MLA paged decode by packing `q = [q_nope, q_pe]` and using the latent cache as K with a narrowed V view.
- Keep CUDA FlashAttnMLA behavior unchanged, including FA3 decode/LSE handling.
- Fix XPU varlen output allocation so omitted `out` tensors use the V head dimension. This is required for MLA where Q/K dim is 576 and V dim is 512, and is behavior-preserving for regular attention where `q.shape[-1] == v.shape[-1]`.

## Validation method

Run from a vLLM checkout on an Intel XPU machine with `vllm-xpu-kernels` installed or on `PYTHONPATH`.

1. Unit tests

Run the following ut repeatedly on XPU:
```bash
cd vllm && python3 -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -v
```
Result (on the rebased branch, against latest upstream/main):

```bash
tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py::test_backend_correctness[...] PASSED
... (197 test cases total)
tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py::test_chunked_context_backend_correctness[fp8-glm-MLAPrefillBackendEnum.FLASH_ATTN] PASSED [100%]

=========== 197 passed, 2 skipped, 17 warnings in 190.83s (0:03:10) ===========
```
(The 2 skips are CUDA-only DCP tests, unrelated to XPU.)

2. End-to-end test

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

tmp_script="$(mktemp /tmp/vllm_xpu_mla_validate.XXXXXX.py)"
trap 'rm -f "${tmp_script}"' EXIT

cat >"${tmp_script}" <<'PY'
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

def main():
    llm = LLM(
        model="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite",
        tensor_parallel_size=2,
        dtype="bfloat16",
        attention_backend="FLASH_ATTN_MLA",
        block_size=64,
        max_model_len=512,
        trust_remote_code=True,
        enforce_eager=True,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.80,
    )

    prompts = [
        "Hello, my name is",
        "The capital of France is",
        "The future of AI in 2030 will be",
    ]
    sampling_params = SamplingParams(
        temperature=0.0,
        max_tokens=64,
        repetition_penalty=1.1,
    )
    outputs = llm.generate(prompts, sampling_params)
    for output in outputs:
        print("=" * 60)
        print("PROMPT:", output.prompt)
        print("OUTPUT:", output.outputs[0].text)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
PY

python "${tmp_script}"
```

Expected result:
- Logs show `Using Flash Attention MLA backend on XPU.`
- Generation reaches `Processed prompts: 100%` and prints outputs for all prompts.

This was validated locally on 2x Intel Arc Pro B60; the run logged `Using Flash Attention MLA backend on XPU.`, completed `Processed prompts: 100%`, and generated coherent outputs for all three prompts (e.g. "Hello, my name is" -> "John. I am a 20 year old male...", "The capital of France is" -> "Paris.").

3. Compile check

```bash
python -m py_compile vllm/_xpu_ops.py vllm/platforms/xpu.py vllm/v1/attention/backends/fa_utils.py vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashattn_mla.py vllm/v1/attention/backends/registry.py
```
All 5 changed files compile cleanly with no errors.

4. Accuracy

Ran `lm_eval` with `--model vllm` against DeepSeek-V2-Lite on Intel Arc Pro B60 with `attention_backend=FLASH_ATTN_MLA`:

- TP=2, `dtype=bfloat16`, `max_model_len=4096`, `enforce_eager=True`:
  - GSM8K (5-shot): `exact_match,strict-match` = 0.3723, `exact_match,flexible-extract` = 0.3783
  - MMLU: overall `acc` = 0.5895 ± 0.0277 (humanities 0.5846, other 0.5538, social_sciences 0.7667, stem 0.5053)
- DeepSeek-V2-Lite GSM8K with `ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASH_ATTN_MLA`, TP=4, `APPLY_CHAT_TEMPLATE=0`, `NUM_FEWSHOT=5`, `MAX_MODEL_LEN=2048` completed successfully; 300-sample result was strict-match 0.3800 / flexible-extract 0.3833, consistent with the base model's expected GSM8K range.

Both are consistent with DeepSeek-V2-Lite's published reference numbers.

title: [ROCm][DSv4][Perf] Use the shared prefill chunk plan in the ROCm sparse prefill
body:
## Purpose

`DeepseekV4ROCMAiterMLAAttention._forward_prefill` splits prefill requests into fixed groups of `PREFILL_CHUNK_SIZE = 4` and sizes the bf16 gather workspace from the static worst case (`N = ceil(max_model_len / compress_ratio)`, `M = N + window_size + max_num_batched_tokens`). The NVIDIA FlashMLA path already uses `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadata.get_prefill_chunk_plan()` (#45061), which packs requests by workspace area and returns each chunk's real widths.

This PR drives the ROCm prefill loop from the same plan. The loop allocates the workspace per chunk as `(chunk_size, chunk_M, head_dim)` and passes `chunk_N` / `chunk_M` to the SWA gather and `combine_topk_swa_indices`, matching the NVIDIA V4 path. Steps with more than 4 prefill requests now run as fewer, larger chunks. Peak memory is unchanged: the plan's area bound equals the worst case that `forward_mqa()` already reserves during warmup. Decode is unchanged, and steps with at most 4 prefills still run as a single chunk.

`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py` has the same loop and is not changed here.

## Test Plan

MI355X (gfx950), TP=1, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, main `4fb767ff0a`.

- Micro: time `_forward_prefill` on live model inputs for main vs. this PR, in interleaved blocks within one process. Each scenario is one prefill step, summed over 43 layers.
- e2e: a fresh server per run, 4 runs per arm per block with the first discarded, one server on the host at a time.

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 65536 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 307 --random-output-len 23 --random-range-ratio 0.25 \
    --num-prompts 1021 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1234
```

- Accuracy: `lm_eval --model vllm --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto`, greedy, `max_model_len=4096`, `seed=1234`. The base arm was run twice.

## Test Result

**Micro** (median of 3 runs; noise floor ≤ 1.1 %):

| prefill step | chunks main → PR | main (ms) | PR (ms) | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 × 11777 tokens | 1 → 1 | 84.6 | 84.8 | −0.2 % |
| 7 × 400–1800 | 2 → 1 | 43.6 | 40.5 | +7.8 % |
| 13 × 700–1100 | 4 → 1 | 70.5 | 58.5 | +20.9 % |
| 29 × 170–430 | 8 → 1 | 67.5 | 41.4 | +63 % |
| 53 × 90–250 | 14 → 1 | 105.0 | 37.7 | +182 % |

On gfx950, part of the gain comes from larger chunks crossing the 1024-query threshold that sends them to AITER OPUS (#54855). With routing pinned to Triton, the gains are +3.9 / +5.0 / +17 / +62 %, and outputs are bit-identical.

**e2e**, 1021 prompts in 307 / out 23 (9 base / 7 patched warm runs, ranges disjoint):

| metric | main | PR | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total tok/s | 27218 | 29075 | +6.8 % |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 5812 | 5401 | −7.1 % |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 5706 | 5328 | −6.6 % |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 272.6 | 254.9 | −6.5 % |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 275.8 | 256.5 | −7.0 % |

No regression under `--max-concurrency` 96, 48 and 3 (Δ of medians, PR vs main):

| workload | warm runs | Total tok/s | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | Mean TPOT | Median TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

**GSM8K** (strict-match):

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Enable FlashInfer mm-prefix attention
body:
## Purpose

This keeps multimodal PrefixLM batches on the native FlashInfer backend. It is the vLLM adapter for FlashInfer's mm-prefix batch-prefill wrapper: it builds per-query `[start, end]` rows from request metadata, decides when the path is eligible, and calls the wrapper, whose attention variant evaluates `(causal AND sliding_window) OR mm_prefix` on every KV tile. No `O(qo_len * kv_len)` mask is materialized; the ranges are one `int32 (N, 2)` buffer sized by scheduled tokens, 128 KiB at 16384 tokens. The prefill still traverses the full rectangle, so the gain is memory, not FLOPs.

The wrapper comes from FlashInfer PR 5189, merged into FlashInfer main on September 18. It is not in FlashInfer 0.7.0, which main pins, so until the next FlashInfer release and pin bump `supports_mm_prefix()` returns `False` and this backend is demoted before selection. FlashInfer builds the variant's JIT module when the wrapper is constructed.

On SM100, `FLASHINFER` is offered ahead of the `TRITON_FLASHINFER` composite for mm-prefix batches, and the composite stays the fallback for what FlashInfer rejects: FP8, `nvfp4_4over6`, NVFP4 on SM100, sinks, DCP, `logits_soft_cap`, forced trtllm-gen and page sizes of 128 and above. The ubatch split now carries `mm_req_doc_ranges`, re-keyed to local request indices, and `is_prefilling`, so a short chunked-prefill tail inside a range stays a prefill. The `validate_configuration` override forwards `use_rswa`; without it, selection through this backend raises `TypeError`.

#47118 also enables FlashInfer for Gemma 4 multimodal models, but only for text-only requests; this PR serves the mm-prefix batches.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mm_prefix.py tests/v1/attention/test_attention_splitting.py tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py -k mm_prefix -rs
PYTHONPATH=/path/to/flashinfer-main pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mm_prefix.py -k flashinfer -rs
```

## Test Result

The CPU tests pass, and breaking each check they cover (the KV dtype, NVFP4-on-SM100, sink, page-size and wrapper-availability rejections, DCP, `use_rswa` forwarding, block-size advertising, and ubatch re-keying and slicing) fails the matching case. The GPU tests compare builder, impl and wrapper against a dense float32 reference on paged KV, with a sliding window narrower than the widest range so both window formulas are checked, and they cover the causal fallback, text-only and decode-only gating, short-extend reclassification and fail-fast on soft-cap and forced trtllm-gen. They need a FlashInfer build that carries the wrapper; on sm_80 they passed on the previous revision (45 passed, 22 hardware skips) and were not rerun for this one. pre-commit passes.

<details>
<summary>Historical serving measurements from the earlier in-tree variant</summary>

These results are historical context, not validation of the current wrapper-based adapter. They were measured with the former in-tree variant on a tree that also carried persistent attention-workspace profiling. That profiling code is not part of this PR, and the measurements have not been repeated against this revision.

Run on 2 SM80 devices, `-tp 2`, BF16 weights and KV, a 31B multimodal model, `--max-model-len 8192`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, `--max-num-seqs 128`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`. FlashInfer carried the mm-prefix batches end to end; a single 896x896 image request completed successfully, and no workspace or KV-cache assertion fired. The same-host comparison against the `TRITON_ATTN` baseline used the image workload definition and seeds from the composite PR's repro block: an 896x896 image plus a configured 1024-token text input and 1024-token output, with multimodal expansion producing 1295-1297 measured input tokens, `--temperature 0 --ignore-eos`, and prefix and mm caches reset between runs. The server configurations differ in attention backend, block size, and available KV capacity, so this compares complete serving configurations rather than isolating the mm-prefix kernel. **This is not a reproduction of that PR's numbers** — different architecture and parallelism, so only the within-host results are meaningful.

Values are `TRITON_ATTN / FLASHINFER`, **bold is better** (higher tok/s, lower latency):

| Conc | Total tok/s | Output tok/s | TTFT (ms) | TPOT (ms) | E2EL (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 14.2 / **58.5** | 6.3 / **25.8** | 3884 / **2167** | 155.4 / **36.6** | 162860 / **39652** |
| 32 | **437.8** / 426.7 | **193.3** / 188.4 | 31441 / **30559** | **134.9** / 140.1 | **169446** / 173846 |
| 128 | 416.2 / **438.0** | 183.7 / **193.4** | 280114 / **275765** | **186.1** / 190.2 | 470526 / **470314** |

Caveats, so the table is not read for more than it says:

- The concurrency-32 FlashInfer figure is the mean of three seeds (10032/10033/10034: 426.6 / 427.0 / 426.7, spread 0.09%). The `TRITON_ATTN` figure on that row is a **single seed**, so its 2.6% lead carries an unmeasured seed-variance error bar and should not be read as a real difference. Concurrency 1 and 128 are single-seed on both sides.
- At concurrency 32, the measured inputs are 1295-1297 tokens with 1024 output tokens, putting the maximum full-request footprint at approximately 74K tokens, above either KV budget; concurrency 128 is more constrained. Scheduling and cache pressure can therefore affect these rows, and they do not isolate attention-kernel cost.
- The two arms do not get identical KV budgets: FlashInfer reserves its attention workspace during profiling and lands at 49,593 tokens against the baseline's 51,515. The FlashInfer configuration is therefore measured with approximately 3.7% less KV capacity.

</details>

title: [Metrics] Expose cached prompt tokens by cache tier
body:
## Changes

- Adds `vllm:prompt_tokens_cached_by_source_total{source}` with `source` in `device`, `host`, `p2p`, `disk`, `external_unspecified`. All five series initialize at zero.
- Counted at admission. Invariant: `sum(source) == vllm:prefix_cache_hits + vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits`. `device` equals `vllm:prefix_cache_hits`.
- Scheduler change is 10 lines at the existing `connector_prefix_cache_stats.record(...)` call, which already runs after `update_state_after_alloc` with the accepted hit count and already excludes preempted re-admissions. `prefill_stats.set` stays where main has it.
- `PrefixCacheStats` gains a typed `hits_by_source: CachedTokensBySource`. `PrefillStats`, `PromptTokenStats` and their wire format are unchanged from main.
- Connector contract: `get_external_cache_hit_sources(request, n) -> CachedTokensBySource`, unordered counts summing to `n`. A miscount is reported as `external_unspecified` with a one-time warning instead of asserting.
- Connector mappings: NIXL, Mooncake transfer, MoRIIO: `p2p`. Mooncake Store and other uninstrumented connectors: `external_unspecified`. Simple offload: `host` or `disk`. MultiConnector delegates to the connector that served the request.
- Native offloading attributes each token range to the tier of the keys loaded for it. On hybrid models a token needs every KV group, so when groups disagree the outermost tier (farthest from the accelerator) is reported. `CacheHitSource` is declared in offload order and exposes `outermost()`. Tokens no loaded key covers are `external_unspecified`. Promotion origin is kept per request so a disk or P2P hit staged into host memory is not relabeled `host`.
- Secondary tier default derives from `Medium`: CPU is `host`, STORAGE is `disk`; P2P sets its own.
- Rust frontend decodes the new `PrefixCacheStats` field and emits the same counter. Per-source handles are created lazily like the other request metrics.

Closes vllm-project/vllm#53368.

## Changes since the first review

Per @robertgshaw2-redhat's review: single source of truth, one write site, minimal scheduler surface.

- Attribution moved from `PrefillStats` to the scheduler's existing admission-time prefix-cache record. The moved `prefill_stats.set`, the ordered source segments and the `PrefillStats` wire change are gone.
- Dropped the failure-path truncation in `_update_requests_with_invalid_blocks`. It changed `prompt_tokens_cached_total`, `prompt_tokens_by_source_total{external_kv_transfer}` and the OpenAI `cached_tokens` field on partial KV load failure. Parity with main is kept; a fix for all affected counters belongs in its own PR.
- Typed `CachedTokensBySource` instead of a dict; `EXTERNAL_UNSPECIFIED`; enum moved under `kv_connector`.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 3,600-second AIPerf AgentX sweeps, evaluations disabled. AIPerf scraped Prometheus. Artifacts include JSON/CSV metrics and request logs.

- [B200 — passed](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34420875287): [DRAM c8](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34420875287/artifacts/10133753012), [Simple NVMe c14](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34420875287/artifacts/10133728096), [native DRAM+NVMe c14](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34420875287/artifacts/10133870624).

Those sweeps ran the first design and exercised the connector-side attribution paths this PR keeps. In the native DRAM+NVMe run, ranges where KV groups disagreed were about 2% of external hits. Not yet rerun on GPU since the admission-time change.

B200 included separate backend backports [#55712](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55712) and [#50014](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50014). P2P: 1,740 completed requests, zero request errors, 435 drain-deadline cancellations.

Locally: stats, tiering, Mooncake Store, NIXL offload, multi-connector, load-failure recovery and connector-level attribution tests pass; Rust tests across `vllm-engine-core-client`, `vllm-metrics`, `vllm-llm` pass with clippy clean. Scheduler-level tests rely on CI.

title: [Perf][MoE] Use fused MiniMax2 routing with non-unit routed scaling
body:
## Purpose

`get_routing_method_type` maps sigmoid + correction bias + renormalize routing (no expert groups) to `RoutingMethodType.MiniMax2` only when `routed_scaling_factor` is 1.0 (added in #44347). MiniMax-M3 uses `routed_scaling_factor=2.0`, so its MoE falls back to `Unspecified`. On SM100 with the MXFP8 checkpoint, that means the modular TRT-LLM path: a separate vLLM `topk_sigmoid` launch per MoE layer, then `trtllm_fp8_block_scale_routed_moe`.

The restriction is no longer needed with the pinned FlashInfer 0.7.0:
- FlashInfer's MiniMax2 routing uses `routed_scaling_factor` as its route scale: final weight = `sigmoid(x) * routeScale / sum` (`trtllm_fused_moe_routing_runner.cu`: `routingData.mRouteScale = routedScalingFactor`).
- Every monolithic TRT-LLM caller that accepts MiniMax2 already passes `routed_scaling_factor` through: FP8 block scale / MXFP8, FP8 per-tensor, and NVFP4.
- The scale is not applied twice. When `apply_routed_scale_to_output` is false, which is the M3 case, the scale goes to the router and the runner gets 1.0.

This PR removes the restriction, and with it the now-unused `routed_scaling_factor` argument of `get_routing_method_type`.

The restriction also, by accident, kept zero-expert models (`ZeroExpertRouter`) off kernels with built-in routing whenever their scale was not 1.0. Those kernels cannot reproduce zero-expert handling, and with scale 1.0 such a model was already mapped to MiniMax2. `ZeroExpertRouter.routing_method_type` now returns `Unspecified` explicitly.

Effect: any model with sigmoid + bias + renormalize routing, no expert groups, and a non-unit scale becomes eligible for the monolithic TRT-LLM kernels on Blackwell. MiniMax-M3 is one such model. The routing semantics are the same as vLLM's `fused_topk_bias`: biased scores select the experts, unbiased sigmoid gives the weights, which are renormalized and scaled.

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs for `MiniMax2 routed_scaling_factor`, `MiniMax-M3 routing trtllm`, `minimax m3 moe routing fused` and `RoutingMethodType MiniMax2`. Nothing touches this mapping. The related merged PRs are #39141 and #44347, and #44347 introduced the restriction.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Routing-method unit tests (new: MiniMax2 with scale 2.0, zero-expert -> Unspecified)
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py -k "routing or degenerate or grouped or zero or minimax"
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py -k routing_method

# New GPU test (SM100): monolithic MXFP8 TRT-LLM with fused MiniMax2 routing and
# routed_scaling_factor=2.0 vs modular TRT-LLM with vLLM fused_topk_bias routing
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py -k "minimax2_routing or deferred_finalize"

# End to end, MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, TP4 on 4x GB300, this branch vs main
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 -tp 4 --max-model-len 8192
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 \
    --ignore-eos --max-concurrency {1,8} --num-prompts {16,128}
```

## Test Result

**Unit tests:**
- `test_routing.py`: 507 passed.
- The routing-method test in `test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py` passed.
- `test_flashinfer.py -k "minimax2_routing or deferred_finalize"`: 6 passed on GB300.
- Both new routing tests fail without the source change.
- The new FlashInfer test fails if the fused path ignores the scale: about 80% of elements mismatch, with a max abs diff of 0.39.
- pre-commit passes.

**Backend actually selected** (server log, MiniMax-M3-MXFP8):
- main: `Using MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPModular`
- this PR: `Using MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPMonolithic`

**Kernel level** (GB300, M3 MoE shapes: H=6144, 128 experts, top-4, MXFP8, 57 MoE layers captured in one CUDA graph; µs per layer):

| tokens | TP4 (I=768): separate top-k | TP4: fused | TP1 (I=3072): separate top-k | TP1: fused |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 17.00 | 15.40 | 48.06 | 46.11 |
| 4 | 44.92 | 42.91 | 118.65 | 117.33 |
| 16 | 88.79 | 86.97 | 271.33 | 269.70 |
| 32 | 115.48 | 113.79 | 408.86 | 406.99 |
| 64 | 146.34 | 146.31 | 548.63 | 546.83 |
| 256 | 219.59 | 219.56 | 852.83 | 851.90 |

Fusing the routing saves about 1.3–2 µs per MoE layer at decode batch sizes. At TP4 that is 91–115 µs per decode step for ≤32 tokens, and about 9% of the MoE time at batch 1. The max relative difference between the two outputs is 4–6e-3.

**End to end, MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, TP4, 4x GB300:**

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| TPOT, concurrency 1 | 4.14 ms | 3.96 ms (-4.3%) |
| Output throughput, concurrency 1 | 233.0 tok/s | 243.5 tok/s (+4.5%) |
| TPOT, concurrency 8 | 7.37 ms | 7.18 ms (-2.6%) |
| Output throughput, concurrency 8 | 942.9 tok/s | 966.2 tok/s (+2.5%) |
| GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 questions | 0.861 / 0.851 / 0.862 / 0.847 (mean 0.855) | 0.853 / 0.861 / 0.852 / 0.860 (mean 0.857) |

The eval is greedy, and each version was run 4 times (4 separate runs, 2 server launches). The spread comes from batch nondeterminism: 1.5 points on main, 0.9 points with this PR. The means match.

**AI assistance:** Claude Code was used for the investigation, the implementation, the tests and the benchmarks. All results above come from runs on 4x GB300.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Fix partial-tail offload for hybrid models (and under DCP)
body:
> **Superseded.** Split per @orozery's review into two PRs: **#58618** (lookup anchor) and **#58619** (DCP store guard + per-group addressing, longest-boundary only). A third, #58620 (store every boundary), was closed after hardware showed no benefit. This PR will be closed once both are in review; the description below is kept for the original analysis and the K3 TP8/DCP8 hardware table.

## Purpose

`OffloadingConnector` never yields a CPU-tier hit for a **hybrid model** (recurrent/SSM groups
alongside full-attention groups) once the prompt is longer than one full-attention chunk. Reuse
reads 0 regardless of how large the CPU pool is.

There are two independent causes. Both are required for the tier to work at all, so they are in
two separate commits.

### 1. Store — partial tails are disabled under DCP, and the store path mis-addresses groups

`supports_partial_tail` required `len(group_block_sizes) == 1` **and**
`decode_context_parallel_size == 1`. Under DCP the full-attention offload block is `dcp ×` the
attention block while recurrent blocks stay unsharded (12288 vs 1536 at DCP 8 — attention groups
are scaled by DCP in `build_offloading_config`/`resolve_dcp_kv_block_size`, `MambaManager.__init__`
explicitly undoes the scaling for recurrent state). Both conditions fail, so the feature is off.

The store path also addressed every group with a single shared physical block index
(`boundary // self._partial_tail_block_size`), which is wrong once block sizes differ, and
`_partial_tail_block_size` was read from `kv_group_configs[0]`, which need not be the
full-attention group.

Fix: allow mixed block sizes when every recurrent block divides the full-attention block,
recurrent blocks are hash-aligned, and hash boundaries split evenly across DCP ranks; address each
group's source block in its own block size; take the window from the full-attention group
explicitly (`partial_tail_window`).

At `dcp == 1` the scale factor is 1, so the guard change is a no-op and the store path resolves to
the same single block index as before.

### 2. Lookup — the search is anchored on a boundary recurrent groups never have

`_lookup` anchored the partial-tail search on `_lookup_complete_chunks`, which requires *every*
group to have a complete chunk at the boundary — including recurrent groups that by construction
hold no state there. The `align` manager CoW-copies its state at the producing prompt's last hash
boundary, which is essentially never a full-attention chunk multiple. So the anchor is 0, the
search is capped at one window from zero, and a correctly stored tail further out is never probed
even though it is resident.

**This half is independent of DCP** and affects every hybrid + `OffloadingConnector` deployment.

Instrumented `_lookup` on a replay, before the change (chunk 12288, hash 128):

```
n=12620  complete_hit=12288  complete_boundary=12288  max_boundary=12544
           boundary=12544 ALL GROUPS HIT                  <- restores
n=15136  complete_hit=0      complete_boundary=0      max_boundary=12160
           boundary=12160 group=0 MISS ... 11776 MISS     <- tail stored at 15104,
                                                            never probed
```

Fix: anchor on the full-attention complete prefix and check recurrent groups only at the candidate
boundary. The anchor honours the same `max_num_new_tokens` / `max_load_tokens` caps as the
complete-chunk lookup, and only chunks verified resident are requested, so the load path cannot
fetch an unverified chunk.

The returned boundary is always strictly greater than the complete-chunk hit, so the change is
additive: it can only widen what a lookup reports, never shrink it. That is also the argument that
it cannot regress an existing deployment.

## Test Plan

New unit coverage in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py`, on a
DCP-shaped hybrid fixture (full-attention offload block = `dcp × attention block` = 32, unsharded
16-token Mamba block, hash 4) — the same shape as 12288 vs 1536 at DCP 8:

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ -q
```

- 3 store tests: the guard accepts mixed block sizes under DCP and still rejects DCP-indivisible
  hashes, EAGLE, and a recurrent block that does not divide the full-attention block; the store
  addresses each group in its own block size; an aligned boundary still goes to the aligned path.
- 7 lookup tests: the tail is found with no recurrent state at the chunk boundary; 0 when no tail
  was stored; 0 when the full-attention chunks are not resident; the tail is preferred over an
  aligned recurrent state; deferral while the anchor chunk is loading; a recurrent state is still
  required at the candidate boundary; and the load path addresses each group correctly.

Hardware validation was done on a 2-node GB300 deployment of a KDA + MLA hybrid at TP8/DCP8 with a
deliberately small 16 GiB CPU pool, using per-prompt isolated trials with a GPU-only prefix-cache
reset between store and replay and a reference run asserted cold (`cached == 0`), so the
comparison is CPU-restore vs full recompute rather than restore vs restore.

## Test Result

Unit suite, run against this branch and against its merge base on a CPU-only host:

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| this branch (`eddff35`) | **100 failed, 354 passed**, 2 skipped |
| baseline (`6ca2b23`, merge base) | **100 failed, 344 passed**, 2 skipped |

The failure sets are byte-identical (`diff` of the sorted `FAILED` lines is empty): **no
regressions, and the 10 added tests account for the entire +10 in passes.** All 100 pre-existing
failures share one signature and are an artifact of running on a host without a GPU:

```
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for VllmConfig
  Value error, Hybrid KV cache manager was explicitly enabled but is not
  supported in this configuration.
```

Hardware result (KDA + MLA, TP8/DCP8, 2 × GB300, 16 GiB CPU pool), tokens restored from the CPU
tier, gated on `vllm:kv_offload_load_tokens_sum` rather than `cached_tokens` (the latter cannot
distinguish an HBM hit from a CPU restore):

| prompt tail | partial tail | unpatched | store fix only | store + lookup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12544 | 256 | 12288 | 12544 | 12544 |
| 13824 | 1536 | 0 | 0 | 13824 |
| 15104 | 2816 | 0 | 0 | 15104 |
| 24064 | 11776 | 0 | 0 | 24064 |
| 24960 | 384 (2 chunks) | 0 | 0 | 24960 |

Restored greedy output is byte-identical to a full recompute in all 9 sizes tested, with partial
tails from 128 to 12032 tokens.

## Notes for reviewers

- **`dcp == 1` is untested on hardware.** That is the default upstream configuration. The
  store-side guard change is a no-op there by construction (the scaling factor is 1), and the unit
  tests cover the existing `dcp == 1` paths, but nothing was measured on a device.
- **Only one hybrid architecture was exercised** (KDA + MLA). Mamba/SSM + full attention should
  behave identically by the same code path, but was not run.
- **EAGLE/MTP remains excluded** by the guard (volatile draft tail) and is untested.
- The lookup fix adds a second `manager.lookup()` pass over the full-attention groups when
  recurrent groups are present. `record_lookup` is idempotent, so no duplicate KV events are
  emitted, but it is extra probe work on the hybrid path. Happy to gate it more tightly if you
  would prefer.
- Related prior work on the sibling connector: #52832 fixed the analogous producer-partial-tail
  gap for Mooncake.
- Two further changes exist on our side but are deliberately **not** in this PR, as they are pool
  efficiency rather than correctness: skipping aligned recurrent stores whose boundary is not a
  full-attention chunk multiple (unreachable rows), and a `min_partial_tail_tokens` knob. Happy to
  send either as a follow-up if they are wanted.

title: [MRV2][PP] Prototype deferred sampled-result receives
body:
## Purpose

Related to #53810.

On non-last pipeline-parallel stages, sampled-result receives are currently
posted as soon as their buffers are allocated, although the results are not
consumed until a later scheduler step. For small broadcasts, the receiver-side
NCCL kernel can remain resident while model kernels execute.

This change delays those receives on CUDA Model Runner V2 workers until the
last safe pipeline step and places them after that step's model work. The last
PP rank remains the immediate broadcast source. A result produced at step `T`
is still consumed at `T + PP`; only the receiver launch moves.

## Activation and scope

The behavior is automatic when all of these are true:

- Model Runner V2 is active;
- async scheduling is enabled;
- pipeline parallel size is greater than one; and
- the platform is CUDA.

Synchronous scheduling, CPU, ROCm, and single-stage execution retain immediate
receive posting. There are no environment-variable gates. `async_scheduling`
is resolved from `None` to a concrete boolean during `VllmConfig` validation,
before `PPHandler` is constructed.

## Correctness and lifecycle guarantees

- Warmup retains immediate collective timing; receive deferral starts only
  after warmup finishes.
- Sampled tokens, sample/rejection counts, and speculative draft tokens retain
  FIFO collective order.
- The sender stays immediate to avoid a cycle with inter-stage activation
  traffic. Its broadcasts are serialized on one dedicated stream; receiver
  deferral can leave the head send waiting, but does not make all queued sends
  simultaneously resident.
- A consume-time fallback posts any receive that missed its scheduled launch.
- Pending receives are flushed at PP-group-uniform idle, shutdown, and
  pause/sleep boundaries before device synchronization. The zero-token worker
  flush and model-runner launch are intentionally redundant: the latter also
  protects direct runner invocations.
- CPU stream placeholders use an explicit `launched` flag because their event
  recording is a no-op.
- PP-only post-update kernels are warmed before serving, including Mamba's
  sampled-count scatter and align-state fused postprocess specialization. The
  warmup uses an all-`-1` request mapping; both kernels return before any
  persistent-state load/store, and a CUDA regression test checks that the
  bookkeeping and recurrent-state buffers remain unchanged.

## Sender-side validation envelope

The H100 W1 runs used CUDA 13.3 and NCCL 2.30.7 with TP8/PP4, concurrency 710,
and no speculative draft tokens. The two per-step broadcasts were about 5.7
KiB each. NCCL protocol selection was left automatic and was not printed by
the logs, so this PR does not claim a specific LL/LL128/Simple protocol or a
validated payload-size cutoff. Larger speculative payloads retain the same
ordering and flush invariants in tests, but still need hardware performance
validation.

## Validation

Focused tests cover receive cadence, immediate/deferred launch idempotency,
FIFO recovery, speculative draft propagation, idle flushing, CPU no-op events,
warmup specialization and state neutrality, and pause-before-synchronize
ordering.

A matched same-base H100 TP8/PP4 A/B was run on the current PR head with 4,000
requests, 615 input tokens, 130 output tokens, concurrency 710, and isolated
cold caches. Both arms completed 4,000/4,000 requests with zero failures:

| Receive mode | Output tok/s | Total tok/s | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Forced immediate after warmup | 2,431.4 | 13,933.9 | 5,622.0 ms | 245.8 ms |
| Automatic deferred (this PR) | 3,368.2 | 19,302.1 | 3,303.8 ms | 182.5 ms |

Automatic deferral improved output and total throughput by **38.5%**, reduced
mean TTFT by 41.2%, and reduced mean TPOT by 25.7%. The deferred run had no
errors, tracebacks, NCCL warnings, or CUDA errors. This run also exercised the
immediate last-rank sender under the validated payload envelope without a hang
or observed throughput regression.

AI assistance was used to analyze failures and prepare the changes; the final
implementation and results should be reviewed by the author.

title: [Bugfix] Use original context length for mRoPE YaRN correction range
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58870.

`MRotaryEmbedding` enlarges `max_position_embeddings` 4x as cos/sin cache headroom (for Qwen2.5-VL video positions) and passes the enlarged value to the base class. For YaRN it borrows `YaRNScalingRotaryEmbedding._compute_inv_freq`, which reads `self.max_position_embeddings` as the *original* context length for `yarn_find_correction_range`. So every mRoPE + YaRN model (Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5 with YaRN enabled) computes its correction range from 4x the original length, and the interpolation ramp no longer matches Transformers (`_compute_yarn_parameters` uses `original_max_position_embeddings`).

For the config in the issue, the ramp moves from (14, 22) to (16, 24) and 9 of 32 inverse frequencies differ from HF by up to 37.5%. Plain YaRN (no `mrope_section`) is unaffected and already matches HF exactly.

The fix records the original length as `original_max_position_embeddings`, the name `Phi3LongRoPEScaledRotaryEmbedding` already uses, and has YaRN's correction range read it:

- `YaRNScalingRotaryEmbedding` sets it to `max_position_embeddings`, so plain YaRN behaves exactly as before.
- `MRotaryEmbedding` sets it before applying the 4x headroom.

The cache size is deliberately unchanged. The 4x headroom is documented as intentional for Qwen2.5-VL video positions, and shrinking it is a separate question from the frequency mismatch.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR references #58870. #53964 (request-static YaRN profiles for mRoPE) also touches `MRotaryEmbedding`, but it keeps taking the correction range from the enlarged length, so it doesn't fix this.

## Test Plan

```bash
# New regression test: vLLM's mRoPE + YaRN cos/sin cache vs. Transformers' YaRN frequencies
pytest tests/kernels/core/test_mrope.py -k yarn

# Surrounding suites
pytest tests/kernels/core/test_mrope.py tests/kernels/core/test_pos_encoding.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_bailing_mrope.py tests/model_executor/test_ernie45_vl_mrope.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_keye_mrope.py tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_vl_mrope.py \
  tests/transformers_utils/test_config.py tests/test_config.py

pre-commit run --files <changed files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed files>
```

Plus the reproducer from #58870, and a model eval: prompt log-probabilities of `Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct` with YaRN enabled (`hf_overrides={"text_config": {"rope_parameters": {"rope_type": "yarn", "factor": 4.0, "original_max_position_embeddings": 32768, "rope_theta": 1e6, "mrope_section": [16, 24, 24]}}}`), bf16, 4 prompts × 3,500 tokens of vLLM docs, compared token by token against Transformers 5.17.0 with the same `rope_parameters`. I checked that the Transformers side actually applies YaRN: its rotary `inv_freq` equals `ROPE_INIT_FUNCTIONS["yarn"]` and `attention_scaling` is 1.1386.

## Test Result

**Regression test:** passes with this change. On `main` both cases fail: 26.7% and 35.6% of the cos/sin cache entries differ from Transformers, by up to 0.197 and 1.62.

**Reproducer from the issue:** on `main`, 9 of 32 inverse frequencies differ from HF. With this change there are none. The cache stays at 2,621,440 rows, and plain YaRN is unchanged (still exact vs. HF, 655,360 rows).

**Suites:** 950 passed, 6 skipped, 20 failed. The same 20 fail on unpatched `main` on this machine: 16 `test_rotary_embedding` bf16 cases with 8,192 tokens hit CUDA OOM on a 6 GB GPU, and 4 config tests need gated `meta-llama` repos. pre-commit and the manual mypy hook pass.

**Model eval:** mean |Δ logprob| vs. Transformers, and top-1 agreement:

| positions | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1–1000 | 0.0389 | 0.0271 |
| 1000–2000 | 0.0497 | 0.0250 |
| 2000–3000 | 0.0596 | 0.0261 |
| 3000–3500 | 0.0680 | 0.0268 |
| **all** | **0.0521** (97.0% top-1) | **0.0262** (98.3% top-1) |

On `main` the gap to Transformers grows with position, as expected from a wrong interpolation ramp. With this change it stays flat at the bf16 noise level. Tokens after position 3,500 were not measured (6 GB GPU).

---

AI assistance was used for this change (analysis, code and this description). The reproduction, tests and eval above were run locally on an RTX 4050 Laptop GPU (6 GB).

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Apply the model's transcription post-processing on the realtime path
body:
## Purpose

The REST transcription endpoints run model output through `post_process_output()` /
`get_streaming_post_processor_cls()`, so models with a structured output format return clean text. The `/v1/realtime`
WebSocket path forwards `output.outputs[0].text` verbatim. For Qwen3-ASR every 5 s segment is a separate generation
that starts with a `language Chinese<asr_text>` header, so realtime clients receive

```
language Chinese<asr_text>今天天气很好language Chinese<asr_text>我们去公园
```

instead of the transcript (the "raw format leaks" part of #35767).

Changes:

- `RealtimeConnection._run_generation` feeds each delta through a streaming post-processor and starts a fresh one at

Related PRs: #49658 also applies the streaming post-processor in `connection.py`, but with a single instance for the

`language Chinese` prefix is emitted again. #51037 strips the header with a private `rsplit("<asr_text>")` helper as

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Decline CUTLASS int8 w8a8 on SM100+ so Triton fallback is reachable
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #54311. `CutlassInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel.is_supported()` takes `compute_capability` but ignores it and always returns `True` on CUDA. So CUTLASS claims every int8 w8a8 layer — but the SM100/SM120 dispatchers wire the int8 func as `nullptr` (`scaled_mm_c3x_sm120.cu`: `nullptr, // int8 not supported on SM120`, same on `sm100`), so the C++ hard-errors at runtime:

```
Int8 not supported on SM121. Use FP8 quantization instead, or run on older arch (SM < 100).
```

The working `TritonInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel` — next in `_POSSIBLE_INT8_KERNELS[CUDA]` — never gets a chance.

## Fix

Decline in `is_supported()` when `compute_capability >= 100` (SM100/SM120/SM121 Blackwell; CUTLASS int8 is only wired for SM < 100), mirroring the sibling `AiterInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel`'s capability guard. Kernel selection then falls through to `TritonInt8`, which overrides `is_supported()` and supports these arches. FP8 is unaffected (SM120 wires the fp8 func).

## Verified on a GB10 (sm_121)

```
CutlassInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel.is_supported(121)
  -> (False, 'CUTLASS int8 w8a8 is not supported on SM100+ (Blackwell); use the Triton int8 kernel.')
TritonInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel.is_supported(121) -> (True, None)
_POSSIBLE_INT8_KERNELS[CUDA] == [Cutlass, Triton, Humming]  # Triton now reachable
```

## Tests

Device-free (`tests/model_executor/kernels/test_cutlass_int8_sm_gate.py`): declines on SM100/120/121, stays supported on SM90/89/80/75, and `compute_capability=None` stays supported (back-compat).

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Reuse prefill main-KV gathers across decoder groups
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 decoder CSA2 groups currently dequantize and gather the same compressed main-KV prefix into a BF16 prefill workspace once per layer, although the four layers share one KV source. This change adds an opt-in, model-owned BF16 buffer with a strict 0–512 MiB budget: the first eligible layer gathers main-KV, its three followers reuse that exact region while each refreshes its own SWA region, and the next group or forward repopulates the buffer. The initial gate covers one-request FlashMLA prefill without DBO, PCP, DCP, or sequence parallelism; unsupported shapes and over-budget gathers use the existing path. It preserves the packed cache format, logical selections, and BF16 attention input. 

This does not duplicate #42504, which adds a single sparse-gather primitive without cross-layer reuse, or #56752, which trims decoder rows and changes the cold-prefill output contract; #54592 targets a quantized DeepSeek-V4 prefill kernel rather than exact DeepSeek-V4.1 BF16 group reuse.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Enable partial-tail offload for hybrid models under DCP
body:
## Purpose

Split out of #57216 per @orozery's review (part 2 of 2): the DCP store guard and per-group addressing, with the `-1` squashed in and `alignment_tokens` reused.

`supports_partial_tail` required `len(group_block_sizes) == 1` **and** `decode_context_parallel_size == 1`. Under DCP the full-attention offload block is `dcp ×` the attention block while recurrent blocks stay unsharded (12288 vs 1536 at DCP 8 — attention groups are scaled in `build_offloading_config` / `resolve_dcp_kv_block_size`, `MambaManager.__init__` undoes the scaling for recurrent state). Both conditions fail, so the feature is off for every hybrid model under DCP.

The store path also addressed every group with one shared physical block index (`boundary // self._partial_tail_block_size`), which is wrong once block sizes differ, and read that block size from `kv_group_configs[0]`, which need not be the full-attention group.

Fix:
- Allow mixed block sizes when every recurrent block divides the full-attention block and is hash-aligned, and hash boundaries split evenly across DCP ranks. The window a tail can lie in is the full-attention offload block, which `SchedulerOffloadConfig.alignment_tokens` already holds — no new field.
- Address each group's source block in its own block size, as the block that *ends* at the boundary: `(boundary - 1) // tokens_per_block`. The old `boundary // tokens_per_block` pointed at the *next* block when the boundary lands on a group's block edge (inert today because `block_indices` is unused on the worker at `blocks_per_chunk == 1`, but wrong the moment that stops holding).
- A hand-off drains every `align` manager for the step, so it can carry more than one boundary (e.g. the last full recurrent block next to the prompt tail, `MambaManager.cache_blocks`). At dcp == 1 the extra ones are full-attention multiples and get filtered. Under DCP they are not, and the existing `assert len(boundaries) == 1` would take the engine core down (see the unit reproducer below). Keep only the longest boundary, which is the tail a consumer's descending probe reaches first. Storing every boundary was proposed separately (#58620) and closed: on hardware, boundaries arrived in separate hand-offs, so longest-only already stored each pair and a consumer diverging before the tail still resumed at the earlier boundary.

At `dcp == 1` the scaling factor is 1, so the guard change is a no-op and the store path resolves to the same single block index as before.

## Test Plan

On a DCP-shaped hybrid fixture (full-attention offload block = `dcp x attention block` = 32, unsharded 16-token Mamba block, hash 4 -- the same shape as 12288 vs 1536 at DCP 8):

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ -q
```

Fail on `main`, pass here:
- the guard accepts mixed block sizes under DCP (window 32) and still rejects a DCP-indivisible hash, EAGLE, and a recurrent block that does not divide the full-attention block; at `dcp == 1` it is unchanged (window 16)
- the store addresses each group in its own block size, fences both source blocks, and the self-describing event covers only the valid prefix of the partial block
- **crash reproducer**: a two-boundary request-end hand-off `[(1, 24, 48), (1, 25, 56)]` asserts on the previous code; now the aligned path stores the recurrent row at 48 and the partial path exactly one pair, at 56
- block index for a boundary in the first block (28 -> `[0, 1]`), mid-block (44 -> `[1, 2]`) and on a recurrent block edge (48 -> `[1, 2]`, the block that *ends* there)
- lookup + load under DCP: the tail is laid out per group (full-attention chunk + partial block at indices 0-1, recurrent state at index 2 past the nulls)

Pass on both: an aligned (full-attention multiple) boundary still goes to the aligned path only.

## Test Result

**Unit suite**, this branch vs. its base (`origin/main` @ a9eafde59c):

| arm | CPU-only host | GB300 (in the vLLM nightly container) |
|---|---|---|
| this branch | 103 failed, **364 passed**, 2 skipped | **475 passed**, 0 failed |
| base | 103 failed, 356 passed, 2 skipped | 467 passed, 0 failed |

On the CPU host the failure sets are byte-identical (no-GPU artifacts). On GPU everything passes. The added tests account for the entire +8; 7 of them fail when run against `main`. The GB300 unit run was on the previous rebase (base `ddd6fbca14`). `scheduler.py` and `test_scheduler.py` are byte-identical to this head, and the only change to `vllm/v1/core` since then is the #56723 `dcp_sharded` refactor, which keeps the block geometry the same (FA scaled by DCP, Mamba not). `mypy-3.12`, `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass.

**Hardware** (1 x GB300 node, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-29468dde8b` with only `offloading/scheduler.py` replaced). Model: Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (KDA + MLA), TP4/**DCP4**, `--mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 128`, OffloadingConnector with a 16 GiB CPU pool. Recurrent block 512, full-attention offload block 2048 (= 512 x DCP4), hash 128: the K3 shape (1536 / 12288 / 128) scaled down.

Protocol per prompt: clear all tiers, cold run (asserted 0 cached), reset only the GPU prefix cache, replay. The table shows tokens restored from the CPU tier, i.e. the replay delta of `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source{source="external_kv_transfer"}`.

| prompt tokens | best boundary | `main` | this PR only | this PR + #58618 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 645 | 640 | 0 | 640 | 640 |
| 2309 | 2304 | 2048 | 2304 | 2304 |
| 2565 | 2560 | 0 | 0 | 2560 |
| 2949 | 2944 | 0 | 0 | 2944 |
| 3717 | 3712 | 0 | 0 | 3712 |
| 4101 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 |
| 4485 | 4480 | 4096 | 4480 | 4480 |
| 17029 | 17024 | 0 | 0 | 17024 |
| 2949, replay diverges at 2700 | 2560 | 0 | 0 | 2560 |

- **`main`:** partial tails are off under DCP, so only whole 2048-token chunks restore, and only when the last full recurrent block lands on the chunk grid.
- **This PR alone:** tails are stored and found within one window of the complete-chunk hit.
- **With #58618:** every prompt restores to its last hash boundary.
- **All trials:** replayed greedy output is byte-identical to the cold recompute (32 tokens), with 0 allocation failures and no assertions or errors in the server logs.
- **Caveat:** on this model each retained boundary arrived in its own hand-off, so the multi-boundary crash path is covered by the unit reproducer only.

An earlier run of the combined change on a 2-node GB300 K3 deployment (TP8/DCP8) is in #57216.

## Notes

- Standalone: correct on its own, but the CPU tier only yields hits beyond one window of the complete-chunk hit once #58618 (lookup anchor) also lands. Merges cleanly with it (verified; the merged tree passes the suite).
- Not duplicating: #53889 scales `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` groups by DCP in `build_offloading_config` (config side, complementary); #52397 fixes the `max_offload_tokens` cap in this function and is left to that PR — the baseline lines are kept verbatim here so the rebase is trivial.
- `tokens_per_hash % dcp == 0` is conservative: store and load copy whole physical blocks per rank, so the copy path does not need it, but it is the only shape validated on hardware.
- `dcp == 1` was not run on hardware for this PR; the guard change is a no-op there by construction and the existing dcp=1 unit tests cover the store path.
- #58413 (MTP/EAGLE Mamba offload) touches the same file and merges cleanly; EAGLE stays excluded by this PR's guard.
- AI assistance (Claude / Devin) was used to draft code and tests; every changed line was reviewed and the tests were run by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Anchor the partial-tail lookup on the full-attention prefix
body:
## Purpose

Split out of #57216 per @orozery's review (part 1 of 2): the lookup half. The DCP store half is #58619.

`_lookup` anchors the partial-tail search on `_lookup_complete_chunks`, which requires *every* KV cache group to have a complete chunk at the anchor boundary, including the recurrent groups. A recurrent `align` group holds state only where a scheduler step ended on one of its block boundaries: in practice at the producer prompt's last full recurrent block and at its tail.

With **uniform block sizes** (dcp=1, the only shape `supports_partial_tail` admits today) the last-full-block boundary is also a full-attention chunk multiple, so that aligned row lands on the chunk grid, `complete_hit` reaches it, and the existing one-window probe finds the tail. The anchor only fails when that row is missing, e.g. evicted separately from the tail. So on `main` today this is a robustness fix.

With **mixed block sizes** -- under DCP the full-attention offload block is `dcp x` the attention block while recurrent blocks stay unsharded (12288 vs 1536 at DCP 8) -- the aligned row sits at a recurrent multiple that is essentially never a full-attention multiple. `complete_hit` is then 0 for any prompt past the first chunk, the search is capped at one window from zero, and a correctly stored tail further out is never probed although it is resident. That is the state #58619 (the DCP store side) would land in without this PR: tails get stored, but only those within one window of the complete-chunk hit are ever found -- the "#58619 only" column of the hardware table below. **This PR is the prerequisite for #58619's lookups to work.**

Instrumented `_lookup` on a replay (chunk 12288, hash 128), before the change:

```
n=12620  complete_hit=12288  complete_boundary=12288  max_boundary=12544
           boundary=12544 ALL GROUPS HIT                  <- restores
n=15136  complete_hit=0      complete_boundary=0      max_boundary=12160
           boundary=12160 group=0 MISS ... 11776 MISS     <- tail stored at 15104,
                                                            never probed
```

Fix: anchor on the full-attention complete prefix and check recurrent groups only at the candidate boundary. Following the review suggestion, the anchor is `_lookup_complete_chunks` itself restricted to the full-attention groups via a new `lookup_groups` parameter, so it honours the same `max_num_new_tokens` / `max_load_tokens` caps, deferral and being-loaded rules as the all-groups hit, and only chunks verified resident can be requested by the load path. No new lookup method.

The returned boundary is always strictly greater than the complete-chunk hit, so the change can only widen what a lookup reports, never shrink it; wherever the aligned row is on the chunk grid the anchor equals `complete_hit` and the behaviour is unchanged. The probe window stays bounded at one full-attention block.

## Test Plan

Eleven tests on the existing dcp=1 hybrid fixture (`_make_partial_tail_scheduler`: 16-token full-attention and Mamba blocks, hash 4):

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ -q
```

Fail on `main`, pass here (they guard the fix):
- tail found with no recurrent state at the chunk boundary (30-token prompt, tail at 28)
- the same across **two** complete chunks (46-token prompt, tail at 44) -- the production shape, where the complete-chunk anchor is 0
- the load path requests only the verified chunk keys plus the tail keys
- `_lookup_complete_chunks(lookup_groups=full_attention_groups)` returns the full-attention prefix while the default still requires every group
- `max_num_new_tokens` caps which tail the anchored search may report
- deferral while the anchor chunk is being loaded, and while it is `HIT_PENDING`

Pass on both (regression guards for what the anchor must not change):
- 0 when no tail was stored; 0 when the full-attention chunk is not resident
- the tail is preferred over an aligned recurrent state at the chunk boundary
- a tail is found after a GPU prefix hit (`num_computed_tokens = 16`)

## Test Result

**Unit suite**, this branch vs. its base (`origin/main` @ a9eafde59c):

| arm | CPU-only host | GB300 (in the vLLM nightly container) |
|---|---|---|
| this branch | 103 failed, **367 passed**, 2 skipped | **478 passed**, 0 failed |
| base | 103 failed, 356 passed, 2 skipped | 467 passed, 0 failed |

On the CPU host the failure sets are byte-identical; all 103 are no-GPU artifacts (`VllmConfig` "Hybrid KV cache manager … not supported", HF-hub 429s). On GPU everything passes. The 11 added tests account for the entire +11; 7 of them fail when run against `main`. The GB300 unit run was on the previous rebase (base `ddd6fbca14`). `scheduler.py` and `test_scheduler.py` are byte-identical to this head, and the only change to `vllm/v1/core` since then is the #56723 `dcp_sharded` refactor, which keeps the block geometry the same. `mypy-3.12`, `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass.

**Hardware** (1 x GB300 node, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-29468dde8b` with only `offloading/scheduler.py` replaced). Model: Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (KDA + MLA), TP4, `--mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 128`, OffloadingConnector with a 16 GiB CPU pool. Recurrent block 512, full-attention offload block 2048 at DCP4 (512 at DCP1), hash 128: the K3 shape (1536 / 12288 / 128) scaled down.

Protocol per prompt: clear all tiers, cold run (asserted 0 cached), reset only the GPU prefix cache, replay. The table shows tokens restored from the CPU tier, i.e. the replay delta of `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source{source="external_kv_transfer"}`.

| prompt tokens | best boundary | DCP1: `main` | DCP1: this PR | DCP4: #58619 only | DCP4: #58619 + this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 645 | 640 | 640 | 640 | 640 | 640 |
| 2309 | 2304 | 2304 | 2304 | 2304 | 2304 |
| 2565 | 2560 | 2560 | 2560 | **0** | **2560** |
| 2949 | 2944 | 2944 | 2944 | **0** | **2944** |
| 3717 | 3712 | 3712 | 3712 | **0** | **3712** |
| 4101 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 |
| 4485 | 4480 | 4480 | 4480 | 4480 | 4480 |
| 17029 | 17024 | 17024 | 17024 | **0** | **17024** |
| 2949, replay diverges at 2700 | 2560 | 2560 | 2560 | **0** | **2560** |

- **DCP1:** this PR is identical to `main` on every trial, including store and load bytes. That is the expected no-regression result: the aligned row is on the chunk grid there, so the anchor equals `complete_hit`.
- **DCP4:** without this PR, only tails within one window of the complete-chunk hit are found. With it, every prompt restores to its last hash boundary.
- **All trials:** replayed greedy output is byte-identical to the cold recompute (32 tokens), with 0 allocation failures and no errors in the server logs.

An earlier run of the combined change on a 2-node GB300 K3 deployment (TP8/DCP8) is in #57216.

## Notes

- Related: the DCP store-side half is in #58619. Both are standalone; they touch adjacent lines in `__init__` and merge cleanly together (verified; the merged tree passes the suite). #58413 (MTP/EAGLE Mamba offload) touches the same file and also merges cleanly.

title: [KV Offload] Store every retained boundary in a partial-tail hand-off
body:
> **Draft — stacked on #58619; only the last commit is new.** This carries the "longest-only vs all" decision @orozery asked for in #57216 out of the DCP fix so it can be judged on its own.

## Purpose

Split out of #57216 (part 3 of 3). #58619 keeps only the **longest** boundary of a partial-tail hand-off. This PR proposes storing **every** boundary the KV cache manager retained inside the trailing full-attention block, and states the trade-off so it can be accepted or closed.

A request-end hand-off drains every recurrent `align` manager for the step, so besides the prompt tail it carries every other retained boundary inside the trailing full-attention block: the last full recurrent block, or one per retained segment under a non-zero `prefix_cache_retention_interval`. Under DCP none of these is a full-attention block multiple, so the partial-tail path owns them.

With longest-only, each of those boundaries ends up with a recurrent row in the pool (the aligned path stores it) but **no full-attention partner**, so a consumer that diverges from the producer between a retained boundary and the tail finds nothing there and recomputes from the last complete chunk. This PR stores each boundary as its own pair, longest first — the order a consumer's descending probe reads them in — moving the per-boundary body into `_build_partial_tail_store_job`.

## Trade-off (the decision)

| | longest-only (#58619) | every boundary (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| CPU pool per request-end hand-off | 1 FA row + 1 recurrent row | + 1 FA row + 1 recurrent row per extra retained boundary (K3 @ DCP 8: one extra pair, for the last full 1536-token recurrent block) |
| reachable by | consumers extending or diverging *after* the tail | additionally: consumers diverging inside the last recurrent block before the tail (≤ 1535 tokens on K3) |
| with `prefix_cache_retention_interval` | retained boundaries in the trailing FA block are dead rows | each is restorable from CPU |

The benefit is bounded by the same span as the cost. On Kimi-K3 shadow traces the divergence-inside-the-last-block case is a minority of an already-minority (regenerate/edit) flow; on the other hand, it is the only way retained boundaries under a retention interval become reachable from the CPU tier under DCP. Happy to close this if longest-only is preferred.

Not in this PR: the assert-to-skip conversions from #57216. I could not construct a reachable case for either — every `align` manager shares one block size (`resolve_mamba_align_size` asserts it), so all retain and hand off the same boundaries, and full-attention block ids of a live request are never the null block — so the asserts stay.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ -q
```

All three fail on #58619 (longest-only) and pass here:
- the two-boundary hand-off from #58619's reproducer now stores both pairs, longest first (`[12, 25]` @ 56 then `[12, 24]` @ 48), next to the aligned row
- a retention-shaped three-boundary hand-off (40, 48, 56) stores three pairs, longest first
- the pool refusing the longest pair does not cost the shorter one, and `kv_offload_allocation_failure` is counted once

## Test Result

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| this branch | 103 failed, **366 passed**, 2 skipped |
| base (`origin/main` @ 90a9515006) | 103 failed, 356 passed, 2 skipped |

Failure sets byte-identical (the no-GPU `VllmConfig` `ValidationError`). No hardware run for this commit; the K3 production branch has run the equivalent since 2026-09-17.

## Notes

- Not duplicating: #52397 (`max_offload_tokens` cap) is untouched.
- AI assistance (Claude / Devin) was used to draft code and tests; every changed line was reviewed and the tests were run by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Truncate Responses API auto-truncation at item level
body:
Fixes #58421

## Purpose

`truncation: "auto"` on `/v1/responses` was mapped to `truncate_prompt_tokens=-1`, which cuts the rendered prompt at the token level. Depending on the tokenizer's truncation side this discards the `instructions` system message first and can split input items mid-message, instead of dropping whole items from the beginning of the conversation as the OpenAI API contract specifies.

This PR resolves it at the item level in `OnlineRenderer.render_responses`: for non-Harmony requests, the derived token-level truncation is disabled and the oldest droppable conversation message is dropped one at a time (re-rendering after each drop) until the prompt fits, keeping the `instructions` system message and the final message intact. When nothing can be dropped, the original length validation error propagates so the client still receives a 400. Subsequent tool-loop turns and the scale-out render endpoint inherit the behavior through the same code path.

## Test Plan

- New regression tests in `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py`:
  - `test_online_renderer_auto_truncation_drops_oldest_items` — verifies items are dropped oldest-first, `instructions` and the final message survive, and token-level truncation stays disabled
  - `test_online_renderer_auto_truncation_surfaces_error_when_undroppable` — verifies the original 400 error propagates when nothing can be dropped
  - `test_online_renderer_disabled_truncation_uses_default_tok_params` — verifies `truncation="disabled"` behavior is unchanged
- Run with: `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py -k truncation`

## Test Result

- `ruff check` / `ruff format` (repo-pinned 0.14.0) pass on both changed files.
- Manual verification against the issue's repro script (Qwen3-0.6B + filler messages) is still pending a GPU machine; CI will run the new unit tests.

title: [Test][Quantization] Gate CUTLASS W4A8 kernel tests to SM90
body:
## Purpose
`test_cutlass_w4a8.py` and `test_cutlass_w4a8_moe.py` gate on compute capability >= 90, but the
CUTLASS W4A8 kernels are built for 9.0a only (`W4A8_ARCHS` in CMakeLists.txt) and
`CutlassW4A8LinearKernel.can_implement` already requires exactly SM90. On any Blackwell GPU the
tests run and fail:

    RuntimeError: encode_and_reorder_int4b, .../cutlass_w4a8/w4a8_mm_entry.cu:419, unified_encode_int4b failed

CI never sees this because the NVIDIA quantization-kernel lane runs on L4. This gates both files
on exactly SM90 to match the kernel, and removes a duplicate `IS_SUPPORTED_BY_GPU` definition in
the dense file that shadowed the first.

## Test Plan

    pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_cutlass_w4a8.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_cutlass_w4a8_moe.py -q

RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU (sm_120), vLLM main at `a9eafde59c`, precompiled 0.30.0 kernels.

## Test Result

title: [Bugfix][DBO] Fall back to eager at the empty-microbatch boundary
body:
## Purpose

With DP token counts `[64, 128]` and a 128-token CUDA graph, the smaller rank has no real tokens in its second microbatch. The existing guard uses `2 * min_tokens < graph_tokens`, so equality still permits FULL replay.

Change `<` to `<=` to use the existing eager microbatch fallback. Extend the existing regression test with the 64-token boundary and make its uniform-decode request counts consistent with the token counts.

Follow-up to #51700; its author [confirmed the bug and requested this fix](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51700#issuecomment-5681158479). title: [Attention] Support NVFP4 KV cache on SM8x with FlashInfer
body:
## Purpose

`--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` has a paged KV write path only on SM100, where trtllm-gen provides the native store. On SM8x there is no matching write and read pair, so the dtype cannot be used there at all.

This connects the two ends: KV writes go through FlashInfer's `nvfp4_quantize_append_paged_kv_cache_with_slot_mapping`, and the same pages are read back by the native paged-attention wrapper, which is already the decode kernel on SM8x. Queries stay in model dtype on that path and FP8 queries remain on trtllm-gen, which extends the gating from #47485 to the `nvfp4` branch. `validate_configuration` rejects SM90 and SM12x, whose XQA decode has no NVFP4 support, and DCP, whose prefill has no NVFP4 handling. Scale-search variants such as `nvfp4_4over6` still require the trtllm-gen store. Both FlashInfer entry points are in the pinned 0.7.0, so no version bump is needed. On the sm_80 host used for validation, KV cache capacity went from 1,446,932 to 4,805,405 tokens (3.32x).

It does not duplicate #46329 or #56550, which target the SM120/121 path; this one is SM8x only and does not enable SM12x. RFC #47684 tracks the wider work.

I used Codex and Claude while implementing and preparing this PR. I reviewed the final diff and ran the tests below.

## Test Plan

```
python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer.py -k nvfp4
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --attention-backend FLASHINFER --kv-cache-dtype <auto|nvfp4> --max-model-len 128K --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --enable-chunked-prefill --reasoning-parser qwen3 --port 8099
python tests/evals/mrcr/mrcr_eval.py --port 8099 --num-samples 30 --needles 2 4 8 --max-tokens 2048 --temperature 0 --seed 42 --concurrency 1
```

## Test Result

The 23 CPU tests pass, and breaking each new check in the backend (the arch and DCP rejections, the dtype gate, the query dtype, the writer requirement, the page split and the view cache) fails the matching test. The GPU test writes a combined page through `do_kv_cache_update()` and compares native prefill against attention over the values that writer stored. It is unchanged from the previous revision, where it passed on sm_80, and was not rerun for this one. pre-commit passes.

MRCR on Qwen3.5-4B, 30 samples across needles 2/4/8 with prompts of 16,626 to 33,231 tokens, measured on the previous revision; the backend change is the same here:

| KV dtype | Match ratio | Prefix hit rate | n2 | n4 | n8 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| auto | 0.8523 | 1.0000 | 0.9949 | 0.7987 | 0.7633 |
| nvfp4 | 0.8452 | 0.9667 | 0.8951 | 0.8773 | 0.7633 |

Only sm_80 was measured; SM86, SM89 and SM100 are untested locally.

title: [Kernel] Enable OAI Triton MXFP4 MoE on SM12x
body:
## Purpose

Disclaimer: The code was largely assisted by Claude Code but the PR itself is handwritten and well tested.

In general, this PR is a follow-up to #41028.

#41028 tries to allow sm120 to use Triton kernels for GPT-OSS models instead of Marlin kernels. However, current implementation of triton kernels does not work on sm12x out-of-box and this PR fixes this. By testing on an RTX 5090:

- Decode speed is the same.
